items.title: Integrations
Epic: Per-tenant email sending domain (donor relances) — verified DKIM/DMARC alignment

labels.name: non-trivial
labels.description: Major version bump or change requiring explicit human review and migration plan — do not auto-merge

labels.name: epic
labels.description: Large body of work that can be broken down into a number of smaller tasks

items.body:
## 0. Why this exists — at a glance

Today every email Givernance sends — donation receipts, team invites, **and donor relances** — leaves from a **single shared `From:` address** resolved by [`resolveEmailFrom()`](https://github.com/purposestack/givernance/blob/main/packages/worker/src/env.ts) (one tenant-agnostic `EMAIL_FROM` env var, fallback `Givernance <no-reply@givernance.local>`). The HTML footer is hardcoded `Sent via Givernance.`

When an NPO operator clicks **Send relance** on a donor multi-select (feature shipped in Epic #274, see `packages/worker/src/processors/send-bulk-email.ts`), the donor receives an appeal **from a domain they don't recognise**. This breaks four things at once:

1. **Donor trust** — recipient never opted in to hear from `givernance.app`, only from their charity. The platform should be invisible.
2. **DMARC alignment** — the org's actual domain isn't on the SPF/DKIM record; the appeal cannot pass strict alignment.
3. **Deliverability under Gmail/Yahoo Feb 2024 bulk-sender rules** — at >5,000 messages/day to either provider, DKIM+SPF+DMARC and RFC 8058 one-click unsubscribe are mandatory, and DMARC alignment requires the From-domain to match the DKIM-signing domain. A shared `givernance.app` From cannot satisfy this. Spam-folder placement jumps from a typical 5–10% baseline to 22–34% for non-compliant senders ([DMARC Report, 2025](https://dmarcreport.com/blog/email-authentication-impact-on-deliverability-spf-dkim-dmarc-inbox-placement)).
4. **Single-bad-tenant reputation contagion** — one rogue tenant on a shared sending pool drops inbox placement 40–60% across the entire customer base ([Mailpool, 2025](https://www.mailpool.ai/blog/multi-tenant-email-architecture-how-agencies-isolate-client-reputation-risk)). For Givernance this is an existential single point of failure.

This work was already aspirationally documented in `docs/05-integration-migration.md` § 3.1 (\"Domain verification: SPF, DKIM, DMARC records per org\") but never implemented. The Epic #274 bulk-email shipment turned a latent doc/code drift into a real product blocker for fundraising.

## 1. Recommendation (MVP)

| Decision | Choice |
|---|---|
| **Sender identity model** | **Subdomain delegation via 3 CNAMEs** (SendGrid \"Automated Security\" pattern). Operator publishes 2 DKIM CNAMEs + 1 Return-Path CNAME on `mail.<their-domain>`. Donor sees `relances@mail.demo-npo.org` with full DMARC alignment. |
| **ESP** | **Resend (EU region)** — already wired (`packages/worker/src/lib/email.ts`), has multi-domain API + EU residency + signable DPA. Suppression scoping (Resend is account-level, not domain-level) handled in our DB to satisfy RGPD Art. 21 per-controller scope. |
| **Transactional vs bulk split** | **Hard split.** Receipts, signup verification, password resets, team invites, MFA codes, security alerts → always platform domain (`givernance.app`). Donor relances + campaign emails → tenant subdomain. Donation tax receipts → tenant subdomain with platform-attestation footer. **Anything authenticating a human or attesting a legal fact stays on `givernance.app`.** |
| **Pricing tier** | **All tiers**, including base. Gating it would be a positioning own-goal vs. our \"transparent, affordable alternative to Salesforce NPSP\" stance. Salesforce gates branded sending behind Marketing Cloud ($10k+/yr) — this is a credible, easily-articulated differentiator. |
| **UX target** | **Mailchimp's verified-domain wizard** — it's the pattern French NPO admins are most likely to have already encountered (Mailchimp is the dominant SMB ESP in France). |
| **Pending-domain policy** | **Hard-block bulk send** when the tenant's domain is configured but unverified (avoid silent fallback to `givernance.app`). Tenants who genuinely have no domain (`@gmail.com`-only NPOs) get a capped fallback on shared `relances.givernance.app` with explicit nudge to acquire a domain (€8–15/yr at OVH/Gandi). |

### Rejected alternatives (with reason)

- **Status quo (single shared `EMAIL_FROM`)** — fails Feb 2024 bulk-sender rules, fails DMARC alignment, exposes platform-wide reputation.
- **Shared domain with per-tenant From-label only** (`\"Demo NPO\" <relances@givernance.app>`) — donor still sees `givernance.app` on hover/expand, DMARC aligned to Givernance only. Useful **only** as the transitional fallback during onboarding, not as the headline solution.
- **Custom apex domain (records on `demo-npo.org` directly)** — Phase 2 upgrade path. SPF 10-lookup limit risk, more onboarding friction; donor-trust gain over subdomain delegation is negligible (donors don't notice `mail.charity.org` vs `charity.org`).
- **Postmark** — no EU region. Reject (EU-only constraint).
- **AWS SES** — operationally heaviest, no first-class multi-tenant identity ergonomics. Phase 3 escape hatch for >100k/month tenants.
- **Brevo (FR-based, originally planned in `docs/05-integration-migration.md` § 3.2 for bulk)** — splitting Resend (transactional) + Brevo (bulk) doubles webhook plumbing, doubles suppression reconciliation, doubles DPA paperwork. Consolidate on Resend until a concrete Brevo-only feature forces the split.
- **Mailgun EU** — feature parity with Resend, switching cost not justified.
- **Scaleway Transactional Email** — does not exist as a first-class product.

## 2. Phasing

### Phase 1 — MVP-blocking (ship before scaling sales beyond design partners)

- New `tenant_email_domains` table (RLS-scoped, one verified domain per tenant initially).
- `EmailSender` interface refactor — add required `tenantId` and `kind: 'transactional' | 'bulk'` parameters. Move From-resolution behind a `SenderIdentityResolver` (cached 60s).
- Resend domain-create + verification poller (worker) with backoff (5 min → hourly, capped at 7 days).
- Settings → **Email sending** UI — Mailchimp-style wizard with 3 copy-paste records + status badge (`pending` → `awaiting_dns` → `verified` / `failed`) + provider-specific screenshots (OVH, Gandi, Cloudflare, Google Domains).
- Free-mailbox deny-list at API layer (`gmail.com`, `yahoo.*`, `outlook.com`, `laposte.net`, `orange.fr`, `free.fr`, etc. — see [Mozilla PSL](https://publicsuffix.org/)).
- `tenant_email_suppressions(org_id, email_hash, suppressed_at, reason)` table — populated from unsubscribe footer + hard-bounce webhooks. **Per-controller scope** (RGPD Art. 21): unsubscribe from Org A does NOT cascade to Org B.
- RFC 8058 one-click List-Unsubscribe header, DKIM-signed, with tenant- and recipient-specific token.
- Operator preview that uses the **real production sending path** (\"send test to me\") — non-negotiable, this is where DMARC misconfigs surface before a real campaign.
- DMARC traffic-light surface (green/amber/red) on the operator dashboard.
- `tenants.physical_address` required field for CAN-SPAM/RGPD footer.
- `docs/24-tenant-email-sending.md` shipping in the same PR (CLAUDE.md doc-discipline rule).
- `diagrams/email-sending-flow.mmd` companion.
- Boot-time guard: hard-fail when `EMAIL_PROVIDER=resend` and `EMAIL_FROM` is unset (currently silently falls back to `Givernance <no-reply@givernance.local>` which is RFC 6761 reserved and gets dropped by receivers — see Risks §5).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] An org_admin can verify `mail.demo-npo.org` via 3 CNAME records in <30 minutes
- [ ] A bulk relance sent to a Gmail recipient passes DMARC alignment (visible in `Authentication-Results` header)
- [ ] Unsubscribing from Org A does NOT suppress Org B's mailings (per-controller scope verified by integration test)
- [ ] Hard-bouncing a recipient suppresses them only for the originating org
- [ ] Bulk send is hard-blocked with structured 400 (`E_TENANT_DOMAIN_NOT_VERIFIED`) when domain is configured but unverified
- [ ] Transactional path (signup, password reset, team invite) continues to send from `givernance.app` regardless of tenant domain status
- [ ] Tenant offboarding immediately calls `domains.remove` on Resend (DKIM key revoked)
- [ ] Free-mailbox domains rejected at API layer with actionable error message

### Phase 2 — 3–6 months post-MVP

- **Custom apex domain** (Option D) as upgrade path — same UI, SPF-include-flattening warning if existing record nears the 10-lookup limit.
- **Multiple sender domains per tenant** (`dons@`, `evenements@`).
- **Bounce/complaint dashboard** per tenant — complaint rate (Gmail threshold 0.30%), bounce rate, sending volume trend.
- **Per-tenant suppression list management UI** — org_admin add/remove, bulk import during Salesforce ETL migration.
- **DKIM rotation** — manual + scheduled annual.
- **Per-campaign From-name override** (`\"Marie Dupont, Trésorière <relance@asso.org>\"`) — NextAfter data shows +28% open rate from named-human senders ([NextAfter](https://www.nextafter.com/blog/test-different-email-sender-name/)).
- **Federated domain support** — model `domain` as shared org-group resource for federations / dioceses / scout movements where 50 chapters share a parent domain managed by HQ.
- **Weekly re-verification poll** — re-poll DNS post-verification; if records disappear or DKIM selector changes, transition to `reverification_failed`, alert org_admin, gate sends to fallback after 72h.
- **DMARC enforcement nudge** — advisory + suggested DNS record when tenant's apex DMARC is `p=none`.

### Phase 3 — later

- **Dedicated IPs** for >100k/month tenants (likely SES backend, dual-ESP routing by tenant tier).
- **BIMI logo verification** (requires VMC, real money).
- **ARC sealing** for forwarded mail.
- **Automatic SPF flattening** for tenants whose record exceeds the lookup limit.

## 3. Architecture sketch

```
tenant_email_domains
  id              uuid pk
  org_id          uuid fk tenants(id) RLS
  domain          citext not null              -- mail.demo-npo.org
  esp_domain_id   text not null                -- Resend domain id
  status          enum('pending','awaiting_dns','verified',
                       'reverification_failed','revoked')
  verification_records  jsonb                   -- {dkim, spf, returnPath, dmarcSuggestion}
  dkim_selector   text
  verified_at     timestamptz
  last_checked_at timestamptz
  rotation_due_at timestamptz
  created_by      uuid fk users(id)
  created_at, updated_at, deleted_at
  unique(org_id, domain) where deleted_at is null
```

Plus on `tenants`:
- `bulk_sender_domain_id uuid null` (denormalised pointer, one join not a scan)
- `bulk_sender_friendly_name text` (defaults to `tenants.name`, operator override without re-verify)
- `physical_address text not null` (CAN-SPAM/RGPD footer)

Plus `tenant_email_suppressions(org_id, email_hash sha256, suppressed_at, reason enum('unsubscribed','hard_bounce','complaint'))` — per-controller scope, indexed on `(org_id, email_hash)`.

`EmailSender` interface refactor:

```ts
export type EmailKind = 'transactional' | 'bulk';

export interface SendEmailInput {
  tenantId: string;
  kind: EmailKind;
  to: string;
  subject: string;
  html: string;
  text: string;
  replyTo?: string;
}

export interface SenderIdentityResolver {
  resolve(tenantId: string, kind: EmailKind):
    Promise<{ from: string; replyTo?: string; espDomainId?: string; fallbackUsed: boolean }>;
}
```

Pending-domain policy: `kind: 'bulk'` with unverified domain → throw `E_TENANT_DOMAIN_NOT_VERIFIED`. `kind: 'transactional'` → always platform domain, `tenantId` used only for friendly-name and Reply-To.

Full architecture & engagement analysis attached as comments below.

## 4. Open product questions

1. **Shared-fallback policy for tenants without a domain.** Hard-block bulk-send entirely, or cap at first 1000 emails / 30 days on `relances.givernance.app` with friendly From-label? Hard-block is deliverability-safe; soft-cap is onboarding-friendly.
2. **DNS-record ownership in federated structures** (dioceses, scout movements, federations of 50 chapters sharing a parent domain managed by HQ). Model `domain` as tenant-scoped or as shared org-group resource? Affects schema, not just UI.
3. **Per-campaign vs tenant-level From-name.** NextAfter argues for human-named senders (+28% opens). Per-campaign override doubles QA surface — MVP fixes at tenant level, Phase 2 adds per-campaign?
4. **Resend account region.** Is the current Resend account already on EU region, or US? DKIM keys are bound to the account, so a US→EU migration is non-trivial.
5. **DMARC enforcement push.** Recommend (or require) tenant move their *own* domain's DMARC to `p=quarantine` after 30 days of healthy sending? Recommending = good citizenship + improves the tenant's overall security; requiring = hostile because it affects email channels we don't control. Probably an \"advisory with one-click suggested DNS record\" pattern, but it's a positioning call.

## 5. Risks

- **Latent boot failure** — `resolveEmailFrom()` falls back to `Givernance <no-reply@givernance.local>` when `EMAIL_FROM` is unset. `.local` is RFC 6761 reserved (mDNS) and is silently dropped or hard-rejected by Resend. The bulk processor's per-recipient try/catch (`send-bulk-email.ts:107-115`) hides this as `failed` increments in logs. **Audit Loki for the past 30 days before this rolls out**, and add a boot-time guard.
- **Worker RLS context** — `data.orgId` is on the job payload, but the worker has no `app_current_organization_id()` GUC equivalent for ESP calls. When `SenderIdentityResolver` queries `tenant_email_domains`, must use `set_config('app.current_org_id', ...)`. **Open question: does the worker already do this for outbox-driven jobs?** If not, this work expands beyond email — it's a worker-RLS hardening project.
- **Bulk send is sequential** (`send-bulk-email.ts:94`). At 200-tenant scale with 1k recipients per campaign, single-threaded send means ~30-min jobs. Per-tenant domain feature **amplifies volume** (operators send more confidently when delivery looks legit). Consider per-domain rate-limiter + parallelisation before Phase 2.
- **Domain hijack on churn** — tenant offboards, lets `demo-npo.org` lapse, attacker buys it, re-creates CNAME pointing at us. Mitigation: immediate `domains.remove` on offboarding (don't wait for CNAME removal) + 30-day deny-list of recently-removed domains requiring platform_admin approval to re-add.
- **Reputation pool contagion** — Resend default is shared IPs. One bad tenant drags the pool. Mitigations: enforce double-opt-in on imported lists (Phase 2), throttle bulk per-tenant per-hour at BullMQ rate-limit level, earmark Phase 3 dedicated-IP path for >100k/month.

## 6. Documentation deliverables

Per CLAUDE.md doc-discipline rule, this Epic ships with:

- `docs/24-tenant-email-sending.md` — Why this exists, user flow Mermaid, ERD, architecture (incl. transactional/bulk split rationale), readiness gates, suppression-list scope (RGPD Art. 21), permissions matrix, GDPR/CAN-SPAM/CASL posture, future work.
- `diagrams/email-sending-flow.mmd` — End-to-end sequence (operator → DNS verify → send → bounce → suppression).
- Update to `docs/05-integration-migration.md` § 3 (mark as implemented, link to doc 24).
- New ADR in `docs/15-infra-adr.md` — \"ADR-NN: Per-tenant subdomain delegation for bulk email; transactional stays on platform domain.\"

## 7. References

- [Google sender guidelines (Feb 2024)](https://support.google.com/a/answer/81126)
- [RFC 8058 — One-Click List-Unsubscribe](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8058)
- [CNIL Sheet 15 — legal basis for direct marketing](https://www.cnil.fr/en/sheet-ndeg15-take-account-legal-basis-technical-implementation)
- [GDPR Art. 21 — right to object](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-21-gdpr/)
- [M+R Benchmarks 2025 — fundraising email metrics](https://mrbenchmarks.com/charts/email-messaging)
- [SendGrid Automated Security — 3-CNAME pattern](https://support.sendgrid.com/hc/en-us/articles/21415314709147-SendGrid-Automated-Security-Domain-Authentication)
- [Mailchimp — domain authentication wizard](https://mailchimp.com/help/set-up-email-domain-authentication/)
- [Mailpool — multi-tenant reputation contagion](https://www.mailpool.ai/blog/multi-tenant-email-architecture-how-agencies-isolate-client-reputation-risk)
- Code refs: `packages/worker/src/lib/email.ts`, `packages/worker/src/env.ts:resolveEmailFrom`, `packages/worker/src/processors/send-bulk-email.ts`, `packages/api/src/modules/constituents/bulk-email-service.ts`
- Existing aspirational doc: `docs/05-integration-migration.md` § 3.1 + § 3.2

## 8. Companion analyses

- Full **technical architecture analysis** posted as comment below (architect-reviewer agent, ESP comparison, DNS verification flow, suppression-list scope rationale, security/abuse vectors, per-phase acceptance criteria).
- Full **engagement / regulatory / competitive landscape analysis** posted as comment below (research-analyst agent, deliverability impact with citations, M+R benchmarks, Salesforce NPSP / Bloomerang / Mailchimp / EveryAction comparison, NPO onboarding friction reality check, donor-trust UX patterns).

---

**Blocks:** none currently — Epic #274 (postal campaigns) shipped without this gate but the relance feature is **production-ready in code only**; recommend disabling or capping the bulk-email Send button to design partners until Phase 1 of this Epic ships.

items.title: Implement distributed lake SQL joins across serverless query workers
items.body:
## Problem and intended outcome

Serverless lake SQL joins currently execute within one process. Local memory/spill limits constrain joins even when scans could be distributed across query pods. Implement a distributed lake SQL runtime that preserves the existing input consistency and SQL semantics while bounding per-task resources and query-wide cost.

Start with native distributed broadcast joins for star schemas. Establish shared query/task state and immutable artifacts that later support shuffle joins. Keep local execution for queries that fit.

The proposal in [serverless-distributed-joins.md](https://github.com/antflydb/antfly/blob/main/docs/design/serverless-distributed-joins.md), merged in #1480, provides the broader strategy ladder. This issue specifies coordination across existing serverless roles and an incremental implementation path. This is proposed work, not existing distributed SQL functionality.

## Fit the existing runtime roles

| Role | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| API | Accept/authenticate requests, apply tenant admission, and route execution to the query service. Continue owning ingestion/table APIs. |
| Query | Coordinate queries and execute scan, broadcast, shuffle, reduce, and result tasks; reuse local data caches. |
| Maintenance | Reclaim expired exchange/results and abandoned query state alongside existing publication and GC work. |
| Combined | Run all responsibilities in one process for development and small deployments. |

A coordinator is a temporary, query-specific responsibility of a query pod, not a new permanent node role or namespace owner. A pod may coordinate one query while running tasks for others. Any eligible query worker can execute a task; cache locality is a scheduling preference, not a correctness requirement.

The current role checks are not a distributed scheduler. Add a separate query-execution lifecycle: query-only/api-only runtimes currently skip the maintenance loop, so query recovery and task polling must not be placed exclusively in that loop.

Later, isolate analytical tasks from latency-sensitive reads using separate query pools with capability/configuration settings before introducing another top-level role.

## Coordination protocol

1. The query service creates a query ID and durable query record containing the versioned plan, authorized inputs, pinned snapshots and accepted WAL cuts, budgets, deadline, and expiry.
2. A query pod acquires coordinator ownership with a monotonically increasing fencing token.
3. The coordinator creates deterministic stage/task IDs and dispatches task references through an authenticated internal transport. Larger plans and artifacts live in shared storage.
4. A worker conditionally claims a task, executes its fragment, and writes immutable attempt outputs under a query/stage/task/attempt namespace.
5. The worker atomically transitions the task record from its current claim to accepted completion, recording the exact output manifest. Acceptance must be conditional on the current ownership revision/fence. A separate lease validation followed by an independent publication is insufficient.
6. Duplicate delivery and speculative attempts are safe: only the accepted output is visible to downstream tasks. A worker acknowledges delivery after durable acceptance.
7. The coordinator advances stages using accepted task records. Notifications are hints; durable state is authoritative. Map completion determines the exact exchange inputs for reducers.
8. After coordinator loss, another query pod acquires the expired lease, resumes retention renewal, reconstructs stage progress, reuses accepted outputs, and redispatches unfinished tasks.

Terminal transitions, cancellation, and stage advancement must also reject stale coordinator ownership. Bound retries, task concurrency, and output retention. Recovery must fail closed if an input retention guarantee has already been lost.

Do not create a Kubernetes Job per row-group task. Kubernetes schedules the long-lived pods; the query runtime schedules bounded fragments. No Raft coordination is required for every task when the shared state backend provides the necessary conditional updates.

### Runtime interfaces

- **QueryStateStore:** conditional query/task records, coordinator/task ownership, fencing, accepted output references, terminal state.
- **TaskDispatcher:** durable delivery or recoverable dispatch, retries, bounded concurrency, eligible worker routing/discovery.
- **ExchangeStore:** immutable typed broadcast/shuffle/result objects, integrity validation, bounded/range reads, expiry.

An object-store CAS backend is an initial option for shared execution state. Reuse the existing work-lease abstractions where appropriate, but add the atomic task-output acceptance protocol rather than assuming the existing lease guard supplies it.

## Input consistency and authorization

- Capture a pinned base snapshot and accepted WAL cut for **each** input. Preserve both base files and overlay records for the whole query; task retries use exactly the same cuts.
- Apply accepted inserts, replacements, and deletes before each input's predicates and limits.
- Apply the build overlay before constructing broadcast artifacts or dynamic filters. Apply the probe overlay and suppress replaced base rows before dynamic filtering and exchange.
- Route overlay mutations consistently with bucket/shuffle partitioning.
- Fragment IR carries schema fingerprints and authorization/credential scopes. Workers resolve scoped access rather than receiving serialized credentials.
- Query pods need narrowly scoped writes for execution records, exchange artifacts, and retention leases; this does not grant table publication or general maintenance authority.
- Account for overlay bytes and requests across all inputs; a per-input pending-record bound is not a query-wide resource bound.

## First distributed strategy: broadcast

```text
Capture and retain input snapshots + WAL cuts
  → build filtered dimension input once
  → publish typed broadcast artifact + dynamic filter
  → fan out fact-table row-group units
  → execute local joins on query workers
  → merge aggregate partials or return result pages
```

Initially support inner joins and left joins where the preserved left input is the distributed probe side. Keep unsupported shapes on the local path when they fit; otherwise return an explicit unsupported/budget error.

Dynamic filtering must follow logical preservation semantics after physical side selection. Do not prune unmatched preserved rows or anti-join absent keys; preserve NULL-key rows when required. Right/full joins over replicated builds require global match tracking and a single owner for unmatched build output.

## Implementation milestones

### 1. Pinned input contract and local fragment execution

- Define a versioned fragment IR instead of serializing in-memory relation nodes.
- Cover scan, overlay, filter, projection, local join, partial aggregate, and result sink.
- Establish query-wide snapshot/WAL retention and cancellation.
- Execute serialized two-input fragments locally and compare against ordinary SQL.

### 2. Shared artifacts and durable task lifecycle

- Define typed broadcast/result formats and immutable attempt manifests.
- Implement query/task state, fenced claims and acceptance, coordinator takeover, retries, and expiry cleanup.
- Add authenticated worker dispatch/discovery and capacity reporting.
- Integrate task CPU/memory/I/O admission with interactive-query budgets.

### 3. Native distributed broadcast

- Build the small side once and fan out probe row-group scan units.
- Install semantically safe dynamic filters before cursor execution.
- Verify exact-key filters can prune bucket partitions and dynamic ranges reach row-group pruning.
- Merge existing aggregate partials; page large results through cursor/continuation contracts.

### 4. Shuffle exchange and reduce

- Write one exchange object per map task, containing contiguous typed partition runs and an indexed footer with offsets, row counts, and byte counts.
- Reducers range-read their partitions from accepted map outputs.
- Reuse the existing grace hash join/skew kernels for local reduce execution, with bounded spill.
- Admit scan/shuffle bytes, task count, object-store requests, and overlay costs before dispatch; enforce actual consumption at runtime.

### 5. Optimization and additional runtimes

- Co-partitioned joins from compatible Iceberg bucket specs; optional bucketed native writes must retain correct equality-delete semantics.
- Adaptive broadcast selection, partition coalescing, and skew splitting from map statistics.
- Correct global unmatched-row handling for replicated skew inputs.
- Cloudflare adapter: Durable Object coordinator, Queues dispatch, R2 exchange, and object-store repartitioning under WASM memory/CPU limits.

## Reuse and boundaries

Reuse local join kernels in `partition_join.zig` / `skew_join.zig`, dynamic filters, row-group scan units, aggregate partials, snapshot pins, work leases, and expiring-object infrastructure where applicable.

The stateful JSON-join implementation in `api/distributed_join.zig` supplies lifecycle lessons, but its finalizer-local durability is not the shared persistence model for serverless SQL. Keep common planner/kernel behavior reusable without making serverless execution depend on stateful finalizer ownership.

Keep small joins on the current local path. Reject work beyond tenant budgets with useful estimates and an explicit `SqlJoinBudgetExceeded` error; do not promise arbitrary many-to-many ETL at any scale.

## Validation / acceptance criteria

- Compare every enabled distributed strategy against local SQL on identical pinned inputs, including NULLs, duplicate-heavy keys, deletes/replacements, side swaps, and preserved unmatched rows.
- Exercise concurrent ingestion and vacuum throughout execution and retry.
- Kill coordinators/workers mid-stage; lose claim/completion responses; redeliver tasks; expire or transfer leases during publication.
- Prove stale attempts cannot commit and each accepted task output contributes once.
- Verify recovery renews retention or safely terminates when input retention is lost.
- Verify cancellation and coordinator crashes leave no exchange artifacts beyond the configured cleanup/retention bound.
- Report task counts, scan/shuffle bytes, object-store requests, per-task peak memory, and latency against configured budgets.
- Test combined single-process execution and multiple native query pods before Cloudflare deployment.

items.body:
[Codex] On behalf of @sfmskywalker.

## State

**Updated 15 November 2026.** This section is the overall delivery dashboard. Detailed receipts remain in the comments and linked PRs.

Portfolio roll-up: [Project #62 — Execution](https://github.com/orgs/elsa-workflows/projects/62/views/2). The item is In Progress, Research proofs, Verification Partial as last read. The App was denied the LatestEvidence update; owner-account board permission is pending. This issue is the current detailed delivery dashboard.

| Program stage | Status | Exit gate |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Prove the kernel | **In progress: final prototype qualification** | Remaining concerns landed with two independent nonauthor clean reviews, causal checks and integrated-main proof |
| 2. Approve the design | **Held behind new round5 hardening; references delivered** | Round4 leftovers → owner delta5 A–F → seven updated answers/retirement evidence → actual independent Astra High architecture review and resolved findings → conditional delegated approval |
| 3. Ship release 1 | **Not started; gated by design approval** | Product provider/profile matrix and composed runtime/API/Studio acceptance |
| 4. Switch Elsa | **Not started** | Demonstrated release acceptance, coexistence disposition and rollback plan |
| 5. Remove the old core | **Not started** | Reviewed exact tracked-code inventory and no remaining supported live-run dependencies |

### Delivered

- Kernel/store/runtime baselines and conformance, graph extraction, StateMachine/agent/ETL prototypes, decided subscription and reply semantics, Park subscription removal, lease guard, values by reference and state-size measurements.
- Storage and fencing references in [docs/architecture](https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-foundation/tree/main/docs/architecture), plus the published [walkthrough](https://vowful-mustard-pd8t.here.now/) and [kernel in motion](https://crystal-pellet-h5m3.here.now/).
- Viewer complete: #4359 → #4492 → #4493 → #4494. Resulting main at c54afb27d0 exactly matches the reviewed final tree. Fresh SQLite checked-fence inventory: 64 passed, zero required failures, one inapplicable skip. These are prototype results, not product acceptance.
- BPMN parents #4328 and #4332.
- Shared Jobs foundation: all 15 concerns merged through #4559, with exact resulting-tree and integrated-main qualification.
- Physical run retirement #4603 (`69ceba7d1974f38e0a2dcaa6130bfe5a2bb229da`): two independent clean exact-head reviews, required deletion-journal/projector consistency and observed revision advancement. Actual squash tree equals reviewed61d; fresh resulting-main targeted builds and one selected permanent projector case pass. This is the first recreation concern only.
- Final-source write-volume/PostgreSQL retention report #4562, updated Storage model #4565 and Ownership and fencing #4566. Each has two clean independent nonauthor reviews; their delivery endpoint is `ce9a0ce932a9bd6311baf9f9bd11562ef8d08aea`. Later main changes require affected integration checks.
- Storage reference viewer read updated to the landed contract in #4510, with two clean independent R1 reviews.
- Ephemeral short waits: #4353 and #4496–#4503, clean R19, complete on main 23ecb8a17f. Resulting prototype source equals the reviewed tree; fresh actual-main 217 races, 9 clock, 8 integration, 23 lease and 89 native scope cases pass.

- Simulator final-idle deadline repair: #4511, clean R2, preserves normal HTTP settlement and missed-event checks.

- Graphical 15-minute demo: [kernel lab](https://jazzy-quasar-ce9t.here.now/), published permanently under the owner account with no expiry; generated artwork, operation-count evidence, fencing and Flowchart path lab. This is an illustrative demo, separate from the queued canonical token explainer.

### Active and next

| Stream | Current state | Next gate |
|---|---|---|
| BPMN #4342, then costs #4357 | R44 closed not clean: FIRST1Major/2Minor, SECONDclean. R45 is a pure90beef pre-integration author checkpoint with670 assertions (12 deliberately INCONCLUSIVE); no final integrated review gate. | Finish Card4 landing, integrate canonical carrier checks with actual main, obtain the requested one-run combined-oracle exception and two clean exact-source reviews, land small concerns, then refresh costs. |
| Shared Jobs foundation / standalone jobs | Foundation delivered in 15 concerns through #4559, with exact-tree and integrated-main verification. The full standalone actor still awaits the owner cost decision below. | Preserve foundation guarantees; obtain the owner decision before standalone actor adoption. |
| Park #4343 and run recreation | Park delivered in11 concerns. Physical first #4603 delivered as69ceba7d with exact reviewed tree and fresh actual-main builds/projector check. Repaired FIRST61d and FULLf391 have two new separate exact-head CLEAN reviews, with a signed correction excluding an empty test filter. | Land the remaining291-line keyed activation and small proof/docs concerns with actual-current-main head bindings; retain historical provider/cost provenance and the separate unanswered standalone lookup decision. |
| Tokens explainer and execution-model reference | Queued after the BPMN stack, as instructed. | Deliver the accurate interactive page and concept reference, independent reviews, merge and complete-site publication. |
| Final design packet | Prepared proposal documents are held because delta 5 changes the design. Clock experiment #4602 is delivered; exact resulting main and its targeted build were verified. | Finish round 4, then hardening A–F; update all seven answers and obtain the actual Astra High architecture review. |
| Round 5 hardening A–F | E's release scope and A's per-virtual-partition journal contract are adopted. Final fence granularity awaits measurements. No hardening code has started. | A/C/F in parallel; B spike alongside and finalization after A; D report; usual small-PR and exact-head clean-pair gates; then the proposal. |

**Owner decision pending:** permit one first-use provider identity lookup on a hot Jobs actor for previously unseen self-reference aliases on MySQL/SQL Server. Cold lookup can be combined; repeats add none; measured PostgreSQL hot claim/completion remains two wire trips. The concrete decision card is in the delivery conversation.

**Review authority:** all numeric review caps for #4229 are removed in favor of as many rounds as reasonably necessary; cumulative counts, two independent nonauthor reviews and resolution of minor-or-higher findings remain required. Independent GPT reviewers replace Opus/Sonnet; an actual independent Astra High architecture review replaces Fable. Ordinary implementation reviews do not satisfy that separate architecture gate.

No product implementation, default switch, old-core retirement or issue closure is claimed. #4176 remains untouched. The existing main-CI issue #4177 is tracked separately; targeted passing checks do not assert whole-main health.

This issue receives a comment at every state transition.

## Mission

Build Elsa's new execution kernel from the clean-slate design, prove it in the prototype, get the design approved, then ship release 1 on it, switch Elsa to it and delete the old core. Everything lands in small PRs (one concern each, about 500 changed lines at most, renames and moves apart from behaviour).

Set by Sipke on 12 November 2026. It supersedes the journal-first plan of #4176 (ADR 0098), which stays open until he has seen it closed.

## The design

- Design sketch draft 5 and the interactive walkthrough: https://vowful-mustard-pd8t.here.now/
- Decided so far:
  - the three layers (actor runtime, durable actors, actor types);
  - partitions only, with Orleans hosting each partition as a grain;
  - the seven kernel defaults and the deployment profiles;
  - the names turn, job and pass;
  - the container semantics: structured containers built in, the Flowchart on a graph engine extracted from today's Flowchart, the StateMachine on a statechart engine, and BPMN hosted on valence-works Bpmn.Semantics;
  - one job concept, with Elsa.Jobs rebuilt on the kernel as a job actor type;
  - the release 1 scope.
- Status: **proposed, not approved.** No product code before the architecture review and recorded design approval on Sipke's behalf under his conditional delegation.

## Plan

1. Land the record (draft 5 and the walkthrough) and the prototype (`prototypes/kernel-model`) on main, in PRs split by area.
2. Finish prototype round 4, one PR per item:
   - the three layers and the renames (done in stage A; landing as #4250-#4260);
   - the card decisions, with SQL Server's checked fence (decided 13 November, finding E9);
   - the Orleans adapter with a runtime conformance suite;
   - the graph engine;
   - the BPMN, StateMachine, agent, standalone-jobs (with the worker protocol) and ETL fan-out spikes;
   - the write-volume measurement (design-now question 7).
3. After round 5 hardening A–F (owner delta of 15 November; round 4 leftovers first), the design proposal (ADR, program plan, answers to seven design-now questions, the list of ADRs to retire) and `docs/architecture/`, one page per PR. Then the actual independent Astra High architecture review (the owner-authorized Fable substitute), resolution of all material findings and conditional delegated design approval on Sipke's behalf once all seven answers are complete.
4. Product slices behind a host switch, with the old core as the default.
5. Switch the default.
6. Delete the old core.
7. Close or supersede #4176, #2564 and #4043.

## Release 1

**In release 1:**
- the kernel and the built-in runtime;
- the Embedded and Cluster profiles;
- the same native model set in both profiles: structured containers, the Flowchart and the StateMachine (owner scope confirmed 15 November);
- synchronous HTTP;
- PostgreSQL, SQL Server and SQLite tuned, and MySQL supported but not tuned;
- Studio on the new core;
- agents as native activities;
- basic observability, retention, admission control and instance migration;
- parked-work operator tooling: inspect, retry and discard;
- decision 10, values by reference, as a release 1 priority (owner delta 5).

**After release 1, proven by spikes now:** BPMN, ETL, the job worker protocol, a dedicated agent model, and MongoDB (proven in CI only for release 1). The Orleans adapter is behind a proven-demand gate, with no automatic product commitment.

items.title: Functional definition: AI-powered real-estate investment sourcing platform
items.body:
> **Original brief:** The current code is for a dashboarding project, we are going to reuse the code as there is a lot of overlap. The application is intended to find the best real estate properties to invest in. It will crawl a list of real estate listing sites, ingest all the data into the database, and apply filtering criteria to present a list of candidates. The user can give feedback to improve filtering over time, across multiple independent "search profiles" (e.g. low-cost/high-yield rentals vs. commercial spaces) sharing the same underlying listing data. A set of per-site connectors parses and normalizes data into the app's model. The system deduplicates properties listed on multiple sites (ideally by owner identity). The app is AI-enabled for search refinement, subjective assessment (occupancy, description-to-criteria matching), and tracks daily new listings and price changes.

## Implementation

This functional definition is broken into 7 phase issues, each with its own task sub-issues (GitHub native sub-issues — visible as a progress checklist on each phase issue):

- #2 — Phase 1: Foundation (6 tasks)
- #3 — Phase 2: Deduplication + basic filtering (8 tasks)
- #4 — Phase 3: Feedback loop v1 (4 tasks)
- #5 — Phase 4: AI layer (7 tasks)
- #6 — Phase 5: Investment analytics (6 tasks)
- #7 — Phase 6: Deal workspace (3 tasks)
- #8 — Phase 7: Multi-profile maturity (3 tasks)

## Review addressed (Fable pass 1)

A fresh Fable-model review of the full 41-issue tree found 5 must-fix problems and 8 worth-improving gaps before any implementation started. All were addressed:

- **`profile_listing_state` re-keyed on `property_id`, not `listing_id`** (#10, #16, #18, #19, #20, #36, #37) — the original keying would have let one deduplicated property carry two independent scores/feedback/pipeline-stages once matched across sites, defeating the point of dedup.
- **Phone-number dedup signal downgraded** (#16) — no longer auto-merges alone; requires corroboration and excludes agency listings, closing an agency-phone-reuse false-positive trap.
- **Idealista feasibility spike added** (#12) — a robots.txt/access check now precedes connector implementation, with Fotocasa as a documented fallback.
- **CI-breakage handling added** (#9) — stripping PowerShop content will break several uncommitted `.github/workflows/*.yml` files; the task now proposes corrected YAML in its PR body per the inherited D-029 pattern instead of surfacing as a surprise.
- **Cadastral lookup given its own task** (#42, new — Phase 2.6) — the spec's #1-ranked dedup signal previously had no owning task; #16 and #12 now depend on it for real.
- **Map view** (#43, new — Phase 2.7) and **property detail page** (#44, new — Phase 2.8) added — both named in §13 but missing from the original 33 tasks; #27, #33, #37 now reference #44 concretely instead of vague placeholders.
- **Renovation/ARV estimate for flip theses** (#45, new — Phase 5.6) — §11's flip-specific metric had no task; the original 5.1–5.5 covered rental-yield metrics only.
- **Scoring model hardened** (#21 requires L2 regularization; #23's cold-start threshold now scales with feature count) — guards against near-perfect-separation degeneracy on small feedback sets.
- **`owner_identity` retention default set** (#10, cross-referenced in #16) — resolves the open GDPR-minimization question in §17 with a 90-day-unlinked-from-active-listing purge default, overridable by the owner.
- **Phase 6's dependency corrected** (#7) — it named Phase 3, but `pipeline_stage` is introduced in Phase 1's schema; the real coupling is to Phase 2.
- **"Relisted at a lower price" pattern named and computed** (#34) and **surfaced as its own digest item type** (#35) — previously an implicit capability of the raw data, not an owned computation.
- **Rental-comp confidence tiering** (#31, propagated into #33) — a median of 3 comparables no longer presents with the same visual confidence as a median of 20.
- Left deliberately unchanged: #9 bundles deletion + decision re-authoring + doc-skeleton rewriting in one task; Fable flagged it as splittable but it was kept as one task (diminishing returns on splitting a Phase-1-first task further).

## Review addressed (owner pass 2)

- **Cadastral lookup connector (#42) cancelled** — the owner correctly pushed back: resolving a `referencia catastral` needs a precise street-number address or tight coordinates, and most listing sources (private listings especially, plus many agencies) deliberately withhold or fuzz exact location to prevent going around the platform. Closed #42 as not planned, unlinked it from Phase 2 (#3), and reverted #16's dedup engine to treat cadastral matching as a rare opportunistic check rather than a built/relied-upon signal — the load-bearing signals are address+coordinates+size, phone-in-description (corroborated, non-agency only), and photo hashing.

## 1. Purpose

Inmo-Tool is a personal real-estate deal-sourcing and scoring platform. It continuously crawls real-estate listing sites, builds a de-duplicated database of properties for sale, and surfaces the ones worth an investor's attention — ranked and explained, not just filtered. The investor's judgment (accept/reject/why) feeds back into the ranking so the tool gets sharper over time, independently for each investment thesis they're pursuing in parallel.

The bar for "useful to an investor" is not "shows me listings that match a price range." It's: *tells me things that would otherwise cost hours of manual site-hopping, cross-referencing, and re-checking* — a new listing appeared, this one dropped 8% after 40 days on market, this "reformado" claim contradicts the photos, this address matches a listing you rejected on another site three weeks ago.

## 2. Primary user & usage pattern

- Single investor (or small family office) managing **several concurrent acquisition mandates** at once — e.g. "high-yield low-cost rental in [city]", "commercial units for owner-occupied business", "fixer-uppers to flip". Multi-tenancy across unrelated users is explicitly **not** a v1 goal (see §16); the multi-profile design exists to let *one* investor run several theses, not to host several investors.
- Usage is a mix of:
  - **Passive digest** — daily/weekly summary of new candidates, price drops, and listings that fell off market (sold/withdrawn).
  - **Active review** — a queue-clearing session per profile, swiping through candidates with quick feedback.
  - **Ad-hoc AI chat** — "find me flats near a metro stop in this district under 200k with a terrace", "why did you rank this one so low?", "compare these three".
  - **Deal workspace** — once a listing becomes a real candidate, tracking it through a pipeline (interested → contacted → visited → offer made → closed/rejected) with notes.

## 3. Core concept: Search Profiles (independent "mandates" over shared data)

A **Search Profile** is the top-level unit of filtering, scoring, and learning. All profiles read from the same raw ingested listing pool, but each has its own:

- **Scope filters** — geography (city/district/neighborhood polygon or radius-from-point), property type(s) (piso, chalet, ático, local comercial, nave industrial, garaje, terreno, edificio completo), price band, size band, and any hard exclusions (e.g. ground floor only, must have elevator).
- **Investment thesis parameters** — target metrics relevant to that thesis (e.g. minimum gross rental yield for a buy-to-let profile; price-per-m² ceiling vs. neighborhood average for a flip profile; zoning/commercial-license requirements for a commercial profile).
- **Independent learned scoring model** — feedback given inside one profile never leaks into another. Two profiles can rank the *same* listing completely differently (a small ground-floor flat might score high for "commercial conversion" and near-zero for "family rental").
- **Independent pipeline state** — a listing can be "rejected" in one profile and "under offer" in another simultaneously.

A listing therefore has one canonical record, but N per-profile projections: `(listing_id, profile_id) → {score, rank_explanation, feedback_history, pipeline_stage, notes}`.

Profiles are user-creatable/editable/archivable via UI, not hardcoded. Cloning a profile (to fork a variant thesis) should be a one-click operation.

## 4. Data ingestion layer (per-site connectors)

Each supported listing site gets a connector responsible for: discovery (search-result pagination for the site's own filters, or a saved-search URL), detail-page fetch, parsing into the canonical schema (§5), and respectful crawling (see §15 for legal/rate constraints).

**Connector contract** (mirrors `etl/sync/*.py`'s per-domain-module pattern in the source project):
- `discover(profile_scope) -> list[external_id]` — cheap, frequent (e.g. hourly) pass to find new/changed external IDs for the geography/type the app cares about, without fetching full detail pages.
- `fetch_detail(external_id) -> RawListing` — full page fetch + parse: price, address/coordinates, m², rooms, floor, elevator, year built, energy rating, condition, description text, photo URLs, listing type (particular vs. agency), contact info as published, first-seen timestamp reconciliation.
- `normalize(RawListing) -> CanonicalListingVersion` — maps site-specific fields/units/enums into the shared schema; unmapped/extra fields preserved in a `raw_extra jsonb` column so nothing is silently dropped even before the schema catches up.
- Connector-level config: request rate limit, concurrency cap, user-agent string, and a circuit breaker that pauses the connector (and alerts) on a spike in 4xx/5xx or a structural parse-failure rate (site changed its HTML/API — don't silently ingest garbage).

**Target sites** (Spain-focused, adjust to actual market): Idealista, Fotocasa, Habitaclia, pisos.com, yaencontre, Milanuncios (private-seller heavy), and any regional/niche boards relevant to the target geography. Idealista and Fotocasa expose limited partner APIs — prefer those over scraping where access is obtainable; scraping is the fallback, not the default (see §15).

Supplementary (non-listing) data sources worth connectors too, since they make scoring meaningful rather than just filtering:
- **Cadastral data** (Sede Electrónica del Catastro) — reverse-geocode an address/coordinate to a `referencia catastral`, which is a strong deduplication anchor (§6) and a source of ground-truth built area, year of construction, and use type independent of what the listing claims.
- **Comparable rents** — pull rental listings for the same area to estimate achievable rent for a for-sale property (needed for yield calculations, §11).
- **Market indices** (Idealista/Fotocasa published price-per-m² indices, INE) — neighborhood-level price trend context, so "this is priced 15% below the area average" is a computed fact, not a guess.

## 5. Canonical data model (sketch)

- **`property`** — the physical asset, one row per real-world unit once deduplicated. `cadastral_ref` (nullable, strong key when known), canonical address, coordinates, geometry/polygon of the building where available, property_type, m2_built, m2_useful, rooms, bathrooms, floor, has_elevator, year_built, energy_rating.
- **`listing`** — one row per (source, external_id): FK to `property` (**correction, implementation review**: NOT NULL — every listing gets its own singleton `property` row at ingest, never a deferred-null reference; dedup reassigns/unions `property_id` rather than filling in an empty one), source site, external_id, url, listing_kind (particular/agency), current status (active/reserved/sold/withdrawn/expired), first_seen_at, last_seen_at, current price, raw description, photo URLs, contact info as published, `raw_extra jsonb`.
- **`listing_price_history`** — append-only: `(listing_id, observed_at, price)`, one row per detected change plus a periodic heartbeat row even when unchanged (so "no data" vs. "confirmed unchanged" are distinguishable).
- **`listing_status_event`** — append-only: `(listing_id, observed_at, status)` — captures the sold/withdrawn/relisted transitions that are themselves a signal (relisted at a lower price after 60 days is informative).
- **`owner_identity`** (best-effort) — candidate identity used for cross-listing dedup: phone number(s) extracted from description/contact fields, agency name, normalized name if present. Many-to-many with `listing`.
- **`search_profile`** — id, name, scope filters (jsonb), thesis parameters (jsonb), created/archived state.
- **`profile_listing_state`** — **correction, implementation review**: keyed `(profile_id, property_id)`, not `(profile_id, listing_id)` as originally sketched here — see the "Review addressed" sections above for why the original keying was a bug (it would let one deduplicated property carry independent, contradictory state per site listing). Columns: score, rank_explanation (LLM-generated, see §9), pipeline_stage, notes, last_scored_at.
- **`feedback_event`** — append-only, keyed on `property_id` (not `listing_id`, same correction as above; `listing_id` is kept only as an optional "which site listing was the user looking at" audit detail): `(profile_id, property_id, listing_id, feedback_type, value, note, created_at)` — the training signal for §7/§8.
- **`ai_assessment`** — per-listing, versioned: occupancy_verdict, condition_verdict, red_flags (jsonb list), description_summary, confidence, model/version used, generated_at — cached so re-scoring on new feedback doesn't require re-running the (costly) LLM/vision pass unless the listing itself changed.

This is intentionally a sketch, not a migration — the actual schema should follow the source project's numeric-PK/typed-column discipline and get its own `docs/architecture/*.md` + `docs/decisions/D-NN-*.md` once implementation starts.

## 6. Deduplication engine

Cross-site dedup is core, not a nice-to-have — private sellers routinely list the same property on 3–4 sites with slightly different photos, prices, or descriptions, and treating those as distinct candidates pollutes every downstream ranking and wastes the investor's attention.

Matching signals, roughly in order of strength:
1. **Cadastral reference**, when derivable from address/coordinates — near-certain match.
2. **Exact address + close coordinates** (within a few meters) + matching m²/rooms within tolerance.
3. **Phone number extracted from the free-text description** (sites often strip contact fields but sellers paste their number into the description anyway) — matches across otherwise-unlinked listings.
4. **Seller/agency reference code** (e.g. Fotocasa's "Referencia: NS603") — a real gap in this list caught after implementation had already started (issue #72): agencies that syndicate a listing to multiple portals very often keep the same internal reference code across all of them, the same practice that makes phone matching useful. Not globally unique (two different agencies can coincidentally use the same short code) — requires the same corroboration discipline as phone matching (agency-name match, or address/price/size proximity) before auto-merging.
5. **Perceptual photo hashing** — same photos (even resized/watermarked differently) reused across a listing on two sites is a strong signal.
6. **Fuzzy match** on address text + price proximity + size proximity as a weaker fallback, surfaced as a *suggested* merge for human confirmation rather than auto-merged, below some confidence threshold.

Merges are reversible and audited (`property_merge_log`): store which listings were merged into which property and on what basis, so a bad auto-merge can be split back apart without data loss. The UI should surface "possible duplicate, not auto-merged" candidates for manual confirmation when confidence is medium.

## 7. Filtering & scoring (per profile)

Two layers, both scoped to a profile:

- **Hard filters** — the scope/exclusion rules from §3; a listing that fails these never reaches the investor for that profile, full stop (e.g. wrong city, no elevator when required).
- **Soft scoring** — everything that passes hard filters gets ranked, not just listed. Score is a blend of:
  - Thesis-fit metrics computed from structured data (yield, price-per-m² vs. area average, days-on-market, price-drop trend).
  - The learned preference model (§8) — how much this listing resembles ones the investor has previously liked/rejected *in this profile*.
  - AI-derived qualitative signals (§9) — e.g. penalize "possibly occupied" for a profile that needs vacant possession.

Every score must ship with a **human-readable explanation** ("ranked high: 6.2% gross yield vs 4.1% area average, priced 12% below comparable listings, 3 photos suggest recent renovation") — an investor won't trust or act on an opaque number, and the explanation is also what makes the feedback loop legible ("I'm rejecting this because the yield estimate looks wrong, not because I dislike the area").

## 8. Feedback loop / preference learning

Feedback types: accept/reject (binary, main signal), star/priority, free-text note, and structured corrections ("this is actually occupied", "yield estimate is wrong, real rent here is X") — corrections should feed back into the AI assessment cache (§5) as ground truth, not just the ranking model.

Learning approach, phased:
- **v1**: transparent weighted-feature model (logistic regression or similar over the structured features already used for hard scoring) retrained per profile on its own feedback history — simple enough to explain, and enough to validate the product loop before investing in anything heavier.
- **later**: incorporate description/photo embeddings so the model can learn softer preferences ("I keep rejecting anything with dated kitchen photos") that aren't captured by structured fields alone.

Cold start (a brand-new profile with no feedback yet) falls back to pure hard-filter + thesis-metric ranking — never blocks on "not enough data," it just doesn't personalize yet.

## 9. AI-enabled features

Reusing the source project's tool-calling LLM architecture (central `assembleRequest` entry point, bounded agentic tool loop, provider-pluggable via OpenRouter) rather than building a new LLM plumbing layer:

- **Conversational search refinement** — "show me flats in this profile under 250k with outdoor space", translated into filter/scope changes, with tool access to query the listing database (read-only) — same shape as the source project's `generate`/`modify` flows over dashboard specs, applied to search-profile scope instead.
- **Explain / compare / analyze** — "why is this ranked #2?", "compare these three", "what changed on this listing since I last looked?" — an `analyze` flow with the same read-only SQL/tool pattern.
- **Occupancy assessment** — LLM read of the description (and ideally photos) to flag likely-occupied ("se vende con inquilino", "alquilada hasta...", furnished-looking photos with personal effects) vs. likely-vacant, with a confidence score — critical for a profile that needs immediate possession.
- **Condition / renovation-need assessment** — from description + photos: reformado / a reformar / obra nueva, and flags like visible damp, dated installations, structural concerns mentioned in text.
- **Red-flag extraction** — legal/financial mentions worth a human's attention: embargo, herencia yacente (unsettled inheritance), comunidad debts, illegal extensions ("construcción no legalizada"), pending litigation.
- **Unstructured-to-structured extraction** — many private listings only have a free-text description; extract rooms/m²/floor/features into structured fields when the site doesn't provide them structured, so those listings aren't unfairly disadvantaged by hard filters that depend on structured data.
- **Photo-based sanity checks** — room count/type plausibility vs. claimed layout, detect stock/staged photos vs. real, rough condition read from images (vision-capable model pass).
- All AI outputs are **cached and versioned** per listing (§5 `ai_assessment`) — re-run only when the listing content changes or the model/prompt version bumps, not on every view.

## 10. Change tracking (new listings & price history)

- Daily connector runs surface **new listings** per profile scope as the primary "what's new" digest item.
- **Price changes** are tracked as first-class events (`listing_price_history`), not just overwritten — a drop after N days on market is itself a ranking-relevant signal (motivated seller) and should be visible in the UI as a trend, not just a current number.
- **Status transitions** (active → reserved/sold/withdrawn, and relisted) are tracked the same way — "sold" removes it from active candidate lists but the historical record stays for comp/market analysis; "withdrawn and relisted 3 weeks later at -10%" is a pattern worth surfacing to the investor.
- **Days-on-market** is a derived metric from `first_seen_at`/status history, used both as a display field and as negotiation-leverage context.

## 11. Investment analytics & metrics

Metrics computed per listing (where the underlying data supports it), to make ranking explanations concrete and to support the deal workspace:

- Price per m² vs. neighborhood/comparable average (needs the market-index/comp data from §4).
- Estimated achievable rent (from comparable active rental listings in the same area/type) and resulting **gross/net rental yield**.
- Simple **cash-on-cash return** estimate given assumed financing parameters (configurable per profile — down payment %, rate, term) — enough for a first-pass filter, not a substitute for real underwriting.
- Days-on-market and price-drop-since-listing, as negotiation signals.
- For flip-type profiles: renovation cost rough-order-of-magnitude (could start as a simple €/m² heuristic by condition tier from the AI condition assessment, refined later) netted against estimated after-repair value from comps.

These are explicitly **decision-support estimates, not underwriting-grade numbers** — the tool should say so in the UI rather than imply false precision.

## 12. Notifications

- Daily/weekly digest (email and/or the dashboard itself) per profile: new candidates above some score threshold, price drops on watchlisted/pipeline properties, status changes on anything in the pipeline.
- Configurable per profile (some theses want daily urgency, others a weekly roundup).
- Watchlist-specific instant-ish alerts (next connector cycle) for price drops or status changes on properties the investor has explicitly flagged as interesting, independent of the digest cadence.

## 13. UI / Dashboard

Reusing the source project's Next.js + Tremor dashboard shell and chat-sidebar pattern rather than building a new frontend from scratch:

- **Profile switcher** — top-level navigation between search profiles, each a self-contained view.
- **Candidate feed** — ranked list/grid with score + one-line explanation, quick accept/reject/star feedback inline (low-friction review sessions are the point).
- **Map view** — geographic distribution of candidates, filterable by score/status.
- **Listing detail** — full normalized data, photo gallery, price/status history chart, AI assessment (occupancy/condition/red flags) with the underlying evidence shown (not just a verdict), cross-site duplicate listings shown together as one property.
- **Deal pipeline / kanban** — per profile: interested → contacted → visited → offer made → closed/rejected, with notes and dates, so the tool doubles as a lightweight acquisition CRM once a listing becomes a real deal.
- **Comparison view** — side-by-side of 2–4 candidates on the metrics that matter for that profile's thesis.
- **Chat sidebar** — conversational refinement and analysis (§9), same architectural slot as the source project's dashboard chat.

## 14. Architecture reuse from powershop-analytics

This project starts as a fork of powershop-analytics specifically because the pipeline shape matches: **external sources → nightly/scheduled sync → normalized Postgres store → AI-driven analytics UI**. Concretely reusable as-is or with light adaptation:

| Source project piece | Reused as |
|---|---|
| `etl/` orchestrator + per-domain `sync/*.py` modules | Connector-runner orchestrator + per-site connector modules (§4) |
| `ps_*` Postgres mirror pattern, watermark-based delta sync | Listing/price-history append-only tracking (§5, §10) |
| `dashboard/lib/llm-context/` central LLM module, agentic tool-calling runner | Conversational search, analyze/compare flows (§9) — same `assembleRequest` boundary, new tool catalog |
| `dashboard/` Next.js + Tremor shell, chat sidebar | Candidate feed, deal pipeline, chat UI (§13) |
| `cli/` unified `ps`-style CLI | Equivalent ops CLI for connector runs, dedup runs, DB inspection |
| Docker Compose + bind-mount data persistence | Same deployment model |
| AI Factory workflows (`.github/workflows/ai-*.yml`, label-driven lifecycle) | Reusable as-is for this repo's own development process, once workflow files are committed by a human (blocked on OAuth `workflow` scope for this initial push) |
| `AGENTS.md`/`ARCHITECTURE.md`/`DECISIONS.md` structure and skills-doc convention | Same documentation discipline, content rewritten for this domain |

What does **not** carry over and needs to be rewritten from scratch: everything domain-specific to PowerShop/4D (the ETL sync modules themselves, the WrenAI semantic model, all business-domain docs/skills, sample queries, data dictionary). Those should be deleted once real connector/schema work starts, rather than left as dead weight — per the source repo's own "backwards compatibility — default is to break it" philosophy, which this project should inherit.

## 15. Legal / compliance / operational constraints

- **Scraping legality & ToS**: most listing sites' terms prohibit automated scraping; prefer official/partner APIs where obtainable (Idealista, Fotocasa) and treat scraping as a fallback with conservative rate limits, a clear identifying user-agent, robots.txt compliance, and no attempt to bypass anti-bot measures (CAPTCHA solving, IP rotation to evade blocks) — this is a personal investment tool, not a commercial scraping operation, and shouldn't be built like one.
- **Personal data (GDPR)**: extracted contact info (phone numbers, names) from listings is personal data even when publicly posted. Minimize retention to what's needed for dedup (§6), avoid building any secondary use (contacting owners in bulk, reselling data), and be deliberate about how long `owner_identity` data is kept.
- **Rate limiting & good-neighbor crawling**: per-connector caps (§4) aren't just about not getting blocked — avoid materially loading source sites' infrastructure.
- **No underwriting liability language**: since §11 metrics are estimates, the UI should never present yield/ROI figures as guaranteed or precise.

## 16. Non-goals / out of scope (v1)

- Multi-tenant SaaS for other investors — this is a single-investor tool; revisit only if there's a reason to productize later.
- Automated bidding/offer submission — the tool surfaces and ranks, a human always acts.
- Full underwriting/financial modeling (mortgage structuring, tax modeling) — §11 metrics are directional, not a replacement for that.
- Geographic scope beyond what the investor is actually targeting — build connectors for real target sites/regions, not a generic "any country" scraper framework up front.

## 17. Open questions for the owner

- Which specific sites and geography are the actual v1 target? (Determines which connectors get built first.)
- Is an Idealista/Fotocasa partner API account available or worth pursuing, vs. scraping-only for v1?
- What financing assumptions (down payment %, typical rate) should default into the cash-on-cash estimate (§11), or should that be entirely per-profile from day one?
- Notification channel preference — email, Slack, dashboard-only, or push?
- Should rejected listings be purged from candidate views but retained in the DB indefinitely (for retraining/market-history value), or is there a retention limit desired (relevant to §15 personal-data minimization for owner identity specifically)?

## 18. Suggested phased roadmap

1. **Foundation**: strip PowerShop-specific ETL/docs/WrenAI content; stand up the canonical schema (§5) and one connector end-to-end (discovery → fetch → normalize → store), no scoring yet — prove the ingestion pipeline.
2. **Dedup + basic filtering**: add a second connector to make cross-site dedup (§6) real, implement hard filters and one search profile, basic dashboard candidate list.
3. **Feedback loop v1**: accept/reject feedback, weighted-feature scoring model (§8 v1), score explanations (§7).
4. **AI layer**: occupancy/condition/red-flag assessment (§9), conversational search via the reused `llm-context` module.
5. **Investment analytics**: comp/yield metrics (§11), price/status history tracking and digests (§10, §12).
6. **Deal workspace**: pipeline/kanban (§13), notes, comparison view.
7. **Multi-profile maturity**: additional profiles, per-profile independent learning validated with real usage, richer photo-based AI assessment.

Each phase should land as its own issue with a `## Plan` / `### Tasks` breakdown per this repo's inherited issue-format convention, once this functional definition is agreed.

items.title: [Note] AI Engineer
items.body:
## AI Engineer 能力地圖：Frame × 關鍵字

以下以每個 frame 作為領域；每個關鍵字一列，欄位固定為一句話理解、概念、技術、實作、情境、注意；「一句話理解」以 Full Stack 工程師熟悉的系統開發視角說明。

### Data Engineering

| 關鍵字 | 一句話理解 | 概念 | 技術 | 實作 | 情境 | 注意 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ETL / ELT | 像後端資料搬運管線：抽取資料、整理格式，再送進分析系統。 | 把來源資料可靠地送到分析層；ETL先轉換、ELT先落地再轉換。 | 批次/增量、CDC、schema evolution、Spark/dbt。 | 以Airflow排程、dbt轉換、資料品質檢查與重跑機制落地。 | 報表、數據同步、資料湖到倉庫。 | 避免全量重跑；處理重複、遲到資料、PII與schema變更。 |
| Data Warehouse | 專門給報表與分析查詢的集中式資料庫。 | 面向分析的集中式資料儲存，重視一致性與查詢效能。 | 星型模型、分區、columnar storage、OLAP。 | 建立raw/staging/mart分層與維度/事實表。 | BI、KPI、跨來源報表。 | 不要把交易庫直接當分析庫；控管成本與資料新鮮度。 |
| Data Lake / Lakehouse | 像大型物件儲存倉庫，但加上可查詢、版本與治理能力。 | 保留大量原始資料並兼顧治理與分析能力。 | Object storage、Parquet、Delta/Iceberg、schema-on-read。 | 以bronze/silver/gold分層，設定catalog、partition與compact。 | 半結構化資料、ML訓練、歷史留存。 | 小檔案與無治理會拖垮查詢；需管理版本、權限與生命週期。 |
| Streaming / Real-time | 把資料當事件即時處理，類似 WebSocket 或 queue consumer。 | 資料事件產生後即時處理，而非等待批次窗口。 | Kafka/PubSub、Flink/Spark Streaming、watermark、幂等。 | 設計topic/schema、consumer group、checkpoint與DLQ。 | 即時告警、推薦、即時儀表板。 | 至少一次不等於不重複；處理順序、背壓、遲到事件與重放。 |
| Data Modeling | 替資料設計可長期維護的 schema、關聯與統計口徑。 | 把業務實體、關係與指標轉成可查詢且可演進的結構。 | 正規化/反正規化、維度建模、SCD、data contract。 | 先定義grain，再建立主鍵、外鍵、指標與欄位字典。 | 跨團隊共用資料、報表與特徵。 | grain不清會造成重複計算；避免只為當下報表硬編模型。 |
| Data Quality & Governance | 替資料加上測試、ownership、權限與可追溯性。 | 確保資料正確、完整、及時、可追溯且有人負責。 | 契約測試、expectations、lineage、catalog、SLA。 | 在pipeline加入schema、null、範圍、freshness與異常告警。 | 重要報表、監管資料、ML輸入。 | 品質規則要可執行；告警過多會被忽略，需訂責任人與處置流程。 |
| Orchestration | 像 CI/CD workflow，負責安排資料任務的順序、重試與排程。 | 管理資料工作流的依賴、重試、排程與可觀測性。 | DAG、Airflow/Dagster、sensor、backfill、retry。 | 任務保持冪等，設定timeout、重試、依賴與失敗通知。 | 多步ETL、每日報表、模型pipeline。 | 不要把業務邏輯塞進排程器；避免隱性依賴與無限重試。 |

### RAG / LLM Application

| 關鍵字 | 一句話理解 | 概念 | 技術 | 實作 | 情境 | 注意 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Architecture | 把 ingestion、搜尋、LLM 與 API 拆成有清楚邊界的服務。 | 定義RAG元件如何串接、資料流如何走，以及同步/非同步邊界。 | Retriever-generator pipeline、API gateway、cache、queue。 | 拆 ingestion、retrieval、generation、evaluation 與 serving。 | 企業知識問答、客服、文件搜尋。 | 先定義延遲、成本、權限與失敗降級，再選框架。 |
| Chunking | 把長文件切成模型搜尋得到、又看得懂的小段落。 | 把文件切成適合檢索與模型上下文的片段。 | 固定長度、語意切分、recursive splitter、overlap。 | 依標題/段落切分，保留metadata並用檢索指標調整大小。 | 長文件問答、規章與技術文件。 | 切太小失去上下文，切太大降低召回；不要切斷表格與程式碼。 |
| Embedding | 把文字轉成可比較相似度的數字向量。 | 將文字轉成向量，讓語意相近內容在向量空間靠近。 | Transformer embedding、cosine similarity、批次embedding。 | 固定模型與版本，建立向量索引並記錄embedding model。 | 語意搜尋、相似案例、RAG召回。 | 模型換版需重建索引；多語、領域詞與向量維度要驗證。 |
| Vector DB | 替 embedding 建索引，讓系統能快速做語意搜尋。 | 儲存與查詢向量及其metadata的資料庫。 | HNSW/IVF、ANN、top-k、filter、Qdrant/pgvector/Milvus。 | 建立collection、索引、metadata filter與刪除/更新流程。 | 大量文件的語意檢索。 | top-k不是品質保證；注意索引更新、租戶隔離與查詢成本。 |
| Metadata Filtering | 像 SQL WHERE，先用權限、租戶或日期縮小搜尋範圍。 | 先用結構化條件縮小可檢索範圍，再做語意搜尋。 | 欄位filter、ACL filter、tenant_id、時間/版本條件。 | 把權限與來源metadata寫入chunk，檢索時強制套用。 | 依部門、產品、日期、權限搜尋。 | filter不能由模型自由決定；缺metadata會造成越權或漏召回。 |
| Hybrid Search | 同時跑關鍵字搜尋和語意搜尋，再合併結果。 | 結合關鍵字精確匹配與向量語意匹配。 | BM25、dense retrieval、rank fusion、RRF。 | 並行查詢兩路召回後融合、去重並評估權重。 | 專有名詞、編號與自然語言混合查詢。 | 只用向量容易漏掉ID/術語；融合權重需用資料驗證。 |
| Reranker | 像搜尋結果的第二輪排序器，把真正相關的內容往前排。 | 對初步召回結果重新排序，提升前幾筆相關性。 | Cross-encoder、Cohere rerank、top-N reranking。 | 先取較大的candidate pool，再對前N筆重排。 | 召回很多但答案常不在前幾筆。 | 會增加延遲與成本；不要把reranker當作權限層。 |
| Query Rewriting | 把使用者模糊的問題改寫成更容易查到資料的查詢。 | 把模糊、口語或多輪問題改寫成更適合檢索的查詢。 | Query expansion、multi-query、HyDE、conversation rewrite。 | 保留原問題，產生候選查詢並記錄改寫結果。 | 追問、省略主詞、跨語言與複雜問題。 | 改寫可能改變原意；需防止注入與錯誤擴張。 |
| Evaluation | 像單元測試與回歸測試，但測的是 AI 回答品質。 | 用可重複的案例與指標衡量檢索和生成品質。 | Recall@k、MRR、faithfulness、answer relevancy、LLM judge。 | 建立golden set、版本化評測並在CI執行回歸測試。 | prompt、模型、chunk策略比較。 | 單一分數會掩蓋失敗類型；要分檢索、生成與安全評估。 |
| Faithfulness | 檢查答案是否真的有文件證據支持。 | 答案是否能被提供的上下文支持，而非模型自行捏造。 | Citation checking、NLI、LLM-as-judge、groundedness。 | 要求引用來源，逐句比對claim與context並設拒答門檻。 | 法規、客服、內部知識問答。 | 有引用不代表真的支持；避免把judge分數當絕對真值。 |
| Hallucination | 模型講得很像真的，但內容其實沒有依據。 | 模型產生與證據不符或不存在的內容。 | Grounding、temperature control、answer abstention、fact check。 | 無證據時拒答，輸出引用與信心，記錄錯誤案例回歸。 | 資料不完整或問題超出知識庫。 | 降低temperature無法根治；需改善召回與輸出驗證。 |
| Failure Modes | 列出系統會怎麼壞，並預先設計偵測、降級與復原。 | 系統在資料、檢索、模型、工具或網路異常下的失敗型態。 | Failure taxonomy、chaos test、timeout、retry、DLQ。 | 建立錯誤分類、fallback、告警與可重現測試案例。 | 上線前演練與事故分析。 | 只測happy path不夠；重試可能放大流量與費用。 |

### Agent

| 關鍵字 | 一句話理解 | 概念 | 技術 | 實作 | 情境 | 注意 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Workflow | 像後端狀態機，把 Agent 任務拆成可控制的步驟。 | 把Agent任務拆成可追蹤、可重試、可控的步驟。 | State machine、DAG、LangGraph、workflow engine。 | 明確定義節點輸入輸出、轉移條件與終止條件。 | 多步研究、客服處理、資料操作。 | 避免讓模型自行決定所有流程；限制迴圈與最大步數。 |
| Tool Calling | 讓模型用結構化參數呼叫 API，而不是只產生文字。 | 讓模型以結構化參數呼叫外部工具完成工作。 | Function calling、JSON schema、tool registry。 | 驗證參數、套用權限、執行工具並把結果回傳模型。 | 查詢API、寄信、寫入資料庫。 | 工具呼叫等同權限操作；需白名單、審計與人工核准。 |
| State | 保存 Agent 做到哪裡、拿到什麼結果，以及下一步要做什麼。 | 保存Agent在多步任務中的上下文、結果與目前階段。 | State schema、checkpoint、短期/長期記憶。 | 用明確schema儲存狀態，支援重試、恢復與版本遷移。 | 長流程、多輪對話、非同步任務。 | 不要把所有對話無限塞進prompt；避免狀態污染與競態。 |
| Planning | 讓 Agent 先拆任務再執行，但每一步仍要驗證。 | 先決定子任務與執行順序，再逐步完成目標。 | ReAct、plan-and-execute、task decomposition。 | 限制計畫深度，逐步驗證工具結果並允許重新規劃。 | 研究、複合查詢、跨系統流程。 | 計畫不是事實；每一步都需驗證，並防止無限重新規劃。 |
| Guardrails | 像 middleware 與 policy layer，限制模型與工具能做什麼。 | 在輸入、工具、輸出各階段限制Agent可做的事。 | Policy engine、schema validation、content filter、allowlist。 | 建立前置/後置檢查，違規時拒絕、修正或轉人工。 | 高風險自動化、金融、客服。 | 只做輸出過濾不夠；工具層和資料層也要防護。 |
| Human-in-the-loop | 高風險動作先停住，交給人核准後才繼續。 | 在高風險或不確定步驟由人審核、接管或核准。 | Approval gate、confidence threshold、escalation。 | 設計待審佇列、審核理由、逾時與回滾流程。 | 付款、刪除、對外發信、敏感回答。 | 人工介入點要可量化；避免所有案件都卡在人工作業。 |
| Structured Output | 要求模型回傳符合 JSON Schema 的資料，方便程式接續處理。 | 要求模型輸出可被程式可靠解析的固定結構。 | JSON schema、Pydantic、constrained decoding。 | 解析後做schema與業務規則驗證，失敗則修復或重試。 | API回應、分類、工作流節點。 | 格式正確不代表內容正確；限制欄位長度與注入內容。 |
| Evaluation | 像單元測試與回歸測試，但測的是 AI 回答品質。 | 用可重複的案例與指標衡量檢索和生成品質。 | Recall@k、MRR、faithfulness、answer relevancy、LLM judge。 | 建立golden set、版本化評測並在CI執行回歸測試。 | prompt、模型、chunk策略比較。 | 單一分數會掩蓋失敗類型；要分檢索、生成與安全評估。 |

### LLM Evaluation

| 關鍵字 | 一句話理解 | 概念 | 技術 | 實作 | 情境 | 注意 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

### Multi-tenant

| 關鍵字 | 一句話理解 | 概念 | 技術 | 實作 | 情境 | 注意 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Multi-tenant Architecture | 同一套後端服務多家公司，但每家的資料與資源必須隔離。 | 同一平台服務多個租戶，同時共享效率與隔離安全。 | Shared service、tenant context、quota、policy。 | 每個request注入tenant context，所有資料與快取操作強制帶租戶。 | SaaS型AI平台。 | 租戶邊界必須端到端驗證，不能只靠前端參數。 |
| Tenant Isolation | 確保任何查詢、快取、檔案與向量都不會跨租戶。 | 防止一個租戶讀寫另一個租戶的資料與資源。 | Logical/physical isolation、ACL、RLS、network policy。 | 在資料庫、快取、向量庫、物件儲存與日誌都套隔離。 | 共享基礎設施的SaaS。 | 要測越權與錯誤租戶context；背景任務也要帶tenant。 |
| Tenant ID | 像 request context 的主鍵，必須一路帶過 API、DB、queue 與 log。 | 識別請求所屬租戶並貫穿整個資料流。 | JWT claims、request context、composite key。 | 由可信身份來源取得，寫入資料表、trace、queue與cache key。 | 多租戶API與非同步工作。 | 不可信任使用者自行傳入的tenant_id；防止IDOR。 |
| Shared Database / Shared Schema | 所有租戶共用表，用 tenant_id 與 RLS 做隔離。 | 所有租戶共用資料庫與schema，以成本換取隔離複雜度。 | tenant_id、RLS、composite index、partition。 | 所有表加tenant_id，Repository層強制篩選並做隔離測試。 | 大量小租戶、成本敏感SaaS。 | 漏一個where就可能資料外洩；索引與熱租戶需特別處理。 |
| Database per Tenant | 每個租戶一個資料庫，隔離更強但維運成本更高。 | 每個租戶使用獨立資料庫，隔離與客製化較強。 | Database provisioning、migration orchestration、connection pool。 | 自動建立/升級/備份資料庫並管理租戶路由。 | 少量大型或合規租戶。 | 運維與連線成本高；migration與跨租戶分析更複雜。 |
| Row-Level Security | 讓資料庫本身強制每列資料能被哪個租戶看到。 | 由資料庫在每一列層級強制租戶存取政策。 | PostgreSQL RLS、session context、policy。 | 交易開始設定tenant context，並測試直接SQL與服務帳號路徑。 | 共享schema的強制隔離。 | 繞過RLS的管理連線很危險；政策需納入migration與測試。 |
| Tenant-aware API | API 從驗證到查詢都必須知道目前是哪個租戶。 | API在授權、資料查詢與回應中都理解租戶邊界。 | JWT、middleware、OPA、quota。 | middleware解析tenant，服務層拒絕不一致context並套用配額。 | 多租戶REST/GraphQL服務。 | 不要只在controller過濾；內部服務與webhook也要驗證。 |
| Multi-tenant Scaling | 避免單一大租戶吃光資源，並能依租戶分片、限流與擴容。 | 在租戶數、流量與資料量成長時維持隔離與效能。 | Quota、sharding、partition、autoscaling、noisy-neighbor control。 | 依租戶分片/限流，監控單租戶資源與升級路徑。 | SaaS成長與大型租戶加入。 | 平均容量會掩蓋熱租戶；需壓測最壞分布。 |
