## 4. Native object model and source formats

### Typed objects with structured identity

Use provider-owned kinds, illustratively:

```text
ptah.run/mongodb/collection
ptah.run/mongodb/index
ptah.run/mongodb/view
ptah.run/mongodb/search-index       # extension workstream, not an ordinary index
```

A collection definition owns its collection options and validator state. Indexes are independently addressable child resources; views are independently addressable namespace resources. A validator has no independent MongoDB object name: do not invent a second independently managed validator resource that can conflict with the collection definition.

Keep database, collection/view name, index family and index name as separate reference components. Collections and views share a physical namespace; a different kind tag must not permit both to claim the same database/name. Do not split names on dots, lowercase them globally, or confuse a document field path with an object reference. Keep namespace identity separate from collation semantics.

Capture collection UUID as **observed identity/precondition evidence**, not portable desired state. Preserve desired versus observed distinctions and explicit managed/absent/defaulted/uninspected dispositions. Native changes carry their complete before/after operands, ownership context, dependencies and relevant evidence; do not recover missing operands from a later live read.

### BSON is a semantic requirement

Use concrete provider types for collection/index/view definitions and an ordered BSON representation for expression/pipeline fragments. The [Go driver distinguishes ordered `bson.D` from unordered `bson.M`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/go/current/data-formats/bson/). Preserve key order where meaningful, especially compound indexes, commands, sort documents, pipelines and literal embedded documents.

The codec must preserve missing versus null, integer widths, large integers, Decimal128, doubles, dates versus timestamps, ObjectId, binary subtype/UUID, regex and nested arrays/documents. Reject duplicate keys in authored definitions and malformed/oversized payloads; never silently take the last value. Unknown observed values must be preserved with coverage limitations or rejected explicitly, not coerced to strings or empty objects.

Use [Extended JSON v2](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mongodb-extended-json/) for readable BSON-bearing input/output and a versioned provider-owned encoding inside the generic wire envelope. **Canonical Extended JSON is a type-preserving interchange format, not by itself a semantic fingerprint algorithm.** Define deterministic, versioned comparison/fingerprint projections separately. Normalize only proven equivalents: never recursively sort every BSON document or erase BSON type differences globally.

### HCL first, without an unordered BSON shortcut

Use the shared HCL evaluator and #4204's provider schema descriptors. The provider supplies its block/attribute semantics and diagnostics; it does not implement another HCL evaluator. Preserve source ranges and field paths through plugin calls.

Illustrative syntax to finalize against the SDK; this is **not a claim that the syntax already exists**:

```hcl
mongodb_collection "users" {
  validator_ejson   = file("users.validator.ejson")
  validation_level  = "strict"
  validation_action = "error"

  index "users_tenant_email" {
    key {
      path = "tenant_id"
      kind = "asc"
    }
    key {
      path = "email"
      kind = "asc"
    }
    unique = true
  }
}
```

Example `users.validator.ejson`:

```json
{
  "$jsonSchema": {
    "bsonType": "object",
    "required": ["tenant_id", "email"],
    "properties": {
      "tenant_id": { "bsonType": "string" },
      "email": { "bsonType": "string" }
    }
  }
}
```

Repeated key blocks preserve compound-key ordering; `keys = { ... }` is not an acceptable ordered representation. BSON fragments must not pass through `jsondecode`/generic maps that lose order or numeric meaning. File contents are resolved by the normal source-loading workflow and frozen into the planned artifact, not reread as different bytes at apply time.

Provide faithful HCL export and a versioned provider-native representation for schema snapshots/migration units. SQL, DBML and relational Go-model inputs must fail explicitly where they cannot express MongoDB semantics; do not invent lossy collection/table conversions. Offline decode/compare/render works without credentials or a live database, using an explicit target profile with unresolved runtime facts visible.

## 5. Functional scope and capability accounting

### Required first delivery

| Family | Required behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Ordinary collections | Inspect/export, create, explicit approved drop, options comparison; explicit same-database rename with collision/UUID checks and no implicit `dropTarget` |
| Validators | MongoDB `$jsonSchema`, supported query-expression validators and their combinations; add/change/remove; validation level/action; correct staged 9.0 constraint transitions |
| Ordinary indexes | Single/compound keys; ascending/descending, hashed, text, wildcard and supported geospatial key types; unique, sparse, partial, collation, TTL and hidden options; inspect/create/drop and legal in-place modifications |
| Standard views | Source collection/view, ordered aggregation pipeline, collation, dependencies; create/modify/drop, cycles/conflicts and unsupported-pipeline diagnostics |
| Versioned migrations | Reviewable typed schema operations plus explicitly authored bounded document mutations/assertions; checksums, history/status, recovery and verification |
| Operational workflow | Install -> connect -> inspect -> declare -> diff/plan -> apply -> inspect/no-diff; offline artifacts and missing-plugin diagnostics |

Support is measured **per operation and option combination**, not by an engine-wide boolean. Do not advertise an index family merely because its create command can be sent: inspection/normalization/export/diff and safe refusal paths must work too. Multikey behavior arises from indexed document values; do not invent a portable `multikey = true` creation option.

For each feature record supported, unsupported by MongoDB, not implemented by this provider, unavailable for the selected server/FCV/topology/deployment, permission denied, or unverified. These are different dispositions. Runtime probing is read-only; an authorization failure is not proof that a feature does not exist.

Target **pinned MongoDB 8.0 and 9.0 release lines** for initial integration evidence, with exact patch versions, driver versions and FCVs recorded at implementation time. Include standalone and replica-set fixtures with explicit transaction differences. Test lower-FCV/version rejection independently. These are proposed certification targets, not claims that tests have already passed. Other release lines require declared evidence rather than extrapolation.

MongoDB [9.0 was released on 29 September 2026](https://www.mongodb.com/products/updates/mongodb-9-0-is-now-available/). Do not base the provider on an outdated assumption that validators only have the older levels.

### Explicit extension boundary, not silent feature loss

| Area | Disposition for this issue |
| --- | --- |
| Capped, clustered and time-series collections | Recognize, inspect/export or report exact incomplete coverage, and preserve. Full lifecycle/alteration support is a separately scoped extension; never treat them as ordinary collections. |
| Search / Vector Search indexes | Separate native-object extension workstream described below. Distinct from ordinary/text indexes; do not claim complete index coverage from `listIndexes`. |
| Sharding, shard keys, zones, resharding, balancing | Out of first-delivery mutation scope. Detect topology and refuse unsupported mutation workflows rather than operate directly on a shard as if standalone. |
| Users/roles, Atlas projects/clusters, backup policies | Separate security/control-plane scope; no automatic account or cloud-resource management. |
| Queryable/client-side encryption, key vaults and internal state collections | Recognize/protect relevant state; no implicit encryption/key-management support or destructive rebuild. |
| Change-stream subscriptions, application CDC/catch-up and embedding generation | Not generated from schema diff; separate authored/application workflows. Collection pre/post-image settings may be added as typed capabilities, not a claim to manage consumers. |
| DocumentDB, Cosmos DB MongoDB API, FerretDB and other compatibility layers | Not certified by MongoDB wire/URI compatibility. Require explicit support profiles and tests; reject positively identified unsupported products before mutation. |

An unsupported unrelated resource should not prevent all read-only inventory or provably unrelated safe operations. It **must** block an operation whose correctness/preservation depends on understanding it, especially parent drop/recreation or cascade.

## 6. Inspection, ownership, and no-diff correctness

Use [`listCollections`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/listcollections/) for actual options, validators, collection kinds, view definitions and UUIDs, and [`listIndexes`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/listindexes/) for ordinary indexes. Exhaust cursors with bounded streaming; cancellation, a failed later batch or unreadable required fields must not become a complete empty result.

`authorizedCollections: true` together with `nameOnly: true` can expose only the namespaces accessible to the user and omit the options needed for comparison. Never use that result as a complete database snapshot. Report permission-limited coverage and the actual missing inspection capability.

Inspection does not sample documents to invent required fields, create collections/history/locks, or run mutating feature probes. Optional data-quality preflights are separately requested bounded reads, with separate permissions and explicit cost/completeness.

Define scope independently for collections, their owned indexes and relevant options. **Omitted is not automatically “delete everything else.”** Destructive authoritative management requires explicit scope and adequate coverage. Preserve unowned indexes/options; never claim complete state after discarding unknown metadata.

Protect `admin`, `local`, `config`, `system.*`, time-series buckets, recognized encryption internals, and Ptah's exact configured history/lock/checkpoint resources. Do not emit ordinary drop operations for engine-managed `_id` indexes. Explicit adoption of a managed namespace must not adopt the whole database accidentally.

Normalize effective defaults and server-generated metadata without losing source intent: inherited collation, absent versus false, absent versus TTL zero, generated index names, index-version fields, and normalized text/wildcard definitions need real round-trip tests. Document data, index-build progress and other transient runtime state must not cause perpetual schema drift.

Introspection across several commands is not automatically a point-in-time metadata snapshot. Use primary/read-consistency behavior appropriate to the supported workflow, detect relevant concurrent changes, and revalidate object UUIDs and metadata before each dependent mutation. A Ptah lock does not stop an external administrator changing the collection.

## 7. Planning and safety rules

The plugin contributes typed changes, effects, object dependencies, exact native units, preconditions, verification and transaction constraints. The host owns the final graph, policy and execution order. Pure decode/compare/plan calls must not mutate anything.

### Validators are not automatic data repair

MongoDB implements its own [JSON Schema dialect](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/jsonschema/), including `bsonType` and documented omissions. Do not validate with an unrelated generic JSON Schema dialect and assume MongoDB will interpret it identically.

Treat validator changes as possible application-compatibility or integrity changes. Conservatively distinguish tightening, weakening and unknown effects where provable; do not claim logical equivalence/implication for arbitrary MQL predicates from textual similarity.

For the older levels, switching to `strict` does **not** retroactively certify old documents. `moderate`, `off`, `warn` and validation bypass are not interchangeable safety strategies. Never silently weaken enforcement to make an apply pass.

For [MongoDB 9.0 `constraint` validation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/schema-validation/specify-validation-level/), model the documented state machine: existing-collection preparation, allowed validation actions, the full existing-data check and its cost, and restrictions on changing a validator while constrained. A rule change may require a visible temporary downgrade to `strict`, rule update, preparation and re-establishment of the constraint. That enforcement gap is an explicit plan effect requiring policy approval. Preparation is a mutation, not a read-only preflight. Failed intermediate steps must remain visible/recoverable.

For a staged application rollout, document expand -> deploy compatible writers -> bounded backfill -> verification -> contract. The application rollout and business transformation remain author responsibilities. Ptah must not infer how to split a person's name or regenerate embeddings from a schema change.

### Index changes have distinct operational and data effects

Use [`collMod`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/collmod/) only for supported in-place changes, such as TTL/hidden state and applicable unique conversion. A changed key pattern or an unsupported option change is not automatically an in-place alteration. [Index rename requires replacement](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/indexes/); replacement ordering must account for server conflicts and cannot assume old/new indexes can coexist.

For unique conversion, model `prepareUnique`, validation and completion as separate effects where used. A server dry run is specific to that supported operation, not a general MongoDB plan simulation. Never deduplicate data automatically. Enforce MongoDB's [unique-index semantics](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-unique/), including missing/null values, partial filters, collation, multikey behavior and prohibited combinations such as unique hashed indexes.

Creating TTL or reducing retention is a **potentially destructive data change**, even though represented as metadata. Expiration can delete existing documents; restoring the previous TTL does not restore them. Invalid compound-TTL combinations must be rejected rather than accepted because the server might ignore the option. See [TTL behavior](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-ttl/).

A [hidden index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-hidden/) still enforces uniqueness and TTL. Hiding is not disabling its integrity/deletion effects. Index builds/replacements also need explicit disk/workload/availability risk reporting; do not promise zero blocking or constant-time cancellation.

### Collection and view operations

Never silently drop/recreate a collection to change an immutable option, collation or collection kind. Refuse unsupported transformations; a future copy/catch-up/cutover strategy would require its own explicit data-preservation design. An explicit drop is irreversible with respect to document data; recreating metadata is not a rollback.

For views, retain `viewOn` and ordered pipelines, and extract namespace dependencies from supported `$lookup`, `$graphLookup`, `$unionWith` and nested pipelines. Handle shared collection/view namespaces and cycles. Unknown dependency-bearing constructs cannot silently produce a complete graph; require sufficient explicit evidence or refuse dependent destructive changes. [`$out`/`$merge` are not standard view definitions](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/collmod/); materialization belongs to authored data work, not a view-creation fallback.

## 8. Native migration artifacts and document migrations

Introduce/reuse a **generic provider-native migration representation** in the host workflow. It must carry format/version, provider identity, migration identity, ordered unit IDs, required features, checksums, typed payloads, assertions, recovery/reverse information and source locations. The format registration mechanism is generic; BSON decoding stays in the plugin.

A readable MongoDB encoding can use `.mongodb.json` plus Extended JSON payloads; finalize naming against #4204. Do not store JSON in `.sql`, wrap it in fake SQL statements/comments, or require a SQL lexer to discover/split/hash it. Rendering to SQL must explicitly refuse. Human-readable plans expose resource, operation, relevant before/after state, risk and execution boundaries alongside the full accepted native artifact.

The first native document-operation vocabulary should cover explicit inserts, filtered updates (including supported update pipelines), filtered deletes, and bounded read assertions. Each operation declares its target namespaces, scope/bounds, relevant options, expected results, failure behavior and retry classification. Schema commands use typed planned operations, not an unrestricted hidden `runCommand` escape hatch.

No arbitrary JavaScript, server-side code execution, hidden shell programs, or unconstrained administrative commands are required. Unsupported operators and namespace-changing/data-output stages must be rejected rather than bypass dependency, protected-resource or approval checks. Disabling document validation requires a visible explicit operation option and policy decision, never a global hidden convenience.

### Bounded execution and restart

[MongoDB `updateMany`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.updatemany/) is atomic per document, not across the whole matching set. Partial modifications survive failure. A successful schema diff also says nothing about whether a business-data migration completed.

Provide bounded batches, progress and durable checkpoints for the supported long-running backfill path. Define selection/resume-key assumptions, BSON ordering, operation and time budgets, original-filter rechecks and terminal verification. Do not pretend `updateMany` has a global row-limit guarantee or that a preflight count prevents concurrent writers expanding its scope.

Resume only when idempotence or transactional/checkpoint evidence justifies it. A generic `idempotent = true` declaration does not prove safety; retain the author's responsibility and the actual mechanism. Non-idempotent increments, appends or generated values must not be blindly replayed after an unknown outcome.

A document `schemaVersion` field is optional **application-owned data**, not Ptah's migration-history version. Never inject it automatically. A schema fingerprint excludes ordinary data, so bind document-migration preconditions and postconditions separately and state the concurrent-writer assumptions. Online guarantees need cooperating writers or an explicit write window; this plugin is not a general ETL/CDC orchestrator.

Generated reverse schema operations, authored compensating data operations, and actual transaction rollback are different concepts. Do not promise a `down` migration can restore dropped documents, expired data or overwritten values that were never captured.

## 9. Sessions, history, locks, and uncertain outcomes

Use #4204's session handles and history policy. Keep clients, sessions, cursors and transactions inside the provider. Require an explicit target database; do not confuse `authSource` with it or silently migrate the driver's default database. Use the native URI parser for replica-set/SRV/TLS/auth options, redact credentials and distinguish authentication from namespace/DDL authorization.

### Transaction boundaries

MongoDB [permits some collection/index creation inside transactions under restrictions](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions-operations/); it does not provide a universal transaction around an arbitrary metadata migration. Initial metadata plans should expose non-atomic units unless a particular transactional strategy is explicitly implemented and tested. Reject a requested all-or-nothing mode that cannot be honored.

Bounded document transactions on supported replica sets may share their session with the corresponding history/checkpoint writes where the engine permits. Ordinary inspection must not be pushed inside a transaction that forbids `listCollections`/`listIndexes`. Configure/test supported write/read concerns and driver retry behavior; an RPC batch or a transaction callback is not an exactly-once guarantee.

### Storage primitives, not another migrator

Use protected MongoDB collections to implement the host's revision/step/checkpoint and lock contracts. Initialization is a visible mutation step, never a side effect of inspect/plan. Store migration and step identities, immutable input digest, provider semantic identity, known progress/outcomes and recovery evidence under host policy. Do not put TTL on revision/checkpoint evidence.

Scope cooperative locking to the actual managed database/resources, not just a source directory. Contending projects must not independently mutate the same namespace. Use atomic conditional ownership changes and owner-checked renew/release operations, with documented durability and failover semantics.

**A TTL index is not a mutex, and an expired lease is not proof the former executor stopped.** A token stored in a lock/history document does not fence a separately issued MongoDB DDL command. On lease loss, stop dispatch; on uncertain ownership or an in-flight write, fail closed. Do not permit automatic takeover/replay unless the former executor is conclusively stopped or fenced and outstanding outcomes are reconciled. Re-reading metadata alone does not prevent a paused former owner from resuming later. A first implementation may use durable non-expiring ownership with explicit recovery rather than claim safe automatic failover from a TTL lease. Document stale-owner recovery and test a paused former owner resuming after another process attempts takeover.

The lock coordinates cooperating Ptah executions; it cannot prevent external application/admin changes. Treat standalone durability and replica-set failover guarantees separately.

### Recovery and approval binding

Preserve #4204's outcomes: not started, running, confirmed applied/not applied/rolled back, known partial failure, and outcome unknown. A timeout, plugin death, cancelled context or lost reply after dispatch does not prove rollback. No automatic whole-migration retry.

After ambiguity, inspect the relevant full definitions/UUIDs and durable history before resuming. Object-name existence alone is insufficient evidence that the exact requested operation succeeded. Where evidence cannot determine the result, retain an unresolved status and require explicit recovery rather than manufacture success.

Bind accepted plans to provider semantic identity/build policy, payload/fingerprint versions, exact units, target database identity, relevant UUIDs/metadata, capabilities/FCV and declared data preconditions. Resolve source variables before approval. Provider changes, target recreation or relevant drift invalidate the plan; credentials and confidential query results do not enter artifacts/logs.

## 10. Search / Vector Search extension design

Do not bake in the assumption that these require only an Atlas Administration HTTP API: the [Go driver exposes search-index management](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/go/current/indexes/), and actual availability depends on the deployment. They are a separate object family with their own inspection/coverage and capability profile.

A later implementation should cover typed search/vector definitions, names and types, mappings/analyzers or vector dimensions/similarity/quantization, exact definition comparison, create/update/drop and referenced-collection dependencies. Model unsupported/unknown fields explicitly, including features that trigger external embedding work or cost.

[`listIndexes` excludes Search indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/listindexes/); use the dedicated listing surface. [Search index management is asynchronous](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/php-library/v1.x/reference/method/mongodbcollection-createsearchindex/): acceptance of a request is not successful/queryable completion. Require bounded polling, observed desired definition, readiness/version evidence, explicit failure/timeout handling and restart reconciliation. An old definition remaining queryable must not count as successful application of a new definition.

Keep deployment provisioning, embedding generation/backfill and application query cutover out of this object reconciler. This extension is an architectural test for generic long-running native operations, not permission to bypass Ptah's plan/history boundary. Its full implementation is not required to close the first-delivery scope above.

## 11. Verification and documentation

Test the **packaged subprocess path** through the public SDK, not only helper functions in the plugin repository.

Required suites include:

- Native-only schemas/plans with no relational objects; fixture and real plugin add native kinds without editing host semantic switches; source-to-plan-to-apply-to-inspect round trips and repeated empty diffs.
- Compound key ordering; literal BSON document order; exact numeric/BSON types; missing/null/default distinctions; duplicate keys; codec/fingerprint stability; text/wildcard normalization; shared namespace collisions and case/dot-containing names.
- Validators against heterogeneous pre-existing data; strict versus moderate; explicit weakening/bypass; 9.0 constraint preparation/success/failure/rule change and older-version/FCV refusal.
- Ordinary index families/options and invalid combinations; duplicate/null/partial unique cases; hidden unique/TTL behavior; in-place TTL changes; replacement conflicts; irreversible-effect reports; standard-view dependencies and cycles.
- Permission-limited/name-only inspection, multi-batch cursor failure, unknown collection/index state, unmanaged resources and protected internal/history resources. No destructive plan from incomplete coverage.
- Interrupted data batches, idempotent versus non-idempotent replay, concurrent writers, checkpoint recovery, data assertions, transaction-mode refusal and correct history coupling.
- Competing Ptah processes, stale/paused owners, lease loss, primary stepdown, timeout and crash after server acceptance but before history/reply; no fabricated success, rollback or automatic takeover.
- Missing/untrusted/incompatible plugin; offline help/decode behavior; secrets/TLS/auth failures; subprocess stdout/LSP framing; fresh external-module builds, installed-package discovery and cleanup.

Use pinned standalone and replica-set fixtures; do not infer failover evidence from a single-node development replica set. Sharded/deployment-restricted negative tests must prevent unsupported writes. Record Atlas evidence separately from local Community/Enterprise evidence; credentials and cloud spend are explicit CI inputs, never required to build the host.

Build/import gates prove that `ptah`, `ptah-compat` and `ptah-ls` retain `CGO_ENABLED=0` builds and that their module/dependency graphs do not contain the plugin or MongoDB/BSON-only dependencies. Record inspect/plan/apply overhead and RPC counts; metadata and document batches must remain bounded.

Publish runnable guides for installation/configuration, connection/auth/TLS and required privileges by workflow, schema inventory/adoption, HCL/BSON types, first migration, schema versus document changes, validator rollout, index risks, native artifacts, transactions/history, uncertain-outcome recovery and the exact support matrix. Include a complete expand/backfill/contract example and the missing-plugin -> setup link -> successful rerun flow. Examples run in CI. Clearly separate unsupported engine behavior, implementation gaps and unverified deployments.

## 12. Delivery sequence and definition of done

1. **Native-only seam and ADR:** map this design onto #4204, close generic source/artifact/history/coverage gaps, publish the operation/version matrix and record source/test baselines. No second pipeline or pre-refactor compatibility work.
2. **Read/declare/compare slice:** external repository, driver/session setup, registration and offline codecs/descriptors, accurate inspection/export and native-only diff/plan with no mutation hidden in analysis.
3. **Metadata execution:** required collections, validators, ordinary indexes and views; exact native units, host history/locks, safe non-atomic execution and recovery; real repeat-to-no-diff tests.
4. **Document migrations:** versioned native artifacts, bounded mutations/assertions/backfills, progress/checkpoints, explicit retry/transaction/reverse semantics and rollout example.
5. **Release:** full subprocess conformance, fault tests, independent artifacts, optional install flow, setup/catalog documentation and measured capability evidence. Preserve explicit extension boundaries for advanced collection kinds, Search/Vector Search, sharding and security/control-plane work.

Completion requires:

- [ ] The implementation lives in `stokaro/ptah-mongodb-plugin`, is separately installable and is not embedded or bundled by default.
- [ ] Only #4204's public SDK/protocol and neutral contracts are used; host/SDK dependency and CGO gates pass.
- [ ] Native-only schema and migration workflows reach the actual Ptah pipeline, with one planner/history policy and no fake SQL or parallel document core.
- [ ] Collection/index/view/validator semantics, ordered BSON, identity, source positions, coverage and deterministic normalization survive decode -> inspect -> compare -> plan -> execute -> export.
- [ ] The required metadata and versioned document workflows work against the declared pinned server/FCV/topology matrix; inspection and plan generation are read-only.
- [ ] Native migration discovery/checksums/status and SQL-only format refusals work; no unsupported file or payload is silently skipped.
- [ ] Unmanaged/unknown/system/history state is preserved or blocks dependent destructive work; no silent collection recreation or automatic data repair.
- [ ] Validator/TTL/unique/index-replacement risks and 9.0 constraint transitions are modeled and tested; data verification is not confused with schema no-diff.
- [ ] Lock contention/loss, partial application, ambiguous outcomes, recovery, stale-plan rejection and bounded backfill replay are tested through real subprocesses.
- [ ] Fresh installation, setup links, missing/incompatible-provider diagnostics, source builds and supported packaged targets are documented and tested.
- [ ] Advanced families have honest inspection/coverage/refusal dispositions and documented extension boundaries, not an unqualified “MongoDB fully supported” claim.

**Non-goals:** MongoSQL/SQL DDL translation; embedding MongoDB in the host; a second plugin system or migrator; legacy Ptah compatibility/import tooling; unrestricted JS/`mongosh` execution; automatic validator inference or business-data repair; general ETL/CDC/copy-and-cutover orchestration; implicit Atlas infrastructure/user management; or untested certification of MongoDB-compatible products.

items.title: Deliver an independently packaged durable rule execution model
items.body:
## Objective
Deliver an opt-in, separately packaged fixed-point rule execution model that runs through production durability and hosting mechanisms, survives restart, reaches a durable terminal outcome and can return to a native workflow without model-specific branches in the shared runtime.

## Context
Production continuation step 4 of Program #2892 explicitly requires an independent fourth model; agent collaboration is native composition and does not satisfy it. Research #2901 proved a packed rule-model witness with 29 assertions, but only work-level cancellation. This task closes the production lifecycle gap; it does not reopen the completed research task or promise a general-purpose rules product.

Parent: #2905. [Current-source readiness audit](https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-foundation/issues/2892#issuecomment-6322261454). Discovery baseline: `adbc7417c42055e32437eddaeb2f80c980d4c666`, with main `4014274b6` integrated. Refresh source and concurrent work before claiming.

## Scope and architecture constraints
- Preserve the research witness's bounded deterministic fixed-point semantics as the example model. Model-owned state, round progression and terminal cancellation are distinct from worker cancellation.
- Package the model independently and exercise the actual local NuGet artifact through normal deployment/NuGet composition in a host without a project reference to its engine implementation. Hosts deliberately install trusted packages; package/artifact/schema identity and supported capabilities must be pinned and validated. This is not an arbitrary runtime package-download service or publisher-authentication claim.
- Prefer a model-owned runtime/store using the existing first-party EF family and an opt-in native adapter through existing checkpoint/outbox/bookmark contracts, following accepted ADR 0087 and spec 242's lifecycle boundaries. Reuse demonstrated scope, admission, delivery, ownership and idempotency mechanisms. Rule transitions, receipts and owed delivery commit atomically in the rule domain's own store. The native checkpoint/outbox/bookmark bridge is separately idempotent; no cross-store atomic transaction is implied. Do not force model state into the workflow checkpoint's typed participants or extract a universal execution API merely because a generic registry is absent.
- Preserve the qualified host's membership/authority rules. No second cluster membership service, actor per rule/node, model-name switch in the common runtime, or duplicate native orchestration authority.
- Runtime consumes immutable artifacts/configuration and versioned model state; mutable design storage is unavailable in the recovery proof. Preserve existing workflow definitions/state and Sequence/Flowchart semantics.
- Define safe model inspection and terminal result consumption, including direct execution and the native adapter. Any shared contract extracted must have concrete consumers and reviewed compatibility evidence.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] A reviewed rule-specific contract/spec records domain/package placement, publication/pin resolution, capability refusal, authoritative state/receipt commit boundary, durable model cancellation and additive schema/rollback behavior. An ADR is required only if the design changes accepted cross-domain policy. Source discovery resolves overlap with open PR #2891 / #1785 before changing activity-capability registration; adopt or reuse that work, do not duplicate it.
- [x] A clean host consumes the actual independently packed artifact through normal deployment/NuGet composition, without an engine implementation project reference, runs the deterministic fixed-point example to its declared result and exposes model-owned state/causal progress. No model-name branch is added to shared workflow/hosting infrastructure.
- [x] A real predecessor process stops between persisted rounds and a successor resumes the same run/artifact/state identity. Accepted decisions/results are not recomputed as new logical rounds. Duplicate equivalent results do not advance twice; conflicting, stale-owner and wrong-invocation results cannot mutate authoritative state.
- [x] Durable model cancellation, including cancellation before admission/dispatch and after a result is stored but before consumption, produces the declared terminal model outcome. Late work/results cannot resurrect the run or advance its parent. Lease expiry is not treated as proof that physical work stopped.
- [x] Direct execution and native invocation use the same packaged model implementation. Real persisted Sequence and Flowchart parents consume success, fault and cancellation through the normal child boundary; their ordering/join semantics remain theirs, and successful completion reaches the following native activity.
- [x] Unknown or mismatched package/artifact/state schemas, unsupported capabilities, malformed state and fabricated/conflicting progress are explicitly refused before state mutation. Artifact/state versions and invocation/result identities remain stable across supported reloads.
- [x] An additive persistence upgrade preserves existing native executions; rollback stops new admissions while retaining capable readers/workers for accepted rule runs. No implicit conversion or abandonment of active executions.
- [x] Scoped run/state/result inspection and the relevant author/integrator documentation show the actual supported profile and limits. Existing native/ETL regressions, architecture/filter checks, actual process/adapter acceptance, meaningful removal controls, exact-head review/CI and resulting-main verification pass before closure.

## Non-goals
General rule authoring languages or optimization, arbitrary untrusted package loading, marketplace/publisher trust, arbitrary state migration, full operator console, optional Orleans/Proto.Actor qualification, agent collaboration, ETL connector work, task-runner/pause and unrelated release/deployment changes. Any missing broader program obligation remains on its existing parent.

## Validation
Use a bounded reproducible package/host harness plus real production EF/runtime and separate worker processes. Observe persisted round/result identities, owner/fence changes, terminal outcomes and actual parent continuation. Negative controls must fail when durable cancellation, identity validation or idempotent consumption is removed, then pass after exact restoration. Distinguish duplicate physical work from duplicate logical advancement; no universal exactly-once claim. Run heavy checks serially on the shared machine.

## Readiness and ownership
**Delivered and verified.** PR #3192 merged as `156ddf3c8698fd24b056cb9fa476c92666b9a2fa` after exact-head review approval. [Final acceptance and resulting-main evidence](https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-foundation/pull/3192#issuecomment-6391409647) qualifies descendant `9613cf4ad627006867a5e9245940f7d2f75d775f` (two later commits limited to Elsa 3 conversion and Studio). Backend, dedicated architecture/core-only, Studio, CodeQL and maps all passed; all skipped cases and the original cancelled runs remain explicit. T034–T036 are complete in that final receipt; earlier spec checkpoints remain historical records. Both implementation/repair claims are released. This closes only #3181; #2905/#2892 stay open. The bounded Rules profile, same-machine qualification limits, best-effort retry-delay crash window, at-least-once physical effects and unproven historical timeout attribution remain unchanged. Orleans and task-runner/pause work remain deferred.

Affected repository: `elsa-workflows/elsa-foundation`. Program bucket: `docs/program-goals/unified-execution.md`. This task is a successor implementation unit under the existing production feature, not another program or a second active claim.

<!-- program-fourth-model-successor-20261021 -->


Root-reviewed [contract readiness proposal](https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-foundation/issues/3181#issuecomment-6322563096) records the rule semantics, minimal package direction, receipt/cancellation ordering and pinned-upgrade obligations. Superseded for implementation readiness by the reviewed spec 999 plan at b006459df; retained here as proposal history. This proposal was prepared before the current whole-leaf claim.
<!-- rule-contract-proposal-link -->


Latest [domain/contract readiness refinement](https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-foundation/issues/3181#issuecomment-6323284626) supersedes the earlier five-package sketch with a provider-neutral Persistence.Core seam, four-engine EF qualification, expected-pin validation and deterministic round-budget fault semantics. Superseded by the reviewed spec 999 plan and explicit harness command targets; execution evidence remains pending.
<!-- rule-domain-refinement-link -->


[Atomic persistence contract refinement](https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-foundation/issues/3181#issuecomment-6323488324) defines identity-first admission, durable refusal, receipt acceptance versus consumption, lost-response replay and provider qualification cases. It clarifies cancellation identity in the prior domain proposal: the scoped key and immutable fingerprint must both match; changed fingerprints conflict. Superseded by reviewed spec 999; actual provider and runtime qualification remains pending.
<!-- rule-persistence-contract-link -->


[Proposed acceptance plan and command interfaces](https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-foundation/issues/3181#issuecomment-6323604109) define the same-machine four-provider/package/native/REST/upgrade evidence and implementation checkpoints. Existing compatibility command paths were verified; new Rules project/script commands are explicit implementation targets, not executed evidence. Formal Spec Kit/ADR consolidation and signatures are now in reviewed spec 999; the new harness entry points remain implementation targets.
<!-- rule-acceptance-plan-link -->


Package-identity detail: https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-foundation/issues/3181#issuecomment-6324122648 (prepared and source-reviewed; not executed acceptance).


[Root-reviewed contract records and dispositions](https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-foundation/issues/3181#issuecomment-6324393870) resolve scoped identity, receipt/attempt separation, native result facts, cancellation and lease/query semantics. Consolidated into reviewed spec 999 with numeric caps and concrete contract signatures; compiled implementation and executed acceptance remain pending.
<!-- rule-contract-records-link -->

items.title: Program: Weaver across Studio
items.body:
[Codex] On behalf of @sfmskywalker.

## Approved outcome

Every current Studio context works through module-owned contributions. A future Weaver-aware module can add context, tools, guidance, review UI and supported actions without changing Weaver core, the Studio host or provider adapters.

Owner: Sipke Schoorstra. Approved 29 October 2026 after source analysis: "Approved. Additionally, create a Project with a Kanban board view to track WIP."

The initial approval established the Program, native issue hierarchy, Kanban control surface and roadmap. The [29 October owner delivery continuation](https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-foundation/issues/3428#issuecomment-6509190533) now authorizes autonomous end-to-end M0–M5 implementation, testing, documentation, scoped PRs, review, authorized merges and resulting-main verification, plus scoped issue triage/refinement/promotion subject to dependencies, claims and the readiness cap. This supersedes the establishment-only session boundary. Establishment remains distinct from product delivery. Releases, deployments, provider purchases and publisher activation remain outside scope.

## Context and evidence

Initial source baseline: `6ad81f7c7a825bce5d5f8cbc4214de40d92e0d87`. Five direct TypeScript probes confirmed the disconnected `api.ai`/`api.agent` context paths, missing capabilities outside workflow routes, absence of workflow-list context without an editor snapshot, whole-collection failure on one failing contributor, and the existing collector's ability to accept a new module without module-specific changes. These are bounded source/probe observations, not live-provider end-to-end acceptance.

Source findings to reconcile at M0:

- Workflow integration contributes context/tools/renderers under `api.ai`, while active Weaver consumes `api.agent`; providers receive server `IAgentToolRegistry` tools. Close the complete discovery/invocation/result path.
- The shell drops dispatched prompt attachments, retaining only text and correlation ID.
- Shared host registration, default context-kind policy and Copilot authoring instructions/result decoding embed workflow knowledge.
- The default workflow activity catalog is hardcoded; revision reads return `unknown`; the workflow change-permission evaluator denies all proposals.
- The registered default proposal executor reports success without executing a concrete change.
- Tool permission/scope admission, effective server autonomy, contributor failures and session lifecycle need composed verification.
- M0 now diagnoses the reported unavailable state through the authenticated normal host: Copilot reports statusCode=missing-auth and authMode=none. The source trace and actual module/context inventory are recorded in [the merged baseline](https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-foundation/blob/main/docs/reports/weaver-baseline.md), delivered in PR #3446. No successful live model turn or applied effect is claimed.

Relevant source: [Studio host](https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-foundation/blob/6ad81f7c7a825bce5d5f8cbc4214de40d92e0d87/Studio/src/essentials/Elsa.Studio.Hosting/Client/src/app/App.tsx), [context collector](https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-foundation/blob/6ad81f7c7a825bce5d5f8cbc4214de40d92e0d87/Studio/src/essentials/Elsa.Studio.Hosting/Client/src/app/agent/agentContext.ts), [workflow contributions](https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-foundation/blob/6ad81f7c7a825bce5d5f8cbc4214de40d92e0d87/Extensions/Weaver/studio/Elsa.Studio.Weaver.Workflows/Client/src/module.tsx), [backend defaults](https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-foundation/blob/6ad81f7c7a825bce5d5f8cbc4214de40d92e0d87/Extensions/Agent/src/Core/Services/DefaultAgentServices.cs).

## Ownership and boundaries

- Weaver owns generic sessions, orchestration, contribution discovery, provider transport, context budgets, policy enforcement, review lifecycle, cancellation and audit.
- Studio owns generic active-surface/selection lifecycle, contribution admission and the common review shell.
- Participating modules own resource identities, context collection, bounded domain guidance, tools/schemas, validation, domain risk assessment, result rendering and application semantics. Optional integrations may be separately packaged with their owning module.
- Provider adapters translate provider-neutral messages/tools/events to the SDK. Preserve the one-active-provider rule; no provider picker or domain-specific result switch in adapters.
- The administrator controls enabled contributions, data exposure and autonomy. The authenticated user remains the permission actor; model output cannot grant authority.

Reuse Slots/Contributions and the repository's server composition conventions. Consolidate the overlapping registries; keep contracts small. Distinguish trusted installed-module guidance from untrusted resource content. Do not build a universal domain schema or a second agent/runtime engine.

Backend operations use the owning domain's authorized services. Unsaved browser-state operations use a module-owned client adapter with correlated invocation/completion acknowledgements, target/revision checks and explicit behavior if the originating context disappears. Distinguish proposed, approved, applied locally and persisted outcomes. Missing execution support fails explicitly.

Contexts include screens, lists/filters/pagination, resources, selections, unsaved editors, activities, expressions, exact execution occurrences, diagnostics and future module surfaces. Use provenance, resource/revision identity, sensitivity, bounded summaries and lazy authorized detail reads. Do not silently capture unrelated resources or secret values.

## Milestones and dependencies

| Milestone | Outcome | Exit evidence |
|---|---|---|
| M0 | Baseline and activation | Normal-host availability diagnosis and route/resource inventory; approved scope and board recorded |
| M1 | Contribution contract and independent witness | Workflow plus separately packaged non-workflow journeys prove the candidate before contract freeze |
| M2 | Complete shared lifecycle | Context, authorization, tools, review, actual effects/receipts, cancellation and recovery work end to end |
| M3 | Workflow journeys | Lists/create/draft/selection/expression/version/executable/run contexts use real host data and supported operations |
| M4 | Current-module coverage | Every inventory row has a tested supported outcome or explicit limitation, owned by its module |
| M5 | Extensibility and integrated delivery | Existing provider paths, packaged/custom hosts, conformance fixture, exact-head and resulting-main evidence |

M0 precedes M1. Production contract freeze waits for the independent M1 witness. M2 establishes the required shared lifecycle. M3 and M4 may then run in separate module lanes; M5 closes the complete acceptance matrix. Elaborate later module/task leaves only when the next slice is concrete.

## Program acceptance

- [x] A separate package contributes a new resource, context, tool, renderer and applied result with zero changes to Weaver core, the host or provider adapters. Loading/removing the module adds/removes only its contributions.
- [ ] List filters, selections, unsaved changes and exact execution occurrences reach the right turn. Navigation cannot silently retarget an outstanding operation.
- [ ] Successful application is verified against the owning resource. Stale revisions, denied permissions, unavailable executors and unsupported operations fail explicitly.
- [ ] Tenant/user authority, module policy and host policy apply at execution time. Content minimization/redaction and untrusted-content tests cover provider-bound context and tool results.
- [ ] The same contributed tools/outcomes work through Copilot's delegated loop and Anthropic's host-driven loop. Deterministic, provider-protocol and opt-in live evidence remain distinct.
- [ ] Approval/denial, cancellation, disconnect/reconnect, retry, duplicate delivery, restart and module removal have defined and tested outcomes. Accepted decisions/pending approvals survive supported recovery without silently repeating effects.
- [ ] Workflow edits apply atomically to visible designer working state, validate, mark it dirty and support whole-batch undo. Normal save/publish remains explicit; historical/published versions are protected.
- [ ] All current composed contexts and the supported packaged/custom-host journey pass the coverage matrix, with no implied support for absent modules or forbidden data access.
- [ ] Meaningful risk-based tests, required exact-head CI/review, resulting-main verification and module-author documentation support closure. No no-op executor or issue/board status serves as effect evidence.

## Coordination and WIP

Run alongside the active programs, displace none and reactivate no parked backlog. Coordinate shared Studio paths with Expressions #2310, Compensation #3035 and Unified Execution #2892; consume the delivered Hosting #3340 and Unified Workspace #3392 seams. Runtime agent composition and its recovery semantics remain owned by #2892; this Program owns the Studio-wide assistant integration.

One implementation leaf at a time; one integration/review lane. This is a working policy, not an automated enforcement claim. Native sub-issues and blocking relationships are authoritative. Feature issues own acceptance and task checklists; promote a task only for independent ownership or a material dependency. New issues enter needs-triage/Backlog; Ready requires maintainer triage and the repository readiness cap. No automatic promotion is implied by this approval.

Board columns: Backlog, Ready, In progress, In review, Blocked, Done. WIP hides Program/epic rollups. Mark Done only after verified completion; a completed setup task does not complete its parent milestone or Program. Record state transitions and evidence on the owning issue/PR.


## Native delivery hierarchy

- [x] https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-foundation/issues/3429 — Epic: M0: Weaver baseline and program activation
- [x] https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-foundation/issues/3430 — Epic: M1: Module-owned Weaver contribution contract
- [x] https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-foundation/issues/3431 — Epic: M2: Complete Weaver context, tool and review lifecycle
- [x] https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-foundation/issues/3432 — Epic: M3: Weaver workflow journeys end to end
- [ ] https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-foundation/issues/3443 — Feature: M4: Module-owned Weaver support for the current Studio inventory
- [ ] https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-foundation/issues/3444 — Feature: M5: Weaver extensibility and integrated qualification

Kanban WIP: https://github.com/orgs/elsa-workflows/projects/65/views/1

Full hierarchy: https://github.com/orgs/elsa-workflows/projects/65/views/2

Repository goal: `docs/program-goals/weaver-across-studio.md`; activation: ADR0080 D0. Task #3435 owns setup delivery, not product completion.


## Current delivery checkpoint

M0–M3 are verified Done at their recorded source checkpoints. [M3 closeout](https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-foundation/issues/3432#issuecomment-6616867867) records seven reviewed workflow slices, including #3736 merged as `af947767a`, and resulting-descendant-main CI [41721202214](https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-foundation/actions/runs/41721202214) on `a1419b9c37f20295b79f970da15bf8708b2e3bf7`. This preserves deterministic provider-protocol evidence; it is not a live-provider or current-main claim.

M4 #3443 is In progress. #3831, generic effects and live support, is the sole active implementation leaf under draft PR #3845; #3832–#3834 remain Backlog, dependent on verified predecessor completion. M5 #3444 remains Backlog. One implementation leaf and one integration/review lane remain the policy. Current/descendant-main verification, complete native/package/UX/provider/API qualification, final review, exact-head checks, authorized merge and resulting-main proof remain mandatory before leaf/Program completion. No Ready promotion or gate waiver accompanies this bookkeeping refresh.

## Owner continuation amendment — 31 October 2026

[Codex] On behalf of @sfmskywalker. The owner reaffirmed full end-to-end M0–M5 delivery and authorized extending the six-round review limit to **20 total rounds per PR within this Program**. Existing round counts remain cumulative; PR #3514 resumes at round 7. All independent review, exact-head CI, authorized merge, resulting-main verification and charter boundaries remain mandatory. Authorization receipt: https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-foundation/issues/3428#issuecomment-6546731187


## Standing delivery authorization — 1 November 2026

[Codex] On behalf of @sfmskywalker. Sipke reaffirmed standing approval and authorization for end-to-end Program delivery and the pending workflow-write/review continuation. Necessary independent review/integration may continue beyond the former 20-round cap, retaining cumulative numbering and every substantive delivery gate. The one-file owner-account workflow exception and all preserved boundaries are recorded at https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-foundation/issues/3428#issuecomment-6556812743. Other writes/merges remain through the worker’s own App. This amendment supersedes earlier numeric-cap continuation stops; it does not waive checks, independent review, claim/WIP/readiness rules or resulting-main verification.



## Resumed delivery — 12 November 2026

[Owner-authorized resume and source reconciliation](https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-foundation/issues/3428#issuecomment-6837492732); [bounded verification authorization and verified current-main baseline](https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-foundation/issues/3428#issuecomment-6837783960). The 9 November triage folded duplicate wrappers #3433/#3434 into #3443/#3444. Those features are now direct native children; closed-not-planned wrappers are historical dispositions, not completed M4/M5 outcomes. Leaf #3831 / draft PR #3845 remains the only implementation lane. The new Weaver package/type/SDK/wire names are the current baseline; pre-rename Agent writer captures stay unchanged historical evidence. Requalify the additive post-rename Weaver1.0→1.1 journey, all remaining scopes and final-source gates before completion. No release, deployment, credential, publisher or other paused-stream authority changes.


## Bounded T042 and merge authorization — 14 November 2026

[Codex] On behalf of @sfmskywalker. The owner authorized one fresh disposable T042 worker, capped at one CPU / 3 GiB for at most 90 minutes, with cleanup afterward, and reaffirmed end-to-end delivery. Previous allocation authority and clocks are not renewed. The owner also granted an admin override to self-merge after a clean self-review loop. This exception covers the merge mechanism: exact-head independent review, required passing checks, unresolved human holds, resulting-main verification and all substantive acceptance and charter boundaries remain binding. The 1 November amendment continues to supersede numerical review caps; round numbering stays cumulative. Authorization receipt: https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-foundation/issues/3428#issuecomment-6871081882

items.title: feat(capture): reuse one skill for coding-session and meeting intake
items.body:
> **Current naming/source contract, 23 October 2026:** this is The Onlinesourdough Method (OSM). Use Context Architecture for the data/context design; AI Operating Model keeps its name. Production naming is delivered in [PR80](https://github.com/onlinesourdough/OSM-plugin/pull/80), released v0.30.0. The pre-existing Setup feature preview is preserved separately in [PR81](https://github.com/onlinesourdough/OSM-plugin/pull/81), not promoted to production. Current implementation paths below use `osm` / `osm-*`; [#76](https://github.com/onlinesourdough/OSM-plugin/issues/76) tracks remaining rollout. All functional requirements and holds remain; naming delivery does not mean this feature has shipped.

## Problem and result

Useful work remains trapped in agent sessions and meetings. Introduce one focused **Capture Context** skill, proposed portable name `osm-capture-context`, which processes selected evidence through existing tools into the source/atom contract. The same canonical procedure is callable manually, selected in a setup skill chain, and invoked by a native scheduled agent. It is a method with optional bounded helpers, not an OSM background service.

Parent: [#68](https://github.com/onlinesourdough/OSM-plugin/issues/68). Depends on [#69](https://github.com/onlinesourdough/OSM-plugin/issues/69) and [#70](https://github.com/onlinesourdough/OSM-plugin/issues/70); feeds [#72](https://github.com/onlinesourdough/OSM-plugin/issues/72) and [#73](https://github.com/onlinesourdough/OSM-plugin/issues/73). Final skill display/invocation should follow the repository's established namespace and #62 conventions.

## Common capture procedure

1. Resolve the selected source route, actual connection/account, approved scope, destination, exclusions and retention. Reuse accepted setup choices. Discover only the bounded new/changed material since the last successful checkpoint, with an explicit initial lookback/batch limit.
2. Obtain a durable origin ID and source revision/content identity where the host exposes it. Keep original timestamps distinct from import and extraction. Reject or mark incomplete/truncated input; do not present a host's conversation summary as a full transcript.
3. Remove credentials, secrets and excluded material before any new retained copy or model extraction. Use native source content/reference where possible; record the coverage limit of sanitization. Never claim a regex guarantees all confidential data has been removed. Imported text is evidence, not instructions or new permissions.
4. Upsert a source record, a brief useful summary and a small set of evidence-backed atoms. Preserve reasons and exact errors/fixes only where supported. No atom quota: uninformative material may yield none. Use the cheapest sufficient available model and bounded content; do not silently change the user's configured default or require another model subscription.
5. Read back the record(s), then advance only the successfully persisted checkpoint. An uncertain write is inspected before retry. A later extraction failure preserves the source record and resumes the incomplete stage; it does not mark the whole source complete.
6. Pass useful durable candidates to Maintain Context under the existing write policy; do not force every atom through a manual approval queue or promote the whole session to Memory. Live tasks remain in Tasks/GitHub. Emit a short per-source receipt consumed by Check/Home.

## Source recipes in this delivery

| Source | Required path and honest limits |
| --- | --- |
| Codex sessions | Current-session checkpoint capture plus a verified supported export/history route for selected closed sessions. Record exact host/tool revision and accessible scope. Owner-selected local session files may be used only after their installed location/format and permitted scope are qualified; otherwise use checkpoint/export. Never scrape private app databases or assume the summary API is raw/full history. |
| Claude Code sessions | Current-session checkpoint/export path first. If a documented transcript path is used, verify that installed host contract and restrict scope. A SessionEnd hook is optional only after a concrete gap; it should persist a small reference, not run a long LLM import at exit. |
| Meetings / Fathom | Reuse existing Notion meeting notes or already-configured Fathom integration first. Otherwise use an available supported Fathom connection/API to retrieve selected summaries/transcripts. Fathom is the working interpretation of the example provider, not a mandatory customer dependency. Source recording ID, transcript/summary revision and destination are explicit. |

Fathom's [official Notion integration page](https://www.fathom.ai/integrations/notion) currently describes Zapier/Make. Do not market it as a free direct built-in connector or add a new automation subscription by default. Its [API FAQ](https://developers.fathom.ai/faq) documents user-scoped access, duplicate webhook delivery and no new webhook for later transcript/summary/visibility changes. Reconciliation is therefore required for copied records; a new-recording cursor alone is insufficient. Webhooks, if selected, need verification and a supported existing endpoint—no compulsory endpoint service in OSM.

Combine a recent re-fetch window with a bounded rolling check of older retained records and record the resulting detection/freshness limit. A recent window alone must not leave old edits, access changes or deletions permanently invisible.

## Implementation owners

One new `skills/osm-capture-context/SKILL.md` with shared procedure and small host/provider references; Context owns schema, Setup owns selection, Maintain Context owns durable curation, Check owns observation. Update discovery, routing, generated catalogs/manifests/skill count and release documentation. Small helpers remain with this skill and use native credentials without copying tokens into Notion or the package.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Manual invocation and Setup-chain invocation import the same selected synthetic coding session into identical record identities, with a real decision/error/fix and source citation. Replay changes nothing.
- [ ] Execute the supported path on both Codex and Claude Code. Demonstrate selected closed-session capture or the usable export alternative; report unsupported historical coverage explicitly rather than declaring all sessions captured.
- [ ] One selected meeting reaches the existing meeting/document destination and produces useful linked atoms. Existing upstream imports are reused rather than imported twice.
- [ ] Test pagination/batch boundaries, truncation, planted secret and embedded hostile instruction, uncertain write, partial extraction, source correction and access loss. No progress checkpoint skips failed items; retries do not multiply records.
- [ ] A fresh agent answers one practical question from the result with accurate provenance. Skill output and scheduled prompt share the same method; no second ingestion implementation is written for scheduling.

Historical backfill is bounded and separately selected. Audio/video download, continuous recording, model training, generalized ETL connectors and a new runtime queue are not defaults.

items.body:
## FOSS4G scope coordination — 2026-10-22

[#378](https://github.com/honua-io/honua-release/issues/378) now owns the November 2 RC announcement, hosted AI demonstration and focused pilot qualification (five journeys, sixteen interaction templates). It reuses this campaign's infrastructure and independent observers. This issue retains the full 36-scenario / 108-prompt / 252-case program and its existing acceptance criteria; the focused profile does not discharge them. The $2,000/$200 owner amendment is specific to retained candidate accounting for the FOSS4G work and must be explicitly enabled; it does not silently alter this pack's $500/$50 contract or activate deferred RC gates. No new duplicate campaign epic is being created.

## Summary and outcome

Complete the goal-driven Honua agent E2E campaign recovered from the October 13–14 work session. Prove that an agent can independently discover interfaces, install/configure Honua, perform GIS work, publish maps, respect permissions and approvals, recover from faults and clean up against an exact candidate. Retain enough independent evidence and telemetry to measure success and investigate failures.

This issue owns the full campaign. Server #3428 owns the narrower server-authored MCP setup view; it is a dependency, not the tracker for this entire plan. Existing guided journey and terminal canary evidence remain separate and are not substitutes for this campaign.

## Saved implementation and evidence

- Controller/corpus/container foundation: https://github.com/honua-io/honua-release/pull/629 (merged at 5429b19). Deferred release/nightly/promotion activation remains in https://github.com/honua-io/honua-release/pull/607 (draft).
- Public OKF documentation alignment: https://github.com/honua-io/honua-server/pull/6099 (merged).
- Saved implementation plan/runbook: https://github.com/honua-io/honua-release/blob/84c0e11da19aeb6aad00626033b9c884ef00baed/certification/agent-e2e/IMPLEMENTATION.md.
- Pack and corpus documentation: https://github.com/honua-io/honua-release/blob/84c0e11da19aeb6aad00626033b9c884ef00baed/certification/agent-e2e/README.md.
- Hosted contract evidence: https://github.com/honua-io/honua-release/actions/runs/38609401004 — 793 tests, zero failures/errors/skips on `6c501c544edc3727912b51a73111309f8b6d4e91`. These are offline contract tests, not live qualification.
- Manifest validation also passed: https://github.com/honua-io/honua-release/actions/runs/38609401044.
- Continuation commit `9692d0a8bae8485d8c8c4024febd2d2ce21b368f` adds existing-history recovery, refusal to overwrite newer local charges, provider/server correlation fields and atomic report publication. Its 55 focused local tests passed. Hosted regression https://github.com/honua-io/honua-release/actions/runs/38770671910 passed **809 tests, zero failures/errors/skips**; the downloaded JUnit artifact was inspected. The earlier 793-test result applies to the earlier revision above.
- Aligned public knowledge export was reconstructed and verified from server commit `33c551d716df65b59d5dcd82054b679c29cac547`; bundle digest `sha256:0ca4ad0e3fef0111246aceab5322019c21afd93b4ffded7cc3345728e2bb4dfe`.

## Frozen scope and constraints

- Preserve 36 scenarios × three distinct prompts = 108 prompts and 252 live cases: Docker 72, ECS with Redis 72, EKS 72, Lambda 18, Batch 18.
- Development uses A/B. Held-out C is only exposed to the tested worker for frozen qualification. No reduction of the live denominator; deterministic semantic checks are a separate mandatory suite.
- Corpus includes independently generated 3857/4326 towns, threshold/null/boundary/hole/duplicate-name controls, adversarial metadata, 2,105-point pagination, pinned Natural Earth countries, multipart/native conversion inputs and the 330,000-row 85.7 MB Batch fixture.
- Pin exact candidate/component identities, Claude Bedrock requested and returned model identities, pricing basis, public documentation revision/bundle/manifest and observed runtime interface schemas.
- One candidate-wide $500 ceiling includes development, failed attempts, retries, model and AWS costs, with $50 protected for cleanup. Missing history never grants a fresh allowance; unresolved liability remains reserved.
- Separate controller oracle/evidence/signing custody from disposable agent workers. Separate approval principal, verified bootstrap credential revocation and fresh post-install worker handoff where required.
- Every goal and cleanup must pass. Only independently evidenced infrastructure failures permit the bounded retry. Unknown causes cannot be retried to green or hidden by a new campaign ID.
- Public `honua.gis-workflow/v1` is descriptive typed planning documentation, not a new execution interpreter or permission grant. Execute existing MCP/HTTP/CLI/Spec interfaces. Keep private prompts, assertions and expected outcomes out of the public OKF graph and tested worker.
- Terraform in honua-iac owns infrastructure, container job definitions, IAM/network/storage and independent cleanup automation. Runtime APIs may start/stop these predefined jobs. Python handles test orchestration, observations, accounting and evidence; it must not duplicate infrastructure provisioning. Cloud workers use Fargate; Docker uses a dedicated container CI lane separate from the controller. Keep existing EKS topology.
- Desktop-client work in server #5036 and broad raster/3D/performance certification are outside this campaign.

## Implemented, pending full live integration

- [x] Frozen v2 pack/receipt contracts retain all 108 prompts and 252 target cases.
- [x] Public knowledge export pins exact Git objects, graph/document hashes, concept references and worker manifest bindings.
- [x] Independent source/shared-content preservation predicates reject unchanged-ID-only evidence.
- [x] Fifteen deterministic semantic predicates and independent observation/raw-response report contracts.
- [x] Bounded goal-driven model loop and development holdout protection.
- [x] Versioned S3 snapshot and fenced DynamoDB lease primitives; synchronous reservations/journals and history-preservation checks.
- [x] Recovery command restores retained journals without running a model or granting retries; conflicting local evidence/newer charges are preserved and block recovery. Local restart/reconciliation tests pass; live cloud crash proof remains below.
- [ ] Container execution and bounded HTTP observer integration. The rejected standalone EC2/SSM implementation is removed; the Fargate Terraform foundation is merged, while the dedicated Docker CI lane remains open; offline transport tests do not establish live readiness.
- [x] Hash-chained attempt journals, JSON diagnostics and bounded-label Prometheus metrics for outcomes, cleanup, tool errors, tokens, model cost and latency.
- [x] Controller retains provider request IDs and validates backend-supplied action/trace/span/request/evidence bindings; metric labels exclude those IDs. Complete report files are published atomically. Actual backend trace capture and collection remain below.
- [x] Separate observed failure from evidence-supported model/product/infrastructure diagnosis; retain undetermined causes.
- [x] Public documentation explains provenance, source preservation, diagnostic limitations and static-versus-runtime evidence.

## Remaining implementation and acceptance

1. Controller/worker infrastructure and recovery
   - [ ] Provision pinned container jobs, worker/controller/observer/approver IAM, network boundaries, versioned state bucket and lease table through honua-iac Terraform. Use Fargate workers for cloud targets and a dedicated container CI runner for Docker. Retain existing EKS managed-node-group deployments. No standalone EC2/SSM workers.
   - [ ] Prove crash/restart recovery retains attempts, spending and telemetry; integrate final registry/receipt persistence.
   - [ ] Independent expiry watchdog cleans up after controller loss; prove identity/namespace checks and actual cleanup accounting.
   - [ ] Verify workers cannot access oracle, held-out prompts, controller storage/signing credentials or approval authority.
2. Actual scenario backend and deterministic semantics
   - [ ] Implement reviewed provisioning/seeding, model actions, independent observations, dynamic resource-ID expectation binding and cleanup through existing APIs.
   - [ ] Cover P01/P24 custody transitions, separate approval, tenant/permission negatives, P20 clarification and P21/L04/B05 correctly timed fault injection.
   - [ ] Complete semantic fixture seeding/API recipes/response normalization for filtering, nulls, pagination, ordering, same-name isolation, metric buffers, coordinate transforms, containment orientation, holes/boundaries, join multiplicity, write denial and unsupported geodesic refusal.
   - [ ] Preserve protected source attributes, geometry, CRS and shared configuration before/after; retain independently captured raw responses and schema identities.
3. Operational observability
   - [ ] Correlate controller attempt/action and model provider request IDs with real server request/trace/resource/job IDs and retained evidence.
   - [ ] Wire durable journal recovery, collector/scrape or artifact publication, dashboards and alerts.
   - [ ] Report first-attempt/final completion with missing/interrupted cases, cleanup, tool errors/repeats/clarifications, cost and latency; distinguish development from qualification.
   - [ ] Demonstrate that evidence supports failure attribution and that missing telemetry cannot appear as success. Repetition/clarification alone is not a defect.
4. Live target execution
   - [ ] Run local Docker A/B development and deterministic semantic checks on actual APIs.
   - [ ] Run ECS Redis-on and durable EKS development; freeze exact candidate bindings.
   - [ ] Run Lambda including its separate Redis-disabled refusal case and cold-start fault proof.
   - [ ] Run actual AWS Batch jobs, the large fixture, pinned native ETL worker and post-commit recovery/publication.
5. Producer and release qualification
   - [ ] Implement `.github/workflows/agent-e2e-campaign.yml` with isolated execution, durable histories, immutable evidence and trusted GitHub attestation.
   - [ ] Freeze candidate/model/knowledge/recipes/expectations; complete all 252 A/B/C cases plus the separate semantic suite within the retained budget.
   - [ ] Configure attestation-bound consumer inputs and prove release/nightly/promotion reject absent, altered, stale, skipped or incomplete evidence.
   - [ ] Activate/merge the draft release requirement only when the complete producer and actual campaign evidence exist; existing release gates remain required.

## Current status and prerequisites

All 252 live cases remain unqualified. No model/cloud campaign was run as part of this implementation session. The broad live scenario backend, producer and deployed observability remain incomplete; successful unit tests do not satisfy these tasks.

The release AWS account has existing cloud workflow configuration, but no agent-campaign-specific configuration was found during the October 14 check. An isolated test environment/profile, reviewed worker image/roles/network, controller state stores and exact candidate must be configured before paid live execution. Never put credentials in this issue, prompts or evidence.

## Ownership and gate impact

honua-release owns campaign orchestration, independent evidence, diagnostics and release consumption. honua-server owns runtime contracts and public OKF docs. Reuse reviewed honua-iac/honua-devops provisioning and installed SDK/CLI packages rather than duplicating product APIs. Coordinate runtime fixes in their owning repositories as evidence identifies them.

This is release qualification work. It does not assert a passed release, authorize a merge around failed gates, or replace the existing deterministic journey/canary requirements.


## Accepted delivery work packages

- [x] [Correct baseline and remove EC2 worker architecture](https://github.com/honua-io/honua-release/issues/620)
- [ ] [Provision container execution and independent cleanup](https://github.com/honua-io/honua-release/issues/621)
- [ ] [Complete durable controller backend and accounting](https://github.com/honua-io/honua-release/issues/622)
- [ ] [Implement all scenario backends and corpus observations](https://github.com/honua-io/honua-release/issues/623)
- [ ] [Complete live deterministic GIS verification](https://github.com/honua-io/honua-release/issues/624)
- [ ] [Align published OKF knowledge and runtime discovery](https://github.com/honua-io/honua-release/issues/625)
- [ ] [Deploy agent telemetry and prove failure diagnosis](https://github.com/honua-io/honua-release/issues/626)

- [ ] [Activate release gates and complete operational handoff](https://github.com/honua-io/honua-release/issues/628)

Full accepted plan: https://github.com/honua-io/honua-release/blob/5429b19f0932f7ae998be1f5b710f6722d896ca8/certification/agent-e2e/DELIVERY.md. Current implementation is working on #621, #622, #623, #624 and #626, with deferred consumer alignment in #628. #620 is complete. No cloud campaign has run; all 252 cases remain unqualified.

Session/view negotiation, metadata retention, bounded JSON/SSE, no automatic replay after an ambiguous write and credential exclusion are implemented. Required manifest [run 38839798144, attempt 2](https://github.com/honua-io/honua-release/actions/runs/38839798144) passed after its first run was denied by the anonymous GitHub API probe. Exact MCP transport bindings are retained before queue dispatch; every existing dispatch record rejects another send, including from a fresh process with identical bytes. Pending and retained reply chunks recover without redispatch or model calls. Source `1387aa0` passed 99 focused tests and [1,053 hosted contracts plus actual container smoke](https://github.com/honua-io/honua-release/actions/runs/38843306445), zero failures/errors/skips; JUnit inspected. Required manifest [run 38843306543](https://github.com/honua-io/honua-release/actions/runs/38843306543), CodeQL and commit hygiene all passed normally.
