Complete backend routing, observation publication and live crash/cleanup proof remain open.
- Current MCP routing: [#639](https://github.com/honua-io/honua-release/pull/639), source `6a4b8bf`, implements the MCP agent_action backend branch. Dispatch checks retained intent, candidate/case/attempt/mode, pinned knowledge, prepaid reservations, queue configuration and an independently observed running worker. Immutable action-evidence references are committed before public results; fresh-controller recovery cannot replay after a lost publication acknowledgement. Discovery and bounded request/trace correlations feed the journal while raw captures stay private. Source `6a4b8bf` passed 192 focused tests and [1,156 hosted contracts plus actual container smoke](https://github.com/honua-io/honua-release/actions/runs/38849578437), zero failures/errors/skips; downloaded JUnit inspected. [#639](https://github.com/honua-io/honua-release/pull/639) merged at `7b19f9cf2dc3c4f18f5605f632d48fe0b569d40c` after required manifest [run 38849578384](https://github.com/honua-io/honua-release/actions/runs/38849578384), CodeQL and commit hygiene passed normally. Full scenario setup/verify/cleanup, other action handlers, producer, independent server telemetry and live qualification remain open. All 252 live cases remain unqualified; no cloud apply or paid model campaign occurred.
- Deferred release/nightly/promotion activation [#607](https://github.com/honua-io/honua-release/pull/607) remains draft. It must not merge before the complete #627 producer and actual qualification evidence exist.

Cloud preflight still requires the complete shared infrastructure/backend/producer integration and a monitored alert destination. The only SNS topic found in us-east-1 had no subscriptions; a destination has been requested. A configured topic alone is not proof of notification delivery.

**All 252 live cases remain unqualified.** No cloud apply, real secret retrieval, paid model run or qualifying campaign has occurred. Complete scenario setup/verification/faults, deterministic live semantics, credential-custody/revocation proofs, deployed observability, producer and complete live qualification remain open under #621–#628. Offline contract counts, mock-provider tests, policy simulations and fixture container smoke do not reduce that denominator.
Current live semantic integration: [PR #641](https://github.com/honua-io/honua-release/pull/641), source `e7fc807`, adds replayable FeatureServer point normalization and reviewed recipes for strict, inclusive and inclusive-with-null selection. All 108 focused tests pass, including retained real API captures. A separate local PostGIS/Redis/server probe used manifest-pinned server `0e03bdd06b3ca3fb1b82388110bb5dfa19b9f8fa`, amd64 image `sha256:8a211f46bbc92fe6907b72fb8bcdc36a808924f3ca001a090591c0752360d2bd`. All three deterministic query checks passed with before/after source captures. Publication initially returned a disabled layer; an HTTP-200 query carrying protocol 404 was rejected. The enable endpoint required the actual serviceName query parameter (omitting it searches service default). Failed and successful setup/query responses are retained in the regression fixture. Scoped Compose teardown completed with volumes requested for removal; no project containers/network remained, and the temporary credential file was removed.

The converter preserves source attributes/nulls/coordinates/order, rejects incomplete/ambiguous/unsupported responses and requires observed result CRS. It does not normalize polygon topology, pagination or job outputs. Hosted checks are running. This manual local probe is not the dedicated Docker CI lane, complete semantic suite, live cleanup qualification or an agent/model campaign. Setup/custody/cleanup backend integration and the remaining semantic recipes remain open; all 252 agent cases are still unqualified. No cloud apply or paid model call occurred.

items.title: Discover new Django, Wagtail, and Django CMS packages on PyPI via BigQuery (classifier + date range)
items.body:
## Goal

Package discovery. We want to pick up new packages for Django, Wagtail, and Django CMS as they land on PyPI, by searching trove classifiers over either a date range ("everything uploaded in the last 7 days") or the whole index ("everything ever tagged Wagtail", for a one-time backfill of what we are missing).

The classifiers that exist today. Spot-checked against the upstream list at https://github.com/pypa/trove-classifiers/blob/main/src/trove_classifiers/__init__.py on 2026-10-27: of the 68 `Framework ::` entries these three are the only Django-related ones. There is no classifier for Django REST Framework, django-ninja, Channels, or any other Django library, so those are out of scope here.

| Framework | Classifier | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Django | `Framework :: Django`, `Framework :: Django :: X.Y` | the big one |
| Wagtail | `Framework :: Wagtail`, `Framework :: Wagtail :: N` | |
| Django CMS | `Framework :: Django CMS`, `Framework :: Django CMS :: X.Y` | |

Matching on the prefix (`Framework :: Django%`) catches both the bare classifier and every versioned one. A later follow-up could also match `requires_dist` for Django packages whose authors never added a classifier, but that is not this issue.

Two modes:

- **Recent:** `--days 7` (or `--since 2026-10-01`) filtered on `upload_time`. This is the scheduled discovery feed.
- **All:** no date filter, grouped by `name`, so we get one row per project with its first and last upload. This is the backfill, and only needs to run once per framework.

Output is a review list, split into "already tracked" (by matching `Package.pypi_url`) and "new to us", not auto-created packages.

## Why BigQuery

None of the APIs we use today can answer that question:

- pypistats.org only takes a single package name per request. No listing, search, or classifier filter.
- PyPI's JSON API (`/pypi/<name>/json`) gives classifiers per package, not packages per classifier.
- PyPI's web search supports a classifier filter but is HTML only and not meant for scraping.

The public BigQuery dataset `bigquery-public-data.pypi.distribution_metadata` has one row per uploaded file with `name`, `version`, `upload_time`, `classifiers` (array), `requires_dist`, `home_page`, `project_urls`, and more. That makes classifier search a plain query, and `upload_time` gives us the date range for free. The same project also has `bigquery-public-data.pypi.file_downloads`, which is where pypistats gets its numbers, so we could join downloads in the same query if we ever want to.

## Things to look into

- [ ] Rough query for the main case, something like:

  ```sql
  SELECT name, MAX(upload_time) AS last_upload, ANY_VALUE(home_page) AS home_page
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.pypi.distribution_metadata`
  WHERE upload_time >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 7 DAY)
    AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(classifiers) c WHERE c LIKE 'Framework :: Django%')
  GROUP BY name
  ORDER BY last_upload DESC
  ```

  Variants: `Framework :: Wagtail%` and `Framework :: Django CMS%`.

  For the "all" mode drop the `upload_time` filter and add `MIN(upload_time) AS first_upload` so we can see how old a project is.
- [ ] Cost. The metadata table is a few GB, so a query filtered on `upload_time` should sit well inside the 1 TB a month free tier. Confirm by looking at bytes scanned on a dry run, and whether partitioning on `upload_time` is available so the date filter actually prunes.
- [ ] Auth and setup. Needs a Google Cloud project and a service account key. Decide where the key lives (Coolify env var) and whether to use `google-cloud-bigquery` or just the REST API with a short-lived token.
- [ ] Diff against our catalogue. Compare result names with `Package.pypi_url` to split into "already tracked", "tracked but we have it under a different PyPI name", and "new to us". The new ones are the interesting list.
- [ ] Where it runs. Probably a management command like `pypi_discover --framework django --days 7` (frameworks: django, wagtail, django-cms; `--all` for the backfill) plus a weekly scheduled job in `init_scheduled_jobs` that writes the new names somewhere a human can review (an admin page or a GitHub issue) rather than auto-creating packages.
- [ ] Nice to have: join `file_downloads` for the last 30 days so new packages come with a download count attached, which would let us rank the review list.

## Related

- #1804 added Wagtail and Django CMS classifier parsing to the probes.
- Awesome list scanning in `probes.tasks.refresh_awesome_lists` is the other "find packages we do not know about" source.

## Cost estimate

On-demand BigQuery is billed on bytes scanned: $6.25 per TiB, with the first 1 TiB per month free per project. Reading public datasets costs nothing for storage; we only pay for our own queries.

- **Classifier search on `distribution_metadata`:** BigQuery only reads the columns a query touches, so pulling `name`, `upload_time`, `classifiers`, and `home_page` is on the order of a few GB per query, not the whole table. The table is not partitioned by `upload_time`, so the date filter trims the result but not the scan. Daily runs across the three classifiers land somewhere around 100 to 200 GB a month. That stays inside the free tier, so the expected cost is **$0 a month**.
- **Joining `file_downloads` for a 30-day download count:** this is the expensive table. A 30-day aggregate across every project scans hundreds of GB per query. Weekly runs would push past the free tier and cost a few dollars a month; daily runs could reach tens of dollars. We already get last-month downloads from pypistats for free, so either skip the join or look up downloads only for the handful of new names via pypistats after the fact.
- **Guard rail:** set a per-query `maximum_bytes_billed` (say 20 GB) in the client so a bad query fails instead of billing, and run `--dry_run` on any new query to see bytes scanned before scheduling it.

## Setup, if we explore it

1. **Google Cloud project.** Create one (for example `djangopackages-bigquery`) at https://console.cloud.google.com. A billing account is not required for the free tier, but without one BigQuery runs in sandbox mode and queries over the free quota fail rather than bill, which is fine for us.
2. **Enable the API.** APIs & Services, enable "BigQuery API".
3. **Service account.** IAM & Admin, Service Accounts, create `djangopackages-bq`. Grant it the `BigQuery Job User` role on the project. That is enough to run queries against public datasets; it needs no access to any dataset of ours.
4. **Key.** Create a JSON key for the service account. Store the whole JSON in a Coolify env var, for example `GOOGLE_BIGQUERY_CREDENTIALS`, on the djangopackages web app, and load it with `google.oauth2.service_account.Credentials.from_service_account_info(json.loads(...))`. Do not commit it.
5. **Dependency.** Add `google-cloud-bigquery` to `pyproject.toml` and lock.
6. **Smoke test** from the Django shell:

   ```python
   import json, os
   from google.cloud import bigquery
   from google.oauth2 import service_account

   creds = service_account.Credentials.from_service_account_info(
       json.loads(os.environ["GOOGLE_BIGQUERY_CREDENTIALS"])
   )
   client = bigquery.Client(project=creds.project_id, credentials=creds)
   job = client.query(
       """
       SELECT name, MAX(upload_time) AS last_upload
       FROM `bigquery-public-data.pypi.distribution_metadata`
       WHERE upload_time >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 7 DAY)
         AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(classifiers) c WHERE c LIKE 'Framework :: Django%')
       GROUP BY name ORDER BY last_upload DESC
       """,
       job_config=bigquery.QueryJobConfig(maximum_bytes_billed=20 * 1024**3),
   )
   rows = list(job.result())
   print(len(rows), "packages;", job.total_bytes_processed / 1024**3, "GB scanned")
   ```

   The `total_bytes_processed` line is the number to put back here so the cost section above can be replaced with a measured figure.
7. **Local development.** The same env var in `.env.local` works, or `gcloud auth application-default login` and drop the explicit credentials for a laptop run.

items.title: Test wall: etl app unit fills (CRUD + permissions)
items.body:
## Decision Summary

- Surface: the etl app's single endpoint family — the `bigquery-jobs` ModelViewSet (list, retrieve, create, update, partial_update, destroy) plus `ETLPermissions` — first-ever tests (the app has no `tests.py`)
- Lane & seam: backend unit lane, one seam — the authenticated HTTP seam (`APIClient` actors from the #374 harness); no new seams, no permission-class-level unit tests
- Shared-schema deviation (flagged in module docstring): etl is SHARED_APPS-only, so `BigqueryJobs` rows live in the public schema — no `in_workspace(...)`, no `set_schema()`, no `Organization` header anywhere in the module
- Caller classes: superuser (authed actor with `is_superuser` flipped and saved — the #377 idiom, slice-local helper), authenticated non-superuser (plain authed actor), anonymous (bare unauthenticated client)
- Superuser CRUD: six named happy-path specs, one per viewset action, hand-written literal oracles
- Serializer edges: two specs — minimal create (only the two required fields; nullable sync-state fields default null) and missing-required-field create → 400
- Rejections per method: authenticated non-superuser → 403 across all six actions; anonymous → pinned crash quirk across all six actions (parametrization over the action/method is the one accepted deviation from one-named-spec-per-edge — the edge is the same, the action is the parameter)
- Anonymous quirk pinned as-is, not fixed (verified against the running app): `ETLPermissions` dereferences `request.user.is_superuser` unguarded while DRF is configured with `UNAUTHENTICATED_USER: None`, and no `IsAuthenticated` is stacked before it — anonymous requests raise `AttributeError` (HTTP 500 in production, a raised exception at the test-client seam, pinned with `pytest.raises`)
- Hard-delete quirk pinned as-is, not fixed: `BigqueryJobs` sets `_safedelete_policy = HARD_DELETE` even though the viewset docstring says "Soft delete" and the project rule is soft-delete-everywhere — destroy pins 204 + 404-on-retrieve + row absent even from the deleted-inclusive safedelete manager (a read-only oracle; the delete itself goes through the endpoint)
- Data setup: `BigqueryJobs` rows built by a slice-local ORM helper in the spec module — no new shared factories (same call as #377); callers come from the shared `authed_client` fixture / `UserFactory`
- PUT idiom: `update` is driven via the actor's underlying client with `format="json"` — the established integration-suite idiom; no `Actor` harness changes
- Existing tests untouched; zero product-code changes
- Ratchet: the landing PR bumps `coverage_floors/unit` to new measured −0.5–1% (per #368; the repo's ratchet runbook pattern applies); etl is already in `.coveragerc`'s source list, so today it drags the unit number at zero coverage and the fill lifts the measured value

## Problem Statement

The etl app exposes a superuser-gated write API (`bigquery-jobs`) that is alive in production and has zero tests — not even a placeholder `tests.py`. The Django 3.1 → 5.2 upgrade chain (the reason the test wall exists) could silently change its auth handling, permission enforcement, serializer requiredness, or CRUD semantics with CI green, because nothing in any lane exercises this surface. A permission-gated write surface with no coverage is exactly the hole the surface-based bar from #366 exists to catch.

## Solution

A single new unit-lane spec module pins the entire etl API surface at the authenticated HTTP seam: every CRUD action succeeds for a superuser with hand-written literal expectations, every action rejects an authenticated non-superuser, and the anonymous path's real behavior (an unguarded-`None` crash) is pinned as the quirk it is. The two observed product quirks — the anonymous 500 and the hard-delete-despite-soft-delete-docstring — are documented in the module docstring and pinned as-is, never fixed in this PR. The same PR bumps the backend-unit coverage floor per the ratchet rule, locking the gain in.

## User Stories

1. As a maintainer driving the Django upgrade chain, I want every etl endpoint action pinned by a direct test, so that a behavior change in DRF routing, serializers, or permissions during the upgrade turns CI red instead of shipping silently.
2. As a backend developer, I want `ETLPermissions` asserted per method for superuser, non-superuser, and anonymous callers, so that a permission regression on this write surface cannot land unnoticed.
3. As a backend developer, I want the anonymous-caller crash pinned as an explicit quirk spec, so that the current behavior is on the record and any future fix (or accidental change) of the unguarded `request.user` dereference must consciously update a test.
4. As a backend developer, I want the `HARD_DELETE` policy pinned at the destroy action, so that the deviation from the project's soft-delete-everywhere rule is documented and a silent policy change is caught.
5. As a superuser operating the BigQuery sync, I want create/update/patch round-trips pinned with literal field values, so that the sync-state bookkeeping fields (`last_updated_at`, `last_synced_at`, `last_synced_row_id`) keep their optional/nullable contract.
6. As a reviewer of test-wall PRs, I want the etl fill to follow the same one-module, shared-factory, literal-oracle pattern as the plio/entries/users fills, so that the suite stays navigable and consistent.
7. As a maintainer of the coverage ratchet, I want the unit floor bumped in the same PR, so that the coverage gained by the fill can never silently erode.
8. As a future contributor to the etl app, I want the shared-schema deviation and both quirks flagged in the module docstring, so that I don't "fix" pinned behavior or add tenant machinery this app doesn't use.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Zero product-code changes.** The PR adds one spec module and bumps one floor file. Both quirks below are pinned, not fixed; fixing either is future work for its own issue.
- **Modules under test**: the etl app's viewset (a stock DRF `ModelViewSet` over `BigqueryJobs`), its `ModelSerializer`, and `ETLPermissions` (view-level and object-level checks both a bare `return request.user.is_superuser`).
- **Shared-schema placement**: etl appears only in SHARED_APPS, so `bigquery_jobs` is a public-schema table. The module builds rows directly — no `in_workspace(...)`, no `set_schema()`, and no `Organization` header on any request (tenancy is irrelevant to this surface; the table resolves in public regardless). The deviation is flagged in the module docstring, mirroring the #377 users fill.
- **Anonymous crash quirk (verified live)**: DRF is configured with `UNAUTHENTICATED_USER: None`, and the etl viewset's permission list contains only `ETLPermissions` — unlike e.g. the organizations viewset, which stacks `IsAuthenticated` first and therefore 401s guests. An anonymous request reaches `has_permission`, dereferences `None.is_superuser`, and raises `AttributeError` — confirmed as an HTTP 500 against the running dev server, and confirmed distinct from the invalid-Bearer-token path (which an authenticator rejects with 401 before permissions run). At the test-client seam the exception propagates, so the spec pins `pytest.raises(AttributeError)` per action.
- **Hard-delete quirk**: `BigqueryJobs` is a `SafeDeleteModel` with `_safedelete_policy = HARD_DELETE`, while the viewset docstring claims "Soft delete a row". Destroy therefore genuinely removes the row. Pinned as-is.
- **Serializer contract**: `schema` and `table_to_sync` are required (CharFields, not blank, no default); `last_updated_at`, `last_synced_at`, `last_synced_row_id` are `null=True` and therefore optional and nullable through the serializer; `id` is read-only. Minimal create payload is exactly the two required strings.
- **Caller construction**: superuser callers reuse the #377 idiom — an `authed_client()` actor with `is_superuser` flipped and saved — kept as a slice-local helper (promoting it to the shared harness would mean touching the #377 module, and existing tests stay untouched; the duplication is accepted deliberately). Non-superuser callers are plain authed actors; the anonymous caller is a bare unauthenticated API client.
- **Row setup**: a slice-local helper creates `BigqueryJobs` rows through the default ORM manager. No new shared factory — the model is two strings plus three nullables, and no other module needs it.
- **PUT**: the shared actor exposes get/post/patch/delete only; `update` uses the actor's underlying client `put(..., format="json")`, the idiom the integration session-lifecycle journeys already use. The shared harness is not modified.
- **Permission-ordering consequence**: DRF checks view-level permissions before object lookup, so per-method rejection specs for detail routes need no seeded row — the 403/crash is pinned as occurring before any object access.

## Testing Decisions

- **Seam (one, existing, highest)**: the authenticated HTTP seam — real routed requests through the full DRF stack (auth, permissions, serializer, ORM) using the #374 harness's actor fixtures. No new seams: no permission-class unit calls (both `ETLPermissions` methods are single `return` statements with no branches, so superuser detail actions plus the per-method rejections already exercise every line and branch), and no serializer-direct fake-view driving (nothing in this surface needs it).
- **Spec inventory** (one module, unit lane, sibling to the other fills — proposed `tests/test_etl_crud.py`):
  - Six named superuser CRUD specs: list (exact id set of hand-constructed rows, with the set proven non-trivial by construction), retrieve (field-by-field literals), create (201; response echoes the literal payload; independently confirmed by a follow-up retrieve), update via PUT (200; replaced literals), partial_update via PATCH (200; the patched field changed, untouched fields still hold their original literals), destroy (204; subsequent retrieve 404; row absent from the deleted-inclusive safedelete manager — a read-only oracle pinning HARD_DELETE, the delete itself performed only through the endpoint).
  - Two serializer-edge specs: minimal create with only `schema` + `table_to_sync` → 201 with the three sync-state fields null; create missing a required field → 400 naming that field.
  - Two parametrized rejection specs across all six actions: authenticated non-superuser → 403; anonymous → `pytest.raises(AttributeError)` (the pinned crash quirk).
- **Oracle discipline**: every expected value is a hand-written literal from the spec's own constructed payloads/rows — never recomputed through the app's own serializer or queryset. List comparisons are exact id sets including a row the action must not disturb; update/patch specs assert both the changed and the deliberately-unchanged fields so a widened write goes red.
- **Quirk policy**: both quirks (anonymous crash, hard delete) are documented in the module docstring and pinned as-is — a product fix later must consciously flip these specs.
- **Prior art**: the #377 users fill (shared-schema deviation flag, superuser-caller idiom, literal-oracle style, one-module pattern), the integration session-lifecycle journeys (client `put(..., format="json")` idiom), and the legacy organizations suite (which already pins the shared auth stack's guest/invalid-token 401s — deliberately not re-pinned here).
- **Run & ratchet**: suite green locally with the documented unit-lane command (`docker-compose exec web pytest --ignore=tests/integration`) — the binding local-first criterion. The same PR re-measures unit branch coverage and bumps `coverage_floors/unit` (currently 90.96) to new measured −0.5–1%, following the repo's ratchet runbook. Floors only move up.

## Out of Scope

- Fixing the anonymous-caller crash (guarding `request.user` or stacking `IsAuthenticated`) — pinned as a quirk; a product fix is future work worth its own issue.
- Fixing the `HARD_DELETE`-vs-soft-delete-docstring mismatch — pinned as-is.
- The ETL pipelines' business-output correctness beyond API behavior (BigQuery sync logic itself).
- The invalid-Bearer-token 401 path — shared auth-stack behavior, already pinned by the legacy organizations suite.
- The `experiments` and `tags` apps — consciously skipped as abandoned (#366 decision 2, on the record).
- Changes to the shared test harness (`Actor`, fixtures, factories) or to any existing test.
- Integration-lane journeys for etl; any product or schema changes.

## Further Notes

- Sequencing: formally blocked by #374; the real gate is its harness slice, which this fill's branch chain already carries (the work builds on the #377 branch, which builds on the harness).
- The anonymous-500 and invalid-token-401 behaviors were verified empirically against the running dev server during PRD drafting (2026-07-16), not inferred from reading alone.
- The anonymous crash means the acceptance criterion's "anonymous is rejected" is satisfied in the pinned-behavior sense: the request never succeeds, but the observed rejection is a 500-class crash, not a 401/403. The spec records reality; the criterion is met by pinning it.
- `.coveragerc` already lists etl in its source scope, so no coverage-wiring changes are needed — the fill purely raises the measured number.

items.title: tubafrenzy turndown data-finalization (BS side): final-dump one-shot sweeps + preservation

labels.name: tubafrenzy
labels.description: Touches WXYC/tubafrenzy (webhook, legacy mirror, flowsheet ETL, reconcile)

labels.name: status:blocked
labels.description: Cannot start until a dependency closes

labels.name: deadline:tubafrenzy-turndown
labels.description: Hard clock: must land before the 2026-08-31 tubafrenzy turndown

labels.name: sev:med
labels.description: Triage severity: impact under common conditions

items.body:
## Problem

tubafrenzy is decommissioned 2026-09-07 (org Project #36; [WXYC/wiki#86](https://github.com/WXYC/wiki/issues/86) Phase-0 decision log). Several open Backend-Service issues describe data conditions whose *mechanism* dies during turndown (mirror, inbound webhooks, and the flowsheet + rotation ETLs all at **Phase 3** — [wiki#88](https://github.com/WXYC/wiki/issues/88), whose ETL stop is prepped in [#1858](https://github.com/WXYC/Backend-Service/pull/1858); `library-etl` alone at **Phase 3.5** — [wiki#89](https://github.com/WXYC/wiki/issues/89), which is chain-ready-gated with no calendar date, unlike Phase 3's committed 2026-09-07. The three ETLs do **not** stop together, and none of them is gated on Phase 5: [wiki#92](https://github.com/WXYC/wiki/issues/92) is dev/test-infra and script cleanup, not an ETL shutoff) but whose *residue* becomes permanent the moment there is no authoritative upstream to reconcile against. Once MySQL is gone, the only authoritative record of the legacy state is the final `mysqldump` captured at last-write. This ticket is the single consumer of that dump on the Backend-Service side: every one-shot cleanup, repair, and preservation task that keys on it lands here rather than as a standing mechanism nobody will maintain for a pipe with weeks to live.

## Blocked by

Native-blocked on the **final `mysqldump` capture** — a [wiki#86](https://github.com/WXYC/wiki/issues/86) / Phase-6 deliverable, re-captured at last-write (immediately before Phase 6a). Nothing here can run until that artifact exists and is accessible to Backend-Service. The dump is PII-bearing (see item 5) — its storage and access are constrained accordingly.

## Scope — what lands here

1. **Final `mysqldump` dependency (the input).** The capture itself is the wiki#86 / Phase-6 deliverable; this ticket consumes it. It shares its "impossible after 2026-09-07" deadline with the BMI artifact capture in #1500 / #1507 — those should ride the *same* capture pass, so coordinate the dump contents before it is taken. **The capture is now specified in `plans/tubafrenzy-final-dump-capture-spec.md` ([WXYC/wiki#111](https://github.com/WXYC/wiki/pull/111)) — that file is the source of truth for what must survive and how to verify it, and Phase 6b step 2 points at it. The list is no longer maintained here.** In brief, the consumers need `BMI_COMPOSER`, `DJ_HANDLE`, `SIGNON_TIME`, `SIGNOFF_TIME`, and both the `FLOWSHEET_ENTRY_PROD.ID` and `ROTATION_RELEASE.ID` keyspaces. Two corrections the spec carries: (a) `FLOWSHEET_RADIO_SHOW_PROD` has **no `START_TIME`** — a show's start is `SIGNON_TIME` and its end is `SIGNOFF_TIME`; `START_TIME` is a `FLOWSHEET_ENTRY_PROD` column, so item 3 reads the former pair; (b) the risk is not a forgotten column but a wrong script — `backup-database.sh` dumps the whole schema so every column survives by construction, while its neighbour `dump-db-for-index-build.sh` omits `ROTATION_RELEASE` and `COMPANY` even in `all` mode.

2. **Ghost-row one-shot sweep** (absorbs #1083). Flowsheet + rotation `legacy_entry_id` ID-set comparison against the final dump: any BS row whose `legacy_entry_id` is absent from the dump's authoritative keyspace is a ghost from a dropped delete-webhook. Logging-only pass first, then batched DELETEs per [`docs/bulk-update-playbook.md`](https://github.com/WXYC/Backend-Service/blob/main/docs/bulk-update-playbook.md) (async-commit + batch-size + `ANALYZE`-after). Do **not** build the recurring reconcile mechanism #1083 originally proposed — the flowsheet + rotation pipe dies at **Phase 3** ([wiki#88](https://github.com/WXYC/wiki/issues/88)), not Phase 5; a single sweep against the final dump achieves the same cleanup with none of the machinery. Note that from Phase 3 onward the leak is *total*, not merely widened: the inbound webhooks are cut and both ETLs stop in the same phase, so no tubafrenzy-side delete reaches BS at all between the flip and the final dump. (Phase 2 — [wiki#87](https://github.com/WXYC/wiki/issues/87), closed — cut tubafrenzy's *outbound* LML calls only and explicitly left the webhooks pushing.) So the sweep must run against the dump, not against a mid-turndown snapshot.

3. **Stub-show `start_time` repair** (absorbs #1084). One-shot `UPDATE wxyc_schema.shows SET start_time = <dump value> WHERE start_time IS DISTINCT FROM <dump value>` for rows created as `/internal` webhook stubs (which persisted `start_time = NOW()`). Consumers (dj-site, iOS V2, archive, semantic-index) read these times, so the wrong values are user-visible and permanent post-turndown. The one-line ETL conflict-set fix #1084 also proposed is redundant given this sweep repairs every stub at once — skip it.

4. **`BMI_COMPOSER` historical source** (feeds #1500). #1499 shipped the composer worker forward-only, so every pre-2026-06-29 flowsheet row has `composer = NULL`. The dump's `BMI_COMPOSER` column is the *only* historical source of the hand-typed composer credits the BMI performance list needs. Preserve the column in the capture; the backfill decision (whether and how to populate `flowsheet.composer` from it) is made in #1500, not here — this ticket only guarantees the source survives.

5. **PII constraint on the dump** (absorbs #1400's surviving contract; **rule corrected 2026-08-27 — [WXYC/wiki#123](https://github.com/WXYC/wiki/issues/123)**). The dump carries DJs' real names in **two** columns: `DJ_NAME` by design, and `DJ_HANDLE` by defect across the whole 22-year corpus (measured: 5,373 of 72,778 shows hold a `DJ_HANDLE` equal to that row's `DJ_NAME`). This item previously stated the rule as "import reads `DJ_HANDLE`, never `DJ_NAME`" — that directed imports at a contaminated column and is withdrawn. The binding rule lives in the capture spec's **PII rule** section ([`plans/tubafrenzy-final-dump-capture-spec.md`](https://github.com/WXYC/wiki/blob/main/plans/tubafrenzy-final-dump-capture-spec.md), amended 2026-08-27): restricted storage (`s3://wxyc-archive/` only, never copied to laptops/drives/tickets/repos), and **no import path passes either column through unfiltered** — any value destined for `shows.legacy_dj_name` or another public-reaching surface is re-resolved through the canonical `resolveDjDisplayName` policy or scrubbed to an equivalent standard; the rule is a filter, not a column choice. `wxyc-crm`'s alumni extract legitimately reads real names and is out of the rule's scope. The `shows.legacy_dj_name` → `legacy_dj_handle` rename #1400 floated is a separate Phase-7 schema-cleanup item, not part of this ticket.

## End state

- Ghost flowsheet + rotation rows deleted (with a pre-DELETE log of what was removed).
- `shows.start_time` corrected for every webhook-stub show to its authoritative tubafrenzy value.
- `BMI_COMPOSER` preserved in the retained dump and confirmed available to #1500.
- PII handling rule for the dump documented and, where importable, enforced.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Final dump captured per [the capture spec](https://github.com/WXYC/wiki/pull/111) (wiki#86 / Phase 6b step 2), its schema-verification output recorded in the Phase 0 decision log, and accessible to BS with `BMI_COMPOSER`, `DJ_HANDLE`, `SIGNON_TIME`, `SIGNOFF_TIME`, and both the `FLOWSHEET_ENTRY_PROD.ID` and `ROTATION_RELEASE.ID` keyspaces intact.
- [ ] Ghost-row sweep run: log-only diff reviewed, then batched DELETEs executed per the bulk-update playbook, with row counts recorded on this issue.
- [ ] `shows.start_time` repair run: count of rows corrected recorded.
- [ ] #1500 confirms `BMI_COMPOSER` is available as its historical source.
- [ ] Dump PII handling rule recorded per the capture spec's PII rule (amended 2026-08-27, wiki#123); any import path (if built) filters **both** `DJ_NAME` and `DJ_HANDLE` through the canonical `resolveDjDisplayName` policy — neither column is passed through unfiltered.

## Related

- Consolidates the final-dump-keyed residue from #1083 (ghost rows) and #1084 (stub start_times), wired as sub-issues.
- Preservation dependency for #1500 / #1507 (BMI capture rides the same dump pass).
- Carries the surviving PII contract from #1400.
- Turndown decision log: [wiki#86](https://github.com/WXYC/wiki/issues/86); org Project #36 (Tubafrenzy decommissioning).



---

_Milestone 1 moved from 2026-08-31 to **2026-09-07** on 2026-08-28 — 24 scheduled DJs still lack a usable Backend account and the classic flowsheet UI is their only surface. Engineering readiness was not the gate. See [WXYC/wiki#125](https://github.com/WXYC/wiki/issues/125)._

items.title: census(spec): how many bare-path citations in `packages/spec/src/**` docblocks name a file that exists NOWHERE in the tree — the 2,635-span axis the gate pins and deliberately declines

labels.name: domain:spec
labels.description: Domain lane — seat card indexed by label:pm:seat

items.body:
Filed by the 分诊 seat while grading **#17578**, which is this card's one confirmed member. ⛔ **Unassigned; this is the census, ⛔ not a gate and ⛔ not a cleanup.**

## The question

`packages/spec/src/**` comment prose cites in-repo files as **bare path code spans** — a filename or package-relative path with **no line number** (`component-props-union-arm.test.ts`, `contracts/realtime-service.ts`). Those spans are deliberately unjudged by the existing gate.

**How many of them name a file that exists nowhere in the tree?**

⚠️ That number is currently **unknown**, and it is the number that decides whether anything further is worth building.

## Why it is not already answered

`scripts/check-spec-docblock-symbol-anchors.mjs` measures and pins the axis, then declines it on purpose (measured on `origin/main` @ `abc4b83ce8b01d4e5af3560a0547421f6f5ca98f`, 2026-09-11T00:5xZ):

```
barePathSpans:              2635
barePathsTrackedAtRepoRoot:  346
:87  "judging every bare path code span here produces **2,290** findings"
     ⇒ registered with `checkBarePaths: false`
```

⭐ **The scope call is correct and this card does not reopen it.** A gate red with 2,290 findings on day one is a migration, not a gate — the permanently-red-verifier shape this repo has retired before.

⚠️ But **2,290 is "unbindable", ⛔ not "wrong".** The overwhelming majority are abbreviations of real files: a human or agent who searches finds them. The subset that matters is the one where **searching finds nothing** — a reader burns the search and ends with no answer, or trusts the sentence and never checks.

⇒ unbindable ≠ dead. **The dead subset has never been counted.**

## Scope — one number, then stop

1. For every bare path code span in `packages/spec/src/**` comment prose, ask the cheap question the existing gate does not: does a file with that basename exist anywhere in `git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/main`? ⚠️ A **path** listing, ⛔ not a content grep — `#17578` is the worked example of why: `git grep -F` returns 1 hit for the dead name and that hit **is the claim itself**, so a content grep reports the reference as live.
2. Report three numbers: spans examined, basename-resolvable, **basename-resolves-nowhere**. Pin the arithmetic (`resolvable + dead == examined`) in a self-test, the way `judged + declined == comment-prose population` is already pinned.
3. List the dead ones with their sites.
4. ⛔ **Stop there.** Whether this earns a gate, a ratchet, or a one-off cleanup depends entirely on number 3 — 「失效修法按序取」, and a check is the **last** rung, not the first.

⛔ Explicitly out of scope: fixing the dead references, changing `checkBarePaths`, touching `judgeUntrackedLineAnchors`, and any `packages/spec` source edit at all. This card produces a **measurement**.

## The seed, and its shape

**#17578** (closed `not_planned` — three classes out as a standalone prose defect, and reopening is free if this census says otherwise): `packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts:1179` says

> `` `component-props-union-arm.test.ts` pins it from this side. ``

```
git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/main | grep -c 'component-props-union-arm'  → 0
git grep -n -F 'component-props-union-arm' origin/main                        → 1  (the claim itself)
lit controls, same corpus:  state-machine.test.ts ✓   view-union-diagnostics.test.ts ✓
```

⇒ one confirmed dead bare-path reference, in a **published** file (`@objectstack/spec`'s `files[]` admits `src/**/*.zod.ts`), pointing at a guard that does not exist.

## Dedupe

Run against the 582-issue open `objectstack` board, 2026-09-11T00:5xZ.

- **#17242** — *"183 `packages/spec/src/**` citations name no tracked file"*. ⛔ **Not a duplicate, and the distinction is the whole point:** #17242 is the residual of the **line-citation** axis (`file.ts:NNN`, 183 of 189 declined by `judgeUntrackedLineAnchors: false`). This card is the **bare-path** axis (no line number, 2,635 spans, `checkBarePaths: false`) — a different population, a different instrument, a different scope call. A pointer comment is going onto #17242 so the two axes are visible from either side.
- **#15809** / **#16960** / **#17065** — the line-citation lineage, same family, all on that other axis.
- **#17512** — issue-number citations that 404. Different corpus (issue numbers, not paths).
- Controls: `docblock` returns **78** open cards on this board, `ADR-0112` returns 18 ⇒ the scan discriminates and the near-misses above are readings.

## What this card does NOT claim

- ⛔ No claim that the dead count is large. It could be **1** — in which case the answer is "close this, #17578 was the whole population" and that is a **good** outcome, cheaply bought.
- ⛔ No claim that `checkBarePaths: false` is wrong. It is right, and stays right whatever this measures.
- ⛔ No claim about other packages. `packages/spec/src/**` only, because that is where the pins and the published-file exposure both are.

**Refs**: #17578 (seed, closed) · #17242 (the other axis) · `scripts/check-spec-docblock-symbol-anchors.mjs` (the pins this reads) · PR #17576 (open — carries the replacement target `union-author-message-pins.test.ts`, which does **not** exist on main yet)

items.title: [Epic] Integration platform — public API, webhooks, OAuth apps, and automation ecosystem
items.body:
## Outcome

Make Connex a reliable system in a customer's broader stack by providing a versioned public API, authenticated outbound webhooks, secure inbound app connections, observable sync infrastructure, and first-class integrations with automation and collaboration tools.

## Why this needs a platform epic

Email/calendar, e-signature, marketing channels, accounting, enrichment, partner portals, and customer-success tools all require the same foundations: external identities, encrypted credentials, event delivery, idempotency, rate limits, retries, permissions, audit, and tenant-safe data contracts. Build those once rather than embedding bespoke connector logic in each feature.

## Product principles

- **API-first domain contracts.** Public behavior is versioned and documented; integrations do not depend on private frontend endpoints.
- **Least privilege.** Apps receive explicit organization/workspace scopes and granular permissions.
- **Reliable delivery.** Every event and mutation has stable identifiers, idempotency semantics, retries, and observability.
- **No cross-tenant shortcuts.** External IDs, secrets, queues, caches, logs, and retry workers remain tenant-scoped.
- **Connector SDK over marketplace theater.** Prove a small set of excellent integrations before building a large catalog UI.

## Workstreams

### 1. Public API program

- Versioned REST API for companies, contacts, employment, deals, pipelines/stages, products/line items, tasks, activities, notes, files/metadata, tags, custom fields, users/teams, leads, campaigns, and reports as those domains exist.
- Cursor pagination, filtering/sorting, sparse fields/expansion limits, bulk endpoints, optimistic concurrency/versioning, and consistent error envelopes.
- OpenAPI specification generated/validated against implementation, examples in EN/JA where useful, and an interactive developer portal.
- Explicit compatibility and deprecation policy.

### 2. Authentication and app model

- Personal access tokens only as a tightly scoped development/admin tool.
- Organization-installed OAuth apps/service accounts for production integrations.
- Granular scopes mapped to existing RBAC permissions plus organization/workspace installation boundaries.
- Secret storage, rotation, expiry, revocation, step-up administration, and metadata-only audit.
- Installation review showing requested permissions and data access.

### 3. Outbound webhooks

- Versioned event catalog for record changes and high-value lifecycle transitions.
- Signed payloads, timestamp/replay protection, stable event/delivery IDs, idempotent consumer guidance, configurable destinations, and test delivery.
- At-least-once delivery with exponential backoff, bounded retention, dead-letter state, manual replay, pause on repeated failure, and per-endpoint health.
- Payload minimization and optional fetch-by-ID pattern for sensitive/large records.

### 4. Inbound sync framework

- Connector-owned external IDs and source metadata with uniqueness guarantees.
- Idempotent upsert, delete/tombstone policy, cursor/checkpoint storage, sync runs, per-record failures, retry/reconciliation, and conflict strategy.
- Reuse duplicate-preflight/merge rather than allowing each connector to create parallel records.
- Background-job limits, provider quotas, and tenant-fair scheduling.

### 5. Initial ecosystem integrations

- Automation: Zapier and/or Make using the public API/webhook contracts.
- Collaboration: Slack and Microsoft Teams notifications/actions.
- Commercial documents: one e-signature provider for #558.
- Accounting/finance: validate demand before choosing providers and define whether Connex is source of truth or a downstream consumer.
- Import/migration connectors from common CRMs only after mapping, provenance, and reconciliation are safe.

### 6. Administration and observability

- Installed-app inventory, owner, scopes, workspace reach, last use, health, recent failures, credential expiry, and revoke controls.
- Per-app/API/webhook quotas, rate limits, usage reports, and abuse detection.
- Support-safe diagnostics that exclude secrets and unnecessary CRM content.
- Organization-wide policy for which app categories/providers are allowed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A third-party developer can authenticate, discover a versioned contract, and safely perform supported CRUD/query workflows without private endpoints.
- [ ] OAuth/service-account scopes enforce existing tenant and RBAC boundaries.
- [ ] Webhooks are signed, replay-resistant, retryable, observable, and manually replayable.
- [ ] Inbound connectors support idempotent upsert, reconciliation, duplicate prevention, and per-record error recovery.
- [ ] Revoking an app/credential immediately blocks future access and scheduled work.
- [ ] API/webhook versioning and deprecation policy are documented and tested.
- [ ] Rate limits prevent one app/tenant from starving others.
- [ ] Audit and diagnostics never expose tokens, credentials, or uncontrolled payload content.
- [ ] Security, SSRF/egress, tenant-isolation, concurrency, replay, deletion, and failure-injection tests are complete.

## Related foundations

#54 · #60 · #87 · #103 · #313 · #368 · #419 · #558 · #560
