items.title: Indexable RLS org policies (tx + ref tables) with prerelease soak
items.body:
## Problem

Every org-scoped read on transactional tables (`individual`, `encounter`, `program_encounter`, `program_enrolment`, …) full-sequential-scans the **entire cross-org table** regardless of how small the querying org is. On prerelease, a concept-filter for an org with only **29,411** rows still scanned all **~1.8M** rows and took **~10s**. This is very likely a major contributor to the May 2026 API response-time regression.

## Root cause

The RLS `USING` clause on transactional tables (generated by `enable_rls_on_tx_table` in `V1_142.2__CreateNewRLSForAccount.sql`) is:

```
organisation_id = (select id from organisation where db_user = current_user)
OR organisation_id IN (SELECT organisation_id from organisation_group_organisation)
```

The `OR` combined with a hashed subplan is **not index-pushable**, so the planner ignores the existing `organisation_id` btree (`individual_organisation_id__index`, `idx_individual_org_date_of_birth`, …) and does a `Parallel Seq Scan` of the whole table. Adding a flat, standalone `organisation_id = <id>` predicate flips the plan to a `Bitmap Index Scan`:

- 29,411-row org (`ashwini`): RLS-only → `Parallel Seq Scan` of 1.8M rows, **~10s**.
- Same query + explicit `organisation_id = N` → `Bitmap Index Scan`, **24.7ms warm**.

This is an access-path problem in the RLS layer — not a missing data index — and it affects **all** org-scoped reads, not just one endpoint.

## Why not a content index / LEAKPROOF

Indexing `observations` (GIN + `jsonb @>`) does **not** help: under RLS, jsonb operators are non-leakproof, so Postgres won't evaluate any content predicate (and therefore won't use a content index) below the security barrier. Marking `jsonb_contains` `LEAKPROOF` was explicitly rejected — it would let a tenant's attacker-controlled `@>` probe run pre-RLS over other orgs' rows, i.e. a **cross-tenant existence/count oracle on sensitive observation data** via the tenant-facing API.

## Already mitigated (partial) — #1005

#1005 injects an explicit `organisation_id = <current org>` predicate (`CHSRepository.inCurrentOrganisation()`) into four external-API list endpoints — `/api/subjects`, `/api/encounters`, `/api/programEncounters`, `/api/programEnrolments` — so the planner uses the org btree there. That is a targeted patch on those code paths only; RLS remains the security backstop. Every other org-scoped query (sync, web, reporting, internal) still hits the full scan.

_Uncovered while dev-testing #1005 against the prerelease DB._

---

## Story (Release 17.0)

**Spec:** `avni-product-ops/analysis/rls-indexable-org-policy/` (analysis + spec + validated experiment scripts)

**As an** integration consumer (e.g. Goonj Salesforce, Ashwini Bahmni) and **as a** field worker syncing data, **I need** org-scoped queries to be served via the `organisation_id` index instead of full cross-org table scans, **so that** API and sync latency is bounded by my org's data size and no longer spikes to 50 s – 2 m under prod load — with reference-data visibility (own org + ancestors + org-group members) preserved exactly.

### Acceptance Criteria

**Functions + policy helpers (one Flyway migration):**
- [ ] Migration creates `public.rls_visible_org_ids()` — `STABLE`, `SECURITY INVOKER`, `RETURNS integer[]`, body: `{SELECT id FROM organisation WHERE db_user = current_user} UNION {SELECT organisation_id FROM organisation_group_organisation}` (exact validated definition in the validation comment on this issue).
- [ ] Migration creates `public.rls_visible_org_ids_with_ancestors()` — same shape: `{recursive parent chain from own org (the org_ids view logic)} ∪ {organisation_group_organisation members}`.
- [ ] `enable_rls_on_tx_table(text)` updated (CREATE OR REPLACE in the same migration) to emit `USING (organisation_id = ANY (public.rls_visible_org_ids()))`; `WITH CHECK` unchanged (`organisation_id = (select id from organisation where db_user = current_user)`).
- [ ] `enable_rls_on_ref_table(text)` updated to emit `USING (organisation_id = ANY (public.rls_visible_org_ids_with_ancestors()))`; `WITH CHECK` unchanged.

**Re-application across all RLS tables:**
- [ ] The migration re-applies `enable_rls_on_tx_table` to every table currently carrying a tx-shaped policy (enumerate from `pg_policies` at authoring time — `individual`, `encounter`, `program_encounter`, `program_enrolment`, `checklist*`, `individual_relationship`, `group_subject`, `subject_migration`, `attendance_record`, `session`, …).
- [ ] Likewise `enable_rls_on_ref_table` for every ref-shaped policy table (`concept`, `concept_answer`, `form*`, `address_level*`, `encounter_type`, `subject_type`, `program`, `translation`, `organisation_config`, …).
- [ ] Migration begins with `SET lock_timeout = '10s';` so a blocked `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` fails the migration fast instead of queueing the cluster.
- [ ] All SQL is schema-qualified (`public.`) — no reliance on `search_path`.

**Equivalence + plan verification (on a migrated DB):**
- [ ] Tx equivalence: for a single-org role and an org-group role, `count(*)` and per-org breakdown on `public.individual` are identical before/after (the validated check on this issue).
- [ ] Ref equivalence: for a child org with a parent (ancestor visibility), an org-group admin, and a plain org — `count(*)` per representative ref table identical before/after.
- [ ] `EXPLAIN` of an org-scoped query **without any app-side org predicate** shows `Index Cond: (organisation_id = ANY (rls_visible_org_ids()))` (Bitmap or Index Only Scan), not a seq scan.
- [ ] `make test_server` green (integration tests exercise RLS semantics throughout).

**Prerelease soak (gates prod rollout):**
- [ ] Migration applied to prerelease early in the 17.0 cycle; applied-state verified (`pg_policies` shows `= ANY(...)` quals on all tx/ref tables; both functions present).
- [ ] Scripted equivalence checks pass post-deploy (single-org, org-group, parent/child — scripts under `avni-product-ops/analysis/rls-indexable-org-policy/`).
- [ ] The four #1005 endpoints re-tested **with the app-side predicates removed locally / ignored** (psql `EXPLAIN` without predicate): index plans confirmed end-to-end on the migrated DB.
- [ ] Integration latency observed over the soak window (Goonj + Ashwini request logs): bounded tails, no correctness reports.
- [ ] Soak exit criteria defined and met (proposal: ≥3 weeks on prerelease incl. at least one ETL full run and one client sync cycle per major org, zero RLS-attributable defects) — recorded on this issue for the prod go/no-go.
- [ ] Prod apply checklist written: deploy window, no-ETL guard, `lock_timeout` behaviour on failure (Flyway retry), rollback note (re-run old `enable_rls_*` definitions from V1_142.2 — also catalog-only, seconds).

### Technical Details
- Current definitions: `V1_142.2__CreateNewRLSForAccount.sql` (functions), policies enforced verbatim on prod & prerelease (verified 2026-06-04 — environments identical except an out-of-band `rule_database_access_log` table on prerelease).
- The validated function + policy SQL and the reversible test method (single-table swap inside `BEGIN…ROLLBACK`) are in this issue's validation comment; reuse verbatim.
- `STABLE` is load-bearing: planner evaluates the function at plan time → accurate estimates (29,235 est vs 29,411 actual in validation). `VOLATILE` would force per-row evaluation; `IMMUTABLE` is incorrect (depends on `current_user` + data).
- Group-admin semantics: a group db_user (e.g. `utthaan`) has no `organisation` row — its visibility comes entirely from the `organisation_group_organisation` arm. The tx function handles this (first arm empty).
- The ancestor chain mirrors the `org_ids` view (`WITH RECURSIVE list_of_orgs … WHERE o.id = log.parent_organisation_id` — child sees parents). Either reuse the view inside the function or inline the recursive CTE; keep `SECURITY INVOKER`.
- Ref tables are small — that half is about **consistency and safety**, not performance; the perf-critical path is the tx tables.
- No new indexes needed: `organisation_id` btrees exist on all tx tables (`V1_93_5` era; `individual_organisation_id__index`, `idx_individual_org_date_of_birth`, …).
- Catalog-only DDL: no data scans, no index builds — runs in seconds, effective at commit.

### Testing Gotchas
- **`"$user"` search_path trap:** under `SET ROLE <org>`, unqualified `individual` resolves to the org's ETL schema (`ashwini.individual` — flattened, no `observations` column, but same row count → silently wrong test results). Schema-qualify `public.` in every verification query.
- Baseline (old-policy) verification counts seq-scan (~10 s cold on `individual`) — expected; capture baselines *before* applying the migration.
- The migration takes brief `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` locks per table within one Flyway transaction — run with the app stopped (normal deploy) and no direct-DB ETL/analytics in flight; `lock_timeout` is the backstop.
- Ancestor visibility is only exercised by orgs that have `parent_organisation_id` set — pick a real parent/child pair on prerelease for the equivalence check (don't assume the test org has one).
- `organisation` table itself has a distinct policy (`organisation_policy`, includes the `openchs`/`openchs_impl` special case) — **out of scope**; don't re-apply helpers to it. `users` table RLS (V1_144) is also distinct — out of scope.
- Policies replicate to the prod read replica via WAL — analytics/Metabase queries get the same plan change; no separate action, but worth knowing when comparing replica query times.
- Prerelease is idle — it cannot reproduce prod's cache-pressure benefit; the soak validates **correctness**, while the perf claim rests on the plan shape + buffer footprint (already measured). Don't over-read idle latency numbers (HTTP floor dominates warm requests).

### Out of scope
- No `LEAKPROOF` changes to any jsonb operator (rejected above — cross-tenant-oracle risk).
- No content (GIN/expression) indexes on `observations` (inert under RLS).
- `organisation` and `users` table policies (distinct, untouched).

---

## Follow-up (not part of this story — post-soak decision)

**Remove #1005's redundant app-side org predicates.** The `.and(inCurrentOrganisation())` predicates added in 16.15 (`e84e6af1d`) become harmless duplicates of the new policy qual (planner dedups the condition). Recommend keeping them through the first prod release of 17.0 as belt-and-suspenders, then deciding removal in a later minor (`IndividualRepository.findSubjects`, `EncounterRepository.findByConcepts*` ×3, `ProgramEncounterRepository.search`, `ProgramEnrolmentRepository.search`). **Sequencing constraint:** removal must never precede the policy migration in any environment — new app code against an un-migrated DB would regress to full scans. Record the decision on this issue when taken.

items.title: Splunk event shape: the per-app snapshot stream, the inventory_id bridge, and what v0 must freeze

labels.name: v0-blocker
labels.description: V0 contract item that other V0 work depends on

items.body:
## Why now

The 2026-08-24 end-to-end test (PR #80 build → Jamf Cloud → outbox → HEC → `index=main`) proved the transport and exposed the gap: the delivery-time shaping designed in docs/splunk-event-shaping.md is unbuilt. What lands in Splunk today is the raw canonical delta wrapped in `{"event": ...}` — nested arrays, `spath`/`mvexpand` hostile, indexed at delivery time instead of the event's own time. The event shape is the product's contract and freezes the moment customer SPL is written against it, so the shape itself is the v0 blocker; enrichment payloads are additive later precisely because the shape reserves their keys.

## Rulings (Kyle, 2026-08-24 design session)

1. **Snapshot stream, per app.** Every device sync emits one HEC event per installed application, `sourcetype=jamf:mac:app`. The application object is what Jamf provided, 100% untouched.
2. **Casing law.** Jamf-sourced fields keep Jamf's casing exactly; LoonInspect-minted fields are `snake_case` (`inventory_id`, `short_date`). Fidelity to the source is the naming convention.
3. **`device_meta` as its own key.** Pre-generated once per device sync, duplicated onto every sub-event. Example fields (list not final): `inventory_id`, `hostname`, `serialNumber`, `assignedUser`. The configurable-with-hard-size-cap requirement from the shaping doc stands.
4. **`inventory_id` is the bridge.** A UUID4 minted **per device per sync pass** at the ingest choke point, stamped on every sub-event of that pull across all sourcetypes — `index=x inventory_id=<uuid>` reconstructs the device; dashboards jump Groups ↔ Apps on one token. `jobId` nests above it (one run → many inventory_ids). Delivery retries reuse the same id.
5. **Reserved enrichment keys, current state only.** `patching{}` and `vulnerabilities{}` on the app event carry what IS true about that build. (`alerts{}` is parked — undefined keys don't ship.)
6. **Changes are their own sourcetypes, not inline.** Inline keys describe what IS; sourcetypes describe what HAPPENED. Change events fan out as `jamf:mac:app:change` (and siblings per entity), carrying the policy's `level` as a first-class field for saved-search alerting, `_time` at the observation window, and the new observation's `inventory_id`.
7. **Sourcetype tree is the routing dimension.** `jamf:mac:app` extends to `jamf:mac:app:vuln`, `jamf:mac:app:change`; device anchor and group-membership streams follow the same pattern.
8. **Envelope.** `time` (epoch, from the event's own timestamp per app.core.runs.event_time — never index time), `host` = device hostname, `sourcetype` per event.

Reference shape:

```json
{
  "event": {
    "application": { "...Jamf's app record, untouched..." : "..." },
    "patching": {},
    "vulnerabilities": {},
    "device_meta": {
      "inventory_id": "<uuid4-per-device-per-sync>",
      "hostname": "...",
      "serialNumber": "...",
      "assignedUser": "..."
    }
  },
  "sourcetype": "jamf:mac:app",
  "time": 1756049903
}
```

## v0 blockers — the shape, nothing else

- [ ] A canonical **per-device snapshot event** enqueued each sync (the delta event survives for generic webhooks and change derivation) — the shaping doc's "expand the delta" conclusion cannot produce a snapshot stream and is superseded on this point.
- [ ] **HEC expansion** in/adjacent to `_build_body()`: snapshot event → N per-app events + device anchor, `device_meta` + `inventory_id` stamped on each. Splunk-destination-scoped; other destination types keep the canonical event.
- [ ] **Envelope `time` + `host`** on every HEC event (subsumes the standalone \_time finding from the e2e).
- [ ] **Changes as `:change` sourcetypes** with `level`, window `_time`, `inventory_id`.
- [ ] **Naming conformance pass** against the casing law (today's wire event mixes camelCase meta with snake_case top level).

## Open rulings blocking the above (Kyle)

- **Which Jamf is "what Jamf provides"** — v4's camelCase as sent today, or the Classic-era names migrating add-on SPL was written against. Freezes with the first customer search.
- **Where the raw app record rides** — fattened snapshot payload at enqueue time (cache-don't-calculate) vs. delivery-time join to the observation ledger.
- Final `device_meta` field list (incl. where `short_date` and `jobId` live); empty `{}` vs omitted keys for disabled features.

## Explicitly not v0

- `vulnerabilities{}` population — blocked on the LoonVD/api.loonsec.io lookup feed; the Wireshark fixture work designs the shape and the Global-API wire contract in parallel.
- `patching{}` population — data already exists per app row (#65/#67); additive fast-follow.
- HEC request batching; configurable `device_meta` surface (size cap noted above).

Implementation splits into focused per-session issues off this one; this issue is the contract record and tracking list.

**Specification blocked: decision required.** Publication does not authorize PM implementation. Implementation remains held.

Existing milestone: M12 — Package, upgrade and rehearse recovery (number 13); actual assignment must be read back at publication.

## Outcome

Produce correlated traces/metrics/redacted audit plus signed/checksummed release pairing, notices and truthful connector evidence; release version requires explicit decision.

## Why this is needed

Operators need safe correlated evidence and reproducible release pairing without exposing tenant data or confusing a client with a server lifecycle.

## Scope and approach

- Correlate redacted traces, receipts, audit and bounded metric labels.
- Produce signed/checksummed paired artifacts and notices under an explicitly chosen release version.
- Qualify persistent shared-server behavior across clients and replicas.

## Essential planning context

Telemetry outages cannot block durable commits. Audit integrity/currentness faults remain observable without high-cardinality IDs or row values in metrics.

Release version remains a user decision; preparation does not invent a tag or certify connector completeness.

Software bill of materials (SBOM), signature/checksum manifests and component locks must agree on exact paired CLI/API/worker/query-helper/schema/bundle identities and notices. Initial assembly is this packet’s responsibility; full Open Container Initiative (OCI) image/native/offline installation remains [pm-upgrade-backup-restore](https://github.com/polymetrics-ai/pm-cli/issues/43) V75/V82/R25.

M12 initial observability/release assembler and manifest contracts plus V76 multi-process same-stack fixture built from already merged Go binaries. This is not finished OCI/package installation proof. Paired PM image creation, full V75 installation and V51/R24 coordinated backup belong to dependent upgrade-backup-restore.

## Dependencies and ownership

- Blocked by [pm-initial-five-composition-proof](https://github.com/polymetrics-ai/pm-cli/issues/41): Exercise supported GitHub/PostgreSQL write/ETL/reverse paths after foundations exist; disposition all five-by-seven cells, generate docs and report actual denominators without claiming full provider parity.

Blocking capabilities use verified issue identities below. All intended packet references resolve to verified identities; later consumers are not blocking prerequisites.

| Action | Path | Owned interfaces / responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CREATE | `internal/server/observability.go` | Own observability behavior within server; bounded role: Safe metrics/audit/trace and health signals; no inline backup owner. |
| CREATE | `.github/workflows/release.yml` | Repository-owned Go stdlib paired packager; exact build/checksum/SBOM/signing manifests and install/upgrade gates |

items.title: observation_source silently defaults to llm_summary, so 81% of a real instance misdescribes its own lineage
items.body:
## What

`POST /store` defaults `observation_source` to `llm_summary` when the caller omits it:

```ts
// src/services/observation_storage.ts:29
export const DEFAULT_OBSERVATION_SOURCE: ObservationSource = "llm_summary";
// src/server.ts:5957, 6167, 6187
observation_source: observationSource ?? "llm_summary",
```

Omission is thereby converted into a positive, and frequently false, claim: *a language model summarised this*. There is no way to distinguish "the caller declared it was an LLM summary" from "the caller said nothing".

## Prevalence

Sampled 32 observations across 18 entity types on a real personal instance (165k entities). **26 of 32 (81%) carry `observation_source` of `llm_summary` (17) or `null` (9).** Only 6 were accurately typed.

The mismatches are not edge cases. In each of these, the observation's own fields name a hard, non-LLM origin:

| Entity type | Field in the observation | observation_source |
|---|---|---|
| `file_asset` | `original_filename: "…pdf"` + SHA-256 `content_hash` | `llm_summary` |
| `image_asset` | `original_filename: "image-….png"`, `file_size: 30596` | `llm_summary` |
| `lab_reading` | `source_file: "<redacted>.pdf"` (clinical lab PDF) | `llm_summary` |
| `email_message` | `gmail_message_id`, `gmail_thread_id` | `llm_summary` |
| `email_message` | nested `source: "gmail"`, `message_id` | `llm_summary` |
| `meeting_analysis` | `source_type: "file"`, `source_reference: "…/recording.mp4"` | `llm_summary` |
| `note` | `source: "Apple Notes (iCloud) — bulk migration"` | `llm_summary` |
| `invoice` | `source: "gmail"`, exact line-item figures | `llm_summary` |
| `post` | `import_source_file` | `null` |
| `company` | `data_source: "<site> and comment"` | `null` |

A byte-identical stored file with a SHA-256 is the least model-derived record possible, and it is labelled as model output.

The sample is `entity_id`-ascending rather than random, so 81% describes the sample and not a certified instance-wide rate. The direction is not in doubt, though: the default applies to every caller that omits the field, which is most of them.

## Why it matters

1. **It corrupts trust calibration.** The field's purpose is telling a reader whether a value was measured, imported, or inferred. If nearly everything says "inferred", the signal is gone — including for the records that genuinely *are* inferred.
2. **It is silent.** Nothing warns at write time, and the value looks plausible on read.
3. **It defeats downstream filtering.** "Show me only non-inferred values" returns almost nothing.
4. **It misrepresents deterministic pipelines.** Rows parsed positionally from a spreadsheet by a script are labelled as LLM output.

Related in kind to #2033 (a correction silently reverted) and #1965 (embeddings silently skipped): the store reports success while quietly recording something untrue.

## Suggested fix

Options, roughly in order of preference:

1. **Make `observation_source` required** at the `/store` boundary. A breaking change, but the field is unreliable today, so little is lost. A migration could treat existing `llm_summary` rows as unknown.
2. **Default to a distinct `unspecified`** enum value. Preserves the caller-said-nothing case honestly and is backward compatible for readers that treat unknown values leniently.
3. **Keep the default but return a warning** in the store response — the same shape as `unknown_fields_count`, which already trains callers to fix their payloads.
4. **Infer from the request**: `file_content`/`file_path` present → `import`. Cheap, and it would have correctly typed the `file_asset` and `image_asset` cases above.

(2) plus (3) seems the best ratio of correctness to disruption.

## Repro

```bash
curl -X POST "$BASE/store" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"entities":[{"entity_type":"note","title":"probe","content":"x"}],
       "idempotency_key":"probe-obs-source-1"}'
# then list_observations on the returned entity_id:
#   observation_source: "llm_summary"   ← nothing in the request said so
```

Found while loading spreadsheet-derived records into a fresh instance: every row was labelled `llm_summary` despite no model being involved anywhere in the pipeline.

<!-- swarm-spec:start -->
## Swarm specification

_This section is maintained by the Ateles swarm. Each lens agent owns exactly one subsection below; the human-written description above these markers is never modified._

### Product / Scope (PM)

**Problem:** `POST /store` (and MCP/CLI equivalents) silently default omitted `observation_source` to `llm_summary`, falsely claiming LLM authorship and corrupting trust calibration, filtering, and pipeline observability.

**In scope**
- Add `unspecified` to the `ObservationSource` enum and make it the write-path default when the caller omits the field.
- Return a non-blocking store-response warning when `observation_source` is omitted (same training pattern as `unknown_fields_count` / `hint`).
- Apply on all store surfaces: REST `POST /store`, MCP `store`, CLI `neotoma store`.
- Update OpenAPI, Zod schemas (`action_schemas.ts`), and agent-instruction surfaces.
- Preserve explicit caller values (`observation_source: "llm_summary"` and other enum members persist exactly as sent).

**Out of scope**
- Making `observation_source` required at the boundary (option 1) — defer unless arch promotes.
- Request-shape heuristic inference, e.g. `file_content` → `import` (option 4) — follow-up issue.
- Historical backfill / migration of mislabelled observations — separate issue.
- Reducer `observation_source_priority` or schema-registry tuning.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] **Effect (REST):** `POST /store` with structured entities and no `observation_source` → `list_observations` on the created entity shows `observation_source: "unspecified"`, not `llm_summary`.
- [ ] **Effect (MCP):** MCP `store` omitting `observation_source` → same persisted value when read back via `list_observations` (MCP call shape).
- [ ] **Effect (CLI):** `neotoma store --entities '…'` without `--observation-source` → same persisted value when read back (CLI call shape).
- [ ] **Explicit value preserved:** `observation_source: "llm_summary"` on any surface still persists `llm_summary`.
- [ ] **Warning emitted:** Omitted `observation_source` returns a documented store-response warning naming the default and directing callers to set the field explicitly.
- [ ] **Contract updated:** `openapi.yaml` and `Observation.observation_source` enum include `unspecified` with documented semantics; MCP/CLI instruction surfaces aligned.
- [ ] **No regression:** Tests asserting explicit `llm_summary` behaviour still pass.

**Priority & sequencing:** P1 data-integrity fix (`contract_discrepancy`, `data-integrity`). Same silent-misreport class as #2033 / #1965. Unblocks trustworthy lineage filtering and import-pipeline observability. **Arch gate next** (interface change despite `bug` label); then ux ∥ impl sequencing per pipeline.

### Engineering

**Layering:** contract/schema → storage default → response warning → surface parity (REST/MCP/CLI share one server-side path — no per-surface logic to duplicate) → docs/tests.

**Files to touch**

1. `src/services/observation_storage.ts`
   - Add `"unspecified"` to the `ObservationSource` union/enum.
   - Change `DEFAULT_OBSERVATION_SOURCE` from `"llm_summary"` to `"unspecified"`.
   - Add an exported helper (e.g. `wasObservationSourceOmitted(input): boolean`) used by the store path to detect omission before the default is applied, so the warning can be generated at the same call site that decides the default — avoids re-deriving "was it omitted" downstream from the persisted value (which would be ambiguous once `unspecified` can also be sent explicitly).

2. `src/server.ts` (lines ~5957, 6167, 6187 per issue; grep for all `observation_source: observationSource ?? "llm_summary"` occurrences — there may be more than 3 call sites, confirm via `grep -n '"llm_summary"' src/server.ts`)
   - Replace each `observationSource ?? "llm_summary"` with `observationSource ?? DEFAULT_OBSERVATION_SOURCE` (import from `observation_storage.ts` rather than re-hardcoding the literal).
   - At each of these call sites, when the omission helper reports true, accumulate a warning entry into the store response payload (same array/field pattern used for `unknown_fields_count`/`hint` — locate that construction in the `/store` handler and extend it, do not create a parallel warning channel).
   - Warning text: name the field, the default applied, and the fix — e.g. `"observation_source" was omitted and defaulted to "unspecified"; set it explicitly (e.g. "import", "manual_entry", "llm_summary") to preserve lineage accuracy.` Keep wording consistent with existing `hint` tone.

3. `src/schemas/action_schemas.ts` (or wherever the Zod `ObservationSource` enum / store request schema lives — grep `ObservationSource` and `llm_summary` for the exact file if different from above)
   - Add `"unspecified"` to the Zod enum so it round-trips through validation on all surfaces (REST body, MCP tool args, CLI arg parsing all validate through this shared schema — this is the single point that gives cross-surface parity for free; no separate MCP/CLI schema edits needed unless those layers maintain their own copies, confirm via grep).

4. `openapi.yaml`
   - `Observation.observation_source` enum: add `unspecified`.
   - Add/extend the `description` to document semantics: caller did not specify a source; distinct from an explicit `llm_summary` claim.
   - Document the new store-response warning field/shape (reuse existing warning-array schema definition if `unknown_fields_count`/`hint` already has one; extend it rather than defining a new schema object).

5. Generated/derived files (regenerate as the LAST step before `gh pr create`, per policy `regenerate_generated_files_before_opening_pr`):
   - `npm run generate:test-catalog` (only if test files are added/moved — they are, see QA-adjacent test files below).
   - Regenerate `openapi_types`, `contract_mappings`, capability manifest, `mcp-docs` — run each repo's standard generate/validate script (grep `package.json` scripts for `generate:` / `validate:` targets touching these artifacts).
   - Run the corresponding `validate:*` checks locally and confirm green before opening the PR.

6. Agent-instruction / doc surfaces referencing `observation_source` defaults (grep repo-wide for `llm_summary` outside test files — likely candidates: MCP tool descriptions/docstrings for `store`, CLI `--help` text, any onboarding doc listing valid `observation_source` values). Update each to mention `unspecified` as the omission default and list it alongside other enum members.

**Data/contract changes**
- `ObservationSource` enum gains one member: `unspecified`. No migration of existing rows (explicitly out of scope per PM section).
- Store response gains a non-blocking warning entry when `observation_source` is omitted, following the existing `unknown_fields_count`/`hint` warning shape — additive, no breaking change to response contract.
- No new entity fields, no schema version bump beyond the enum addition.

**Build-step checklist**

**Test coverage required at impl (for Cicada's build PR, per impl sign-off checklist)**

### QA / Test Plan

### Definition-of-done checklist

### Gate posture

Sign-off is conditional on: fixtures above committed in the implementation PR, and `agentic_evals` CI lane green on them. If Cicada's PR ships without the omission-vs-explicit-unspecified distinguishability fixture (the case most likely to be skipped, since it's easy to conflate with the plain-omission case), this is filed as a `[BLOCKING]` concern rather than signed off — that fixture is the one that actually prevents the issue's failure mode from recurring in a new form (explicit `unspecified` misclassified as omission, or vice versa).

### Security / Arch

**ADR — decision:** Add `unspecified` to `ObservationSource`, change write-path default from `llm_summary` → `unspecified` when the caller omits the field, and emit a structured non-blocking store warning on omission. Explicit enum values round-trip unchanged. **Not promoted:** required-field enforcement (option 1) or request-shape inference (option 4).

**Gate posture:** Interface change correctly arch-gated despite `bug` label (`contract_discrepancy`). **Verdict:** `SIGNED_OFF` — proceed to impl with amendments below.

#### Architectural constraints (immovable)

- **Contract-first** per `docs/architecture/openapi_contract_flow.md` and `change_guardrails_rules.mdc` — spec before handler.
- **Single write seam:** REST `POST /store`, MCP `store`, CLI `neotoma store` share one server path; no per-surface default logic.
- **`observation_source` is request-scoped** — one value applies to every observation in the batch (`openapi.yaml` `StoreStructuredRequest.observation_source`). Per-entity omission is not representable; QA must not assert mixed per-entity sources in one call.
- **`unspecified` is a lineage sentinel, not a provenance class** — do **not** add it to `DEFAULT_OBSERVATION_SOURCE_PRIORITY` / reducer tie-break lists in this PR (PM out-of-scope); reducer behaviour with `unspecified` rows is a tracked follow-up.
- **No historical backfill** in this change.

#### Eng-spec amendments (blocking for pattern conformance)

- [ ] **Warning channel:** Emit via existing `store_warnings[]` with stable code **`OBSERVATION_SOURCE_OMITTED`** — same object shape as `MISSING_CONTENT_FIELD` / `SOURCE_PRIORITY_IGNORED` (`code`, `message`, `observation_index`, `entity_type`, `entity_id`). Extend the `store_warnings[].code` description in `openapi.yaml`; do **not** overload top-level `hint` (contractually bound to `unknown_fields_count > 0`).
- [ ] **Warning scope:** Because omission is request-level, emit **one** `store_warnings` entry per store call (use first created entity for `observation_index` / `entity_id`; message states default applies to all observations in the request). Do not duplicate N identical warnings for N entities.
- [ ] **Pure helper module:** Add `src/services/observation_source_warning.ts` (mirror `source_priority_warning.ts`) exporting `wasObservationSourceOmitted(rawParsed)` and `buildObservationSourceOmittedWarning(...)`. Predicate MUST inspect raw parsed input (`observation_source === undefined`) **before** default application — explicit `"unspecified"` must not warn.
- [ ] **Schema file path:** Zod enum lives in **`src/shared/action_schemas.ts`** (not `src/schemas/`). Append `"unspecified"` **last** in `OBSERVATION_SOURCE_VALUES`; update locked contract test order accordingly.
- [ ] **Stale comment purge:** Update `DEFAULT_OBSERVATION_SOURCE` / `action_schemas.ts` comments that claim MCP callers are “LLM-driven by construction” — that rationale is exactly what #2241 invalidates.

#### Contract-first build order

1. `openapi.yaml` — add `unspecified` to all `ObservationSource` enums; document sentinel semantics (distinct from explicit `llm_summary`); document `OBSERVATION_SOURCE_OMITTED` in `store_warnings[].code`; flip default description to `unspecified`.
2. `npm run openapi:generate` → `src/shared/openapi_types.ts`.
3. `src/shared/action_schemas.ts` — enum + types.
4. `src/services/observation_storage.ts` — `DEFAULT_OBSERVATION_SOURCE = "unspecified"`.
5. `src/services/observation_source_warning.ts` — pure helper.
6. Wire into **`src/actions.ts` and `src/server.ts`** store handlers (both paths today emit `store_warnings`; grep both, not `server.ts` alone).
7. Agent-instruction surfaces (below) + `docs/developer/mcp/tool_descriptions.yaml` + CLI `--help` for `store`.
8. Tests / eval fixtures → `npm run generate:test-catalog` + all `validate:*` / `generate:*` for touched artifacts (last step before PR).

No new `operationId`; `contract_mappings.ts` row unchanged. Additive response field only — not a legacy-payload **rejection** tightening; if any `tests/contract/legacy_payloads/` fixture asserts omission → `llm_summary`, flip expected persisted value and note in `CHANGES.md`.

#### Agent-instruction coherence (blocking)

Current MCP instructions (`docs/developer/mcp/instructions.md` § observation_source) instruct agents to **omit** the field for LLM chat — directly contradicts the fix. After this ships:

- [ ] **Omission default:** Document that omitted `observation_source` persists as `unspecified` and triggers `OBSERVATION_SOURCE_OMITTED` in `store_warnings`.
- [ ] **Explicit LLM writes:** Instruct agents doing LLM extraction/summary to set **`observation_source: "llm_summary"` explicitly** on every `store` call (user-phase, attachment, closing store as applicable).
- [ ] **Pipeline writers:** Instruct import/ETL/daemon paths to set `import`, `sensor`, `workflow_state`, or `sync` explicitly — never rely on omission.
- [ ] **MCP ↔ CLI parity** per `docs/developer/agent_instructions_sync_rules.mdc` — mirror in `docs/developer/cli_agent_instructions.md`; update CLI `--observation-source` help (currently claims `llm_summary (default)`).
- [ ] **Hooks / turn instructions:** Any session hook text that sets or assumes `llm_summary` on omission must be updated in the same PR.

Impl sign-off blocked if instructions still tell agents to omit the field for ordinary chat.

#### Cross-surface parity

- [ ] Identical behaviour on REST, MCP, CLI via shared Zod parse + shared store handler — policy `cross_surface_contract_parity_tested_all_surfaces` (`ent_2ad0677fe23c0c1878ae43e8`).
- [ ] Contract tests: `tests/contract/openapi_schema.test.ts`, `tests/contract/contract_mcp_cli_parity.test.ts` green after enum/warning doc update.
- [ ] **QA fixture correction:** Drop or rewrite “batch mixed per-entity observation_source” — replace with “multi-entity batch, field omitted once at request level → all observations `unspecified`, one warning”.

#### Security requirements

- [ ] **Auth unchanged:** Standard bearer / AAuth on all store and read-back paths; no new public endpoints or grant surfaces.
- [ ] **`idempotency_key` required** on every mutating eval fixture and integration test (`StoreStructuredRequest` contract); replay/idempotency behaviour must not change because of the default flip (omission path only).
- [ ] **Tenant isolation:** Every post-store read-back (`list_observations`, `entities get`, MCP equivalent) MUST use the **same authenticated `user_id`** as the write; assert created `entity_id` is not readable under a different tenant/fixture user. Warning payload MUST NOT include observation field values — only `entity_type`, `entity_id`, indices, and generic guidance (PII-free by construction, same bar as `ResolverWarning`).
- [ ] **Credential exposure:** Warning `message` strings are static templates; forbid interpolating tokens, file paths, or entity payload content.
- [ ] **Trust calibration:** Downstream filters treating `llm_summary` as “model-inferred” remain valid for **explicit** values only; document that legacy rows mislabelled `llm_summary` are unchanged until backfill issue ships.

#### Reversibility & risks

| Change | Reversibility |
|---|---|
| Default constant + enum member | Trivial revert |
| `store_warnings` code | Additive; clients ignore unknown codes |
| Agent-instruction flip (omit → explicit `llm_summary`) | **Harder** — agents/hooks must be updated together or chat lineage regresses to `unspecified` |

**Tracked risks (non-blocking):** (1) reducer ignores `unspecified` in priority map — competing observations may tie unexpectedly until follow-up; (2) stats dashboards bucketing `unspecified` separately from `llm_summary`; (3) 81% historical mislabels remain until backfill issue.

#### Arch acceptance checklist

- [ ] OpenAPI + generated types committed before handler edits.
- [ ] `OBSERVATION_SOURCE_OMITTED` in `store_warnings`, not `hint`.
- [ ] Omission detected pre-default; explicit `unspecified` silent.
- [ ] MCP + CLI instructions + `--help` tell agents the new contract.
- [ ] Cross-surface parity tests pass with `idempotency_key` on every mutating case.
- [ ] Read-back tests enforce tenant-scoped access.

### Legal

### Legal / Compliance

**Scope check:** This change touches the `store_warnings[]` response shape, an enum addition, and agent-instruction text. It does not add a new endpoint, a new data category, or a new third-party data flow. Legal review here is narrow and confirms the above rather than raising new blockers.

#### Dependency licensing

- [ ] No new third-party dependencies are introduced by this change (new enum member, pure helper module, response field, doc/instruction edits only). **No licence audit action required.** If Cicada's implementation PR pulls in any new package to build/test this (e.g. a fixture/test helper lib), flag it in the PR description for a follow-up licence check against the project's licence (resolve from `product_profile`) — do not assume none will be added.

#### PII / data-handling on public-effect surfaces

- [ ] **Warning payload is the only new public-effect surface** (`store_warnings[]` entry returned to the calling client). Confirming Security's constraint from this angle: the warning `message` MUST be a static template — no interpolation of entity field values, file paths, tokens, or free-text content. This is a legal control, not just a security one: interpolating a stored field into a response payload risks re-exposing PII/content the caller may not be authorized to see back in that exact channel (e.g. a webhook/log sink relaying store responses), and risks the warning itself becoming an unintended export path for regulated data (health/financial content plausible given the `lab_reading`/`invoice` examples in the issue).
- [ ] **`observation_index` / `entity_id` are identifiers, not content** — acceptable to include per Security's spec. No additional consent or disclosure obligation attaches to returning an entity's own ID to its own authenticated owner.
- [ ] **No new data category is collected or retained.** `observation_source: "unspecified"` is a lineage/provenance label, not personal data about a data subject — it does not expand what regulated data categories the system holds and does not itself trigger a lawful-basis reassessment under the data-protection regime in `locale_profile`.
- [ ] **Downstream trust-calibration disclosure (should-fix, non-blocking):** if the operator has published or represented (to customers, in a privacy notice, or in the anchor offer artifact under my standing claims-review gate) that `observation_source` reliably indicates data lineage, that representation was **already inaccurate** pre-fix (per the issue's 81% finding) and remains **partially inaccurate post-fix** for the ~81% of historical rows still mislabelled `llm_summary` until the backfill issue ships. Recommend: if any customer-facing material makes a lineage/provenance accuracy claim tied to this field, route it through my anchor-offer claims-review gate before it is next published, and note the historical-mislabel caveat explicitly rather than silently relying on the fix alone.

#### Guest-token / credential scope

- [ ] **No guest-readable surface is touched.** This change does not modify any entity type's `guest_access_policy`, does not add a new public/guest-accessible field, and does not change auth/AAuth scope on `/store` or read-back endpoints (confirmed against Security's "Auth unchanged" item). No guest-token exposure analysis is required for this PR.
- [ ] **Confirm at PR review, not assumed:** if implementation surfaces the new `store_warnings[].code`/`message` through any guest-facing or public-read path (e.g. a public issue/PR bot comment echoing a store response verbatim), re-run this check — the static-template constraint above becomes load-bearing the moment a guest/public reader can see it.

#### Escalation

- [ ] **No escalation to qualified counsel required for this change.** It is an internal data-lineage/schema correction with no new contract, no new regulated data flow, and no third-party licensing change. Escalation trigger conditions (contract above threshold, regulatory enforcement risk, IP dispute, employment matter) are not present.
- [ ] **Recommend, not block:** track the historical-mislabel disclosure item above against the operator's next customer-facing claim involving `observation_source`/data lineage — file as a follow-up note to the anchor-offer claims-review gate, not as a blocker on this PR.

**Verdict:** Sign as-is. No must-fix redlines. One should-fix (customer-facing lineage-claim disclosure, tracked above) carried forward as a non-blocking follow-up against the claims-review gate, not against this implementation.
<!-- swarm-spec:end -->

items.title: Test wall: users app unit fills (filters + role visibility)
items.body:
# Test wall: users app unit fills (filters + role visibility)

Unit-fill workstream for the **users app** — one of four per-app fills from [backend unit coverage gaps (#366)](https://github.com/avantifellows/plio-backend/issues/366), part of the [test-wall map (#362)](https://github.com/avantifellows/plio-backend/issues/362). Formally blocked by #374 (its harness slice is the real gate and is already merged on the base branch).

## Decision Summary

- Surface under test: `UserViewSet` query-param filter branches (`ids`, `organization`, `email` — singly, combined, empty, and invalid) and `RoleViewSet` per-caller-class visibility rules, both in the users app
- Seam: **one** — the authenticated HTTP list seam (`GET /users/`, `GET /roles/`) driven through the harness `authed_client` actor fixture; no lower viewset/queryset seam introduced
- Caller for the user-filter specs: a superuser actor (the existing permission gate restricts list to superusers; the gate itself stays pinned by legacy tests, not re-tested)
- Org context for the role specs: selected only via the `Organization` request header on the actor call — never `set_schema()`; unknown shortcodes fall back to the public schema by design, which is what makes the unknown-workspace branch reachable at this seam
- Role visibility matrix pinned per caller class: superuser → all seeded roles; no header → none; unknown-shortcode header → none; non-member → none; org super-admin → org-admin + org-view; org-admin → org-view; org-view → none
- Filter quirks pinned as-is (not fixed): an all-invalid `ids` value silently skips the filter and returns the full list, while an invalid `organization` value returns an empty list (asymmetry pinned); empty-string params are treated as filter-absent; duplicate membership rows collapse via the organization filter's de-duplication
- Soft-delete edge: a soft-deleted user stays invisible to `ids`/`email` filters (safedelete manager is the filters' base queryset)
- Expected values: hand-listed sets of constructed user IDs and literal role-name lists from the spec's own rows — never recomputed by re-running the app's filtering; list responses compared as unordered sets (neither model declares an ordering)
- Data: users-app tables live in the shared public schema (SHARED_APPS), so specs build rows directly with the shared factories — no `in_workspace(...)` needed (deliberate, flagged deviation from the tenant-schema fills); roles come from the seeded `DEFAULT_ROLES`, membership rows are created directly as the harness fixtures already do; no new shared factories
- Style: pytest specs in one new unit-lane module; one edge per named spec; existing tests untouched; test-only PR — no product changes
- Lane and command: backend-unit lane, green locally with `docker-compose exec web pytest --ignore=tests/integration` (binding local-first criterion)
- Ratchet: bump the backend-unit floor in `coverage_floors/unit` (currently 88.37) to new measured −0.5–1% in the same PR; floors only move up

## Problem Statement

`UserViewSet`'s `ids`/`organization`/`email` filters and `RoleViewSet`'s visibility rules are branchy, permission-adjacent logic with no direct tests. The legacy suite pins only that a superuser may list users and a general user may not; no test in any lane passes a single filter param, and the role-visibility matrix is touched only incidentally by one integration journey's access probes (two of seven branches). These branches decide **who sees which users and which roles are grantable** — a queryset-manager or request-parsing shift anywhere in the Django 3.1 → 5.2 upgrade chain could silently widen or empty those lists with CI green. The surface-based bar from #366 flags exactly this: the methods execute under line coverage; the branches never do.

## Solution

Pin every filter branch and every visibility branch in isolation at the HTTP list seam: each spec builds a small hand-constructed set of users, memberships, and (seeded) roles, calls the list endpoint as a named caller class, and asserts the exact ID set or role-name list from its own constructed rows. Observed quirks are pinned as-is and documented in the spec docstrings. The PR lands in the backend-unit lane and ratchets the unit coverage floor so the gain is locked in.

## User Stories

1. As a maintainer driving the Django upgrade chain, I want each `UserViewSet` filter branch and `RoleViewSet` visibility branch pinned by a unit test, so that an ORM or request-parsing shift between Django 3.1 and 5.2 fails CI instead of silently changing who sees which users and roles.
2. As a platform admin (superuser), I want `ids`, `organization`, and `email` filters to return exactly the matching users — singly and combined — so that admin tooling built on the users list stays correct.
3. As a platform admin, I want invalid and empty filter values to keep behaving exactly as they do today (pinned as-is), so that existing consumers of the endpoint don't break under the upgrade.
4. As a workspace super-admin, I want the roles list under my workspace header to show exactly the org-admin and org-view roles, so that I can grant only roles I am allowed to grant.
5. As a workspace org-admin, I want the roles list to show only the org-view role, so that I cannot escalate anyone beyond my own grant rights.
6. As an org-view member or a non-member, I want the roles list to be empty for that workspace, so that role machinery never leaks to callers with no grant rights.
7. As a workspace admin, I want soft-deleted users excluded from filtered user lists, so that deleted accounts never resurface through admin queries.
8. As a test-wall contributor, I want the users fill written pytest-style on the shared harness (actor fixture, factories, seeded roles), so that specs stay consistent with #374 and free of ad-hoc auth or schema machinery.
9. As a test-wall contributor, I want expected values hand-listed from each spec's constructed rows, so that no spec is a tautology that re-runs the app's own filtering.
10. As a reviewer, I want one edge per named spec, so that a red test names the broken branch directly.
11. As a maintainer, I want the backend-unit floor bumped in the same PR, so that the fill's coverage gain cannot silently erode later.
12. As a developer on this repo, I want the whole unit lane green with the one documented command, so that I can verify the fill locally before CI.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Test-only PR.** No changes to users-app views, permissions, serializers, or models. Quirks observed while pinning (see Further Notes) are documented in spec docstrings, not fixed.
- **One new unit-lane spec module** in the shared tests package (outside `tests/integration/`), the shared home for the whole users fill — mirroring the plio and entries fills' single-module pattern, with a module docstring stating scope, the caller classes, and the oracle discipline. Slice-local helpers stay in-module; only helpers a second module needs graduate to the shared harness.
- **Harness reuse:** the `authed_client` actor factory (each spec names its caller class explicitly), the session-scoped workspace fixtures for the two seeded organizations, and the shared user factory. The superuser caller is built by flipping the superuser flag on an authed actor and saving — the same idiom the integration membership journey uses.
- **Shared-schema data, no workspace switching (flagged deviation):** the users app is in SHARED_APPS, so users, roles, and membership rows live in the public schema. Unlike the plio/entries fills, specs build data directly with no `in_workspace(...)` — there is no tenant-schema row anywhere in this fill. The `Organization` header on the actor call is the only org-context selector; the tenant middleware resolves it (falling back to the public schema for unknown shortcodes), which keeps every `RoleViewSet` branch reachable at the HTTP seam. The no-`set_schema()` rule is satisfied throughout.
- **Roles and memberships:** roles are the three seeded `DEFAULT_ROLES` (fetched by name, never re-created — "specs never build ad-hoc role machinery", per the integration journey's discipline); membership rows are created directly on the membership model, the same way the harness's own creator fixture does. No new shared factories.
- **Assertion shape:** user-list responses are compared as unordered sets of `id`s; role-list responses as sorted lists of `name`s (neither model declares a default ordering, so ordered assertions would be brittle).
- **Coverage ratchet:** measure the unit lane as CI does on the merged state, then bump `coverage_floors/unit` (currently 88.37) to measured −0.5–1% in the same PR per the committed ratchet rule. Never lower a floor.

## Testing Decisions

**Seam — one, existing, highest:** the authenticated HTTP list seam (`GET /users/`, `GET /roles/` through the harness actor). This is the highest seam that observes both branchy surfaces, and it is already established in the unit lane by the #375 report-CSV fill (HTTP seam, unit lane) and by the legacy users suite. The lower alternative — calling `get_queryset()` directly on a viewset with a fabricated request — would be a **new** seam that bypasses the permission, header, and middleware wiring the branches depend on; it is rejected. The integration lane is not the right home either: the per-branch matrix is exactly the unit-fill territory #366 carved out, while journeys keep flows.

**`UserViewSet` filter spec plan** (caller: superuser actor; expected value = a hand-listed set of constructed user IDs):

- No filter params → the full user set (exactly the spec's constructed users plus the caller)
- `ids` single value → that user only; `ids` multi-value CSV → exactly those users
- `ids` with no matching rows → empty list (no-match branch)
- `ids` mixed valid/invalid tokens → invalid tokens dropped, valid ones applied
- `ids` all-invalid tokens → filter silently skipped, full list returned (quirk pinned as-is)
- Empty-string `ids` / `organization` / `email` → treated as filter-absent (full list)
- `organization` with members → exactly that workspace's members; a member of only the other seeded workspace is excluded (decoy)
- `organization` with no members → empty list
- `organization` non-integer → empty list (quirk: asymmetric with the `ids` behavior — pinned as-is)
- `organization` de-duplication: a user holding two membership rows in the same workspace appears once
- `email` exact match → that user; `email` no match → empty list
- Combined `ids` + `organization` + `email` → conjunction: only the row satisfying all three survives; rows satisfying a strict subset are excluded
- Soft-deleted user (deleted via the model's own `delete()`) → absent even when explicitly requested by `ids` or `email`

**`RoleViewSet` visibility matrix** (expected value = literal role-name list):

- Superuser, no header → all three seeded roles
- Non-superuser, no header → empty
- Header with unknown workspace shortcode → empty
- Header valid, caller not a member of that workspace → empty
- Member as org super-admin → exactly org-admin + org-view
- Member as org-admin → exactly org-view
- Member as org-view → empty (fall-through branch)

**What makes a good spec here:** assert only external behavior (the list response's ID set / name list); expected values come from the spec's own constructed rows or the seeded role names, never from re-running the filter or visibility logic; one branch per spec, named for the branch.

**Prior art:** the #375 report-CSV fill (HTTP seam in the unit lane, decoy-row discipline, hand-listed literals) and the #376 entries fill (single-module pattern, one-edge-per-spec naming) on this base branch; the integration membership lifecycle journey (seeded-roles discipline, superuser-actor idiom, header-driven org selection). Legacy `users/tests.py` stays untouched — its superuser-gate and config/setting specs are not duplicated.

## Out of Scope

- The org-user viewset entirely — its list queryset branches, destroy flow, and query-param handling are delegated to the integration `org/` axis (#374), per the issue's scope decision
- Org membership lifecycle and the tenancy/permission matrix — integration lane (#374)
- OTP flow and the other auth endpoints (convert-token, SSO token, get-by-access-token) — integration-only per the #366 inventory; legacy tests keep them
- User config/setting actions, caching behavior, and the user-list permission gate — already pinned by the legacy suite
- Product changes, including fixing the pinned quirks (the `ids`-vs-`organization` invalid-input asymmetry; empty-string params as filter-absent)
- The other per-app fills (#375 plio, #376 entries, #378 etl) and the frontend/e2e lanes (#379, #380)

## Further Notes

- **Sequencing:** formally blocked by #374; the real gate — its harness slice (pytest wiring, actor fixture, factories, seeded roles and workspaces) — is already merged into the base branch this work stacks on, alongside the completed #375 and #376 fills.
- **Quirks pinned, not fixed:** (a) an all-invalid `ids` value drops every token and then skips the filter, returning the **full** list, while an invalid `organization` value returns an **empty** list — callers see opposite failure modes for the same mistake; (b) empty-string filter values mean "no filter", not "match nothing"; (c) the `email` filter is a raw exact match (no normalization).
- **Near-dead branch, decided:** the `ids` handler's numeric-conversion fallback (return-nothing on conversion error) is unreachable for ordinary input — tokens are digit-gated before conversion — and can only be reached by exotic Unicode digit-like characters (e.g. a superscript digit, which passes the digit check but fails conversion). Decision: attempt one spec pinning that fallback with such a token; if it proves brittle in CI, drop the spec and document the branch as effectively dead in the module docstring instead. Do not chase the branch in the coverage ratchet either way.
- **Accepted overlap:** the integration membership journey asserts two visibility outcomes (org-view → none, org-admin → org-view) as access probes inside a lifecycle flow. The unit matrix re-pins them as direct per-branch specs; the duplication is deliberate — a red probe names a broken journey, a red matrix spec names the broken branch.
- **ADRs:** `docs/adr/` does not exist in this repo; no ADR conflicts. Vocabulary follows `CONTEXT.md` (workspace, organization header, role, lane, floor).

items.title: POST /store has no field for data origin: the provenance column records who wrote a row, never where it came from
items.body:
## What

Every observation has a `provenance` column, but a caller cannot write to it. Server-side it is populated with **client attribution**:

```json
{"attribution_tier":"unverified_client","attributed_at":"…",
 "client_name":"local-agent-mode-mcpsrv_neotoma","client_version":"1.0.0"}
```

Across 32 observations sampled on a real instance, **every non-null `provenance` had exactly this shape, and none carried any origin information**. `client_name` varied only across `local-agent-mode-mcpsrv_neotoma`, `claude-code`, `cursor-vscode`, `Anthropic/ClaudeAI`.

That answers *which harness performed the write*. It does not answer *where the data came from* — the file, sheet, row, URL, message id, or API endpoint — and `POST /store` accepts no field that does. Its allowed set is:

```
commit, entities, external_actor, file_content, file_idempotency_key,
file_path, idempotency_key, interpretation, mime_type, observation_source,
original_filename, relationships, source_priority, source_peer_id,
source_storage, strict, intake
```

`observation_source` gives a six-value category (`sensor` / `llm_summary` / `workflow_state` / `human` / `import` / `sync`). `original_filename` names one file for the whole request. Neither identifies a row's actual origin, and a request commonly carries entities from more than one place.

## What the auto-created source record looks like

Storing entities without a file creates a `source` whose own provenance is:

```json
{"upload_method":"api_store","client":"api","source_priority":100,
 "uploaded_at":"…"}
```

with `original_filename: null` and `source_type: null`. It describes the HTTP request, not the origin. So `source_id` is non-null (81% of the sample) and still leads nowhere.

## The consequence

Origin ends up in ad-hoc, per-type snapshot fields invented independently by each writer. Observed in one instance: `source_file`, `source_url`, `source_reference`, `source_type`, `audio_file_path`, `original_source_file`, `import_source_file`, `data_source`, `enrichment_source`, `source_artifacts`, and a nested `source`.

Consequences:

- No cross-type query can ask "what came from this file?" — every type spells it differently, and some not at all.
- The Inspector's Sources page cannot show anything meaningful, because the real trail is not where it looks.
- Field-level provenance (#2026 touches the same area) resolves to an observation whose source record says only "an API request happened".
- Writers that do it well are doing it by convention. `transcription` is the best case seen — `observation_source: "sensor"`, plus `audio_file_path`, `original_source_file` and a `data_source` naming the producing script — but nothing in the API asked for any of it, so nothing else inherits the practice.

## Why this is likely to be systemic

Agents write most records here. An agent supplies what the schema asks for. The schema asks for nothing about origin, so origin is omitted — and the `observation_source` default (#2241) then labels the row `llm_summary`. The two defects compound: the typed field is wrong, and there is nowhere to put the truth.

## Suggested fix

Add a caller-supplied origin to `POST /store`, separate from the server's client attribution. Sketch:

```jsonc
{
  "entities": [...],
  "origin": {
    "kind": "file | url | email | api | manual",
    "locator": "Atencion al cliente.xlsx#Tickets/row97",  // sheet+row, message id, endpoint
    "producer": "tools/derive_all.py@4a5409c",            // code that shaped it
    "retrieved_at": "2026-08-27T09:00:00Z",
    "notes": "identity columns aliased; other columns verbatim"
  }
}
```

Points worth preserving in whatever shape it takes:

- **Per-entity override.** One request often mixes origins; a single `original_filename` cannot express that.
- **A `producer` slot.** Which script or agent, at which revision, shaped the value — the difference between "from this spreadsheet" and "from this spreadsheet, via a parser that was wrong until Tuesday".
- **Keep client attribution separate.** Who wrote it and where it came from are different questions; merging them loses both.
- **Surface it on read.** `retrieve_entity_snapshot` and the Inspector should show the trail, or writers get no feedback that it is missing.

A transitional option: keep storing origin in `data_source`, but **declare it on the base schema for every entity type** so it stops being per-writer convention. That is the workaround adopted in the client pipeline that surfaced this — origin is folded into a declared `data_source` string per entity, e.g.

```
tools/derive_all.py@4a5409c | file=<workbook>.xlsx | sheet=WHOLESALE (invoice sub-table) | fixture=… | identity aliased
```

It works, but it is prose where a typed column belongs: a consumer has to know the convention and parse it.

Related: #2241 (the `llm_summary` default), #2026 (`retrieve_field_provenance` on null `source_id`).

### Engineering

**Goal:** Let callers declare *where upstream data came from* on `POST /store` / MCP `store` / CLI `store`, persist it on each created observation (separate from server-written client attribution), and surface it on read paths so writers get feedback and field provenance is not stuck at “an API request happened.”

**Design (follow `external_actor` pattern):** `observations.provenance` already holds parallel facets — AAuth/client attribution (`client_name`, `attribution_tier`, …) and `external_actor`. Add a third facet, **`data_origin`**, answering “where did the *payload* come from?” Server attribution remains server-only; callers cannot write attribution keys.

#### Contract / schema

- [ ] Add shared **`DataOriginInput`** (`src/shared/action_schemas.ts`):
  - Zod **`.strict()`** object; export `DataOriginInputSchema`, type `DataOriginInput`.
  - Fields:
    - `kind`: enum `file | url | email | api | manual` (**required** when `origin` is present)
    - `locator`: string (**required** for `file|url|email|api`; optional for `manual`) — sheet+row, message id, URL, API path, etc.
    - `producer`: optional string — script/agent + revision, e.g. `tools/derive_all.py@4a5409c`
    - `retrieved_at`: optional ISO-8601 datetime string
    - `notes`: optional string
  - Reject unknown keys (same discipline as `ExternalActorInputSchema`).

- [ ] Extend **`StoreRequest`** (closed top-level set):

  - Update `StoreRequestSchema` in `action_schemas.ts`, `openapi.yaml`, `openapi_actions.yaml`.

- [ ] Document persisted shape on **`Observation.provenance`** in OpenAPI:
  - `provenance.data_origin` mirrors the input object (all optional fields caller supplied).
