milestone.title: v0.0.56 — Admin Cache Elevation
milestone.description: Runtime-controllable, self-explaining, tenant-scoped Query Cache. PRD #4544; governance boundary ADR-0033; vocab CONTEXT.md § Query Cache. Config-block removal phase 2 (#4551) graduates to the next tag.

items.body:
Produced by the admin-cache elevation cycle: audit (`.claude/research/admin-cache-audit-2026-07-10.md`, with the grill-outcomes register appended) → grill session (2026-07-10). Vocabulary is pinned in **CONTEXT.md § Query Cache**; the governance boundary is **ADR-0033** (the key captures row-determining inputs; hits re-apply presentation governance; veto seams run before the cache check). The two fix-invariant bugs (#4532 nested-claims key material, #4533 flush audit-await) are filed separately and proceed independently.

## Problem Statement

The Query Cache engine is sound — tenant-isolated keys, governance-ordered hits, honest audit durations — but nobody can steer it, see it, or trust its edges. A SaaS workspace admin is told to set an env var they cannot set, and no runtime knob exists anywhere: tuning or disabling the cache during an incident means editing a config file and redeploying three regions. A chat user is served up-to-five-minute-old data with no age shown, no way to force a refresh ("refresh that number" silently returns the same stale rows), and an agent that doesn't know caching exists so it asserts stale numbers as current. An admin tightening RLS believes it applies instantly — but pre-change rows keep serving from the cache. The only management verb is a fleet-wide flush that any org admin can fire once a second, coldstarting every tenant in the region while the dialog implies self-scope; the stats are lifetime-since-boot fleet totals that don't move after a flush and leak cross-tenant activity. And the plugin cache-backend seam advertises Redis while its synchronous contract makes Redis impossible — a wrong-shape plugin backend breaks SQL execution fleet-wide the moment it loads.

## Solution

The Query Cache becomes runtime-controllable, self-explaining, and scoped to the tenant. The knobs move to the settings registry — workspace admins toggle caching and tune TTL from the cache page itself, hot-reloaded, no redeploy — and the config-file block is deprecated. Every cache hit carries its age: the user sees "cached · 3m ago," the agent is told about caching so it caveats time-sensitive answers, and a bypass affordance makes "refresh that number" actually re-run and re-freshen the entry. Governance follows one written principle (ADR-0033): the resolved RLS config joins the key material, so an RLS change instantly orphans pre-change entries; plugin veto hooks run before the cache check. Invalidation grows scope: entries carry org/connection tags, tenant admins flush their own entries (with their own counts), fleet-wide flush becomes a platform-admin verb with blast-radius disclosure, and internal callers purge exactly the org they mean. Stats bucket by org with a since-labeled lifetime rate and a moving last-hour rate. The cockpit shows what's cached — an entry table with age, rows, connection, and SQL preview, per-entry delete — with honest disabled/warming/refused states. The plugin backend contract goes async (Redis becomes buildable) with shape validation that fails a bad plugin's init visibly while the cache degrades safely to the in-process LRU.

## User Stories

1. As a SaaS workspace admin, I want to enable or disable the Query Cache for my workspace at runtime, so that I control the freshness/speed trade-off without asking the operator to redeploy
2. As a SaaS workspace admin, I want to set my workspace's cache TTL from the admin console, so that my cache lifetime matches my data's actual change cadence (e.g. hourly ETL → 60s TTL)
3. As a platform admin, I want the cache's memory budget (max entries) as a platform setting with hot reload, so that I can tune a region's cache without a restart
4. As a platform admin, I want a `ttl`/`maxSize` change to actually take effect on the running backend, so that the settings page never silently lies about what's applied
5. As a self-hosted operator, I want cache knobs to work through the same settings/env chain as every other Atlas knob, so that there is one precedence story with a visible source instead of a config-file special case
6. As a self-hosted operator with a `cache:` block in my config file, I want a loud boot warning during the deprecation window, so that I migrate deliberately instead of discovering my block is ignored
7. As a workspace admin on the cache page, I want the enable/TTL controls inline next to the hit-rate they affect, so that diagnosing and fixing a freshness problem is one screen
8. As a workspace admin, I want the disabled-cache page state to show the actual toggle (not env-var copy I can't act on), so that the page's guidance is always actionable in my deploy mode
9. As a chat user, I want cached results labeled with their age ("cached · 3m ago"), so that I know how current the number I'm looking at is
10. As a chat user, I want "refresh that number" to actually re-run the query, so that I'm never stuck with stale data for the full TTL
11. As a business user sharing a result, I want the age visible on the result card, so that my audience knows the as-of time without asking
12. As the Atlas agent, I want the executeSQL tool description to tell me caching exists and what `cached`/age mean, so that I caveat time-sensitive answers instead of asserting stale numbers as current
13. As the Atlas agent, I want a bypass-cache input scoped to explicit user requests for fresh data, so that I can honor "right now" questions without wrecking the hit rate
14. As a chat user whose colleague just refreshed a shared query, I want that refresh to re-freshen the shared entry, so that everyone on the same key benefits immediately
15. As a chat user of a cross-group (fanout) question, I want per-leg cache signals reported honestly, so that an all-cached composite answer doesn't masquerade as a fresh zero-second query
16. As a workspace admin tightening RLS, I want pre-change cached rows to become instantly unservable, so that the policy I just saved is enforced the moment I save it
17. As a compliance reviewer, I want one written principle for what governance is baked into cached rows vs re-evaluated per hit, so that cache behavior under policy change is auditable by design rather than by archaeology
18. As a plugin author with a `beforeQuery` governance hook, I want my rejection to apply to warm cache hits too, so that an incident lockdown can't be bypassed by previously-cached queries
19. As a plugin author with an `afterQuery` hook, I want its live-executions-only semantics documented, so that I don't build egress accounting on an assumption the cache silently breaks
20. As a workspace admin, I want to flush only my organization's cache entries, so that fixing my stale data never coldstarts other tenants
21. As a workspace admin, I want the flush confirmation to show my org's entry count, so that the number I'm confirming is the number I'm deleting
22. As a platform admin, I want fleet-wide flush as a platform-only verb with an explicit blast-radius disclosure, so that region-wide coldstart is a deliberate operator action, not a tenant misclick
23. As a SaaS operator, I want org deletion and residency migration to purge exactly the affected org's entries, so that tenant offboarding never degrades every other tenant's performance
24. As a SaaS operator, I want tenant admins to see only their own org's cache stats, so that fleet-wide counters stop leaking a cross-tenant activity signal
25. As a workspace admin, I want a last-hour hit rate alongside the since-labeled lifetime rate, so that I can tell whether my TTL is right *now* rather than averaged since boot
26. As a workspace admin who just flushed, I want the stats to visibly respond (window rate moving, entry count at zero), so that I can tell the flush worked
27. As a workspace admin, I want my stats to survive a TTL/maxSize change, so that tuning a knob doesn't erase the evidence I was tuning against
28. As a workspace admin, I want to see what's actually cached for my org — age, row count, connection, a SQL preview — so that "the cache" stops being an opaque number
29. As a workspace admin, I want to delete a single cache entry, so that fixing one stale dashboard number doesn't require flushing everything of mine
30. As a workspace admin, I want a refused flush (cache disabled) to render as an error with the reason, not a green "Flushed 0 entries" banner, so that the UI never reports failure as success
31. As an SDK consumer, I want a refused flush to be a structural 409, so that my client can't mistake refusal for success without parsing a body flag
32. As a trial admin on first visit, I want a warming/empty state instead of "0.0% hit rate" over an empty bar, so that a brand-new cache doesn't read as a broken one
33. As a keyboard/screen-reader user, I want the disabled-flush explanation reachable without a mouse, so that I learn *why* the button is disabled
34. As a non-engineer workspace admin, I want TTL and fill-gauge jargon explained in place, so that the page is legible without a glossary
35. As a datasource-plugin author, I want an async `CacheBackend` contract, so that the advertised Redis/Memcached backend is actually buildable without blocking the event loop
36. As a plugin author implementing an external backend, I want scope (org/connection) part of the contract, so that my backend supports org-scoped flush with the same semantics as the built-in LRU
37. As a platform admin who installed a cache plugin with a broken backend, I want the plugin to fail init visibly (red in plugin health) while queries keep working on the in-process LRU, so that I know I'm not on Redis and nothing is silently down
38. As an operator reading the docs, I want the caching guide to be accurate about audit behavior, tuning surfaces per deploy mode, and flush scope, so that the docs never instruct me to do something my deployment can't

## Implementation Decisions

All vocabulary per CONTEXT.md § Query Cache; governance per ADR-0033. Decisions from the 2026-07-10 grill (register appended to the audit doc):

- **Knobs move to the settings registry.** Cache enabled + TTL are workspace-scoped (workspace > platform > env > default); max size is platform-scoped (it budgets one shared per-region LRU). Hot-reload semantics: a `ttl`/`maxSize` change recreates/resizes the backend, and reported stats derive from the resolved settings — no constructor-frozen decorative values. Counters carry across recreation.
- **The config-file `cache:` block is deprecated two-phase.** Release N: block present → loud boot warning, values ignored; release N+1: schema removal. The SaaS deploy-config pin is deleted in the same change. This dissolves the env-shadowed-by-config-block trap — one documented precedence chain with the registry's visible `source`, no bespoke tier.
- **Hit surfacing.** The hit response gains a cache-age field (from the entry's stored write timestamp); the result card renders "cached · Xm ago"; fanout propagates per-leg cache/masking signals instead of hardcoding them false. The executeSQL tool description documents caching, the `cached` flag, and the age field.
- **Bypass.** executeSQL gains a bypass-cache input, described as "only when the user explicitly asks for fresh/current data." Bypass skips the read but keeps the write, so the fresh result re-freshens the shared entry. Governance-safe by construction: the live path re-runs every gate, so bypass costs performance only.
- **Governance principle (ADR-0033).** The resolved RLS configuration hashes into the cache key alongside org, connection, SQL, and claims — an RLS change orphans pre-change entries by construction (rejected alternative: event-based flush-on-settings-change). Plugin `beforeQuery` dispatch moves above the cache check (a veto blocks warm hits; a rewrite lands in the key). `afterQuery` and connection SLA metrics stay live-path-only, documented as observing executions. The claims serialization also gets the recursive canonical fix and an unstated-invariant sentence + test for the no-org/no-claims key collapse (#4532, L9).
- **Scoped invalidation joins the `CacheBackend` contract.** `set()` takes org/connection scope tags; a flush-by-org operation joins the contract; the LRU implements it with an org→keys side index kept consistent across set, delete, eviction, TTL expiry, and flush. Per-connection flush falls out by filtering an org's entries. Org deletion and residency migration switch from nuclear flush to exact-scope purge.
- **The flush contract.** Tenant admin flush is org-scoped and shows the org's own entry count. Fleet-wide flush is platform-admin-only with a one-sentence blast-radius disclosure in its dialog. No cooldown machinery — the dangerous verb is simply no longer tenant-reachable. A refused flush returns 409 (not 200 with a body flag), and the page branches on the typed body into an error surface.
- **Stats bucket by org.** Each bucket carries a since-labeled lifetime hit rate plus a last-hour rate via two-generation lazy rotation (two integers per bucket, no ring buffer). No reset verb. Workspace admins see their org's bucket; platform admins see fleet totals + resolved config. Stats and the entry list lazily drop expired entries so the fill gauge never counts corpses.
- **The cockpit.** Workspace enable/TTL knobs render inline on the cache page via the established dedicated-surface pattern (hidden from generic settings, writable through the page). An entry-inspection table lists the org's entries (age, row count, connection, ~200-char SQL preview stored on the entry) with per-entry delete. Honest states: deploy-mode-aware disabled state with the actual toggle, warming/empty state on fresh boot, no placeholder-zero stat cards when disabled. Accessibility sweep: keyboard-reachable disabled-button explanation, description text on jargon stats. Design-pass note: the org index makes live entry ordering by recency/hit-count cheap — the entry table is a candidate for a distinctive "entries bubbling" treatment in the impeccable pass.
- **The plugin backend contract goes fully async** (get/set/delete/flush/flush-by-org/stats), one breaking change bundled with the scope additions. The LRU wraps trivially; call sites await. The phantom-hit failure mode dies structurally (a Promise is now the expected shape). Backend registration validates shape; a failing backend **fails the plugin's init** (visible in plugin health) while the cache degrades to the in-process LRU. The contract-violating test stub and the "e.g. Redis" docblocks are fixed to the new contract.
- **Docs corrections land with the slices they describe:** cache-tuning guidance moves to the self-hosted tree with a settings-registry path for SaaS; flush-scope and blast-radius semantics documented; the restart-required caveat deleted once hot-reload lands; the agent-path-only caching scope and structurally-low hit-rate expectation get one sentence each; the replica-count cap rationale gains the cache as a second reason. (The already-false 0ms-audit-log claim was fixed during the grill.)

## Testing Decisions

Good tests pin external behavior at the highest existing seam — tool results, route responses, backend contract — never internal call order or index bookkeeping.

- **executeSQL tool seam** (mocked connection via the shared connection-mock helper; prior art: the sql-cache audit suites): age present on hits, bypass skips read/keeps write, RLS-config change → miss, `beforeQuery` rejection blocks a warm hit, rewrite changes the key, fanout per-leg cache signals, nested-claims regression.
- **Admin route seam** (prior art: the admin-cache route suite, upgraded to run against a **real** LRU backend instead of mocking the cache module wholesale): org-scoped vs platform flush authorization, 409 refused flush, org-bucketed stats shape (lifetime + window + since), entry list scoping, per-entry delete authorization.
- **LRU backend unit seam** (prior art: the existing cache suite): side-index consistency across set/evict/expiry/delete/flush-by-org, two-generation window rotation, counters carried across recreation, lazy expiry in stats/list.
- **Plugin lifecycle seam** (prior art: the effect-lifecycle suite): shape-invalid backend fails plugin init and surfaces in health while the LRU keeps serving; a conforming async backend is accepted and awaited.
- **New seam — cache config-resolution tests** using the existing reset hook + settings mocks: the registry precedence matrix (workspace > platform > env > default), backend recreation on knob change, deprecation boot warning when a config block is present. This closes the audit's zero-coverage finding on the resolution singleton.
- **Web**: the cache page stays on shared admin plumbing (`useAdminFetch`/`useConfigForm` with schema parsing); the wire contract is carried by route tests; browser coverage optional, after functional slices.
- Isolated-runner discipline throughout (`bun run test`, mock-all-exports, no top-level singleton mutation).

## Out of Scope

- **Shipping a Redis/Memcached backend plugin** — this PRD makes it buildable (async + scoped contract, #2055's seam) but does not build it
- **Multi-replica cache correctness** (#2069) — the single-replica assumption stays; this PRD only adds the cache to the replica-cap rationale so a future cap-lift can't miss it
- **Byte-based memory accounting / per-entry size caps** (audit M6) — entry-count remains the bound; stays tracked in the audit for a future hardening pass
- **Key normalization beyond trim** (audit L8) — structurally low hit rates get a doc sentence, not a semantic-fingerprint project
- **Caching for dashboard/metrics/REST execution paths** (audit L10) — agent-path-only stays; documented, not changed
- **#4532 and #4533** — filed independently; this PRD assumes the nested-claims serialization fix merges with or before the key/governance slice

## Further Notes

- **Sequencing (from the grill register):** (1) registry knobs + config-block deprecation, (2) key/governance per ADR-0033 (RLS-in-key, `beforeQuery` ordering), (3) `CacheBackend` contract redesign (async + scope + org index) — one breaking change, (4) cockpit (org-bucketed stats + window, org-scoped flush, entry table, inline knobs, honest states), (5) hit surfacing + bypass. Slices 1, 2, and 5 are independent of 3; slice 4 depends on 3.
- **Retirements this PRD performs:** the config-file `cache:` block (two-phase), the env-var copy on the disabled page state, the fleet-wide tenant flush, the lifetime-only counters, the sync `CacheBackend` contract and its contract-violating test stub, and the docs' restart-required tuning caveat.
- Lineage: elevation audit `.claude/research/admin-cache-audit-2026-07-10.md` (+ grill-outcomes register) → CONTEXT.md § Query Cache + ADR-0033 → this PRD → `/to-issues`.

items.body:
<!-- pm-packet:pm-flows-schedules-recovery -->

Preparation revision: full-r4. Planning specification. Publication does not establish specification readiness or authorize PM feature implementation.

**Specification blocked: immutable implementation context required.** Publication does not authorize PM implementation. Implementation remains held.

Existing milestone: M9 — Add Temporal schedules, controlled recovery and fairness (number 10); actual assignment must be read back at publication.

## Outcome

One schedule authority, unique occurrences, overlap/misfire/catchup/DST policy and CAS updates; replay-safe rollout and cancel/resume preserve accepted specifications.

## Why this is needed

Schedules and recovery need one orchestration authority and stable occurrences so retries, DST and worker rollout cannot duplicate effects.

## Scope and approach

- Validate explicit DAG producers and independent branches.
- Use Temporal schedules with stable occurrence/RequestId/CAS identity and complete-run overlap.
- Exercise grant revocation, fairness, replay-safe deployment and truthful cancellation drain.

## Essential planning context

Temporal alone owns schedule timing: restricted day-of-month/day-of-week use AND, UTC/IANA zones, daylight-saving missing-time skip and BOTH repeated fall instants. Preserve selected UTC, overlap SKIP, 1h catchup and zero jitter; SKIP covers the full run. These source policy values are distinct from test fixture values.

Scheduled workflow begins effect-free; first activity admits one occurrence and adopts existing execution. It must not trigger a second API-origin start.

Fairness requires explicitly enabled Temporal matching plus shared PostgreSQL tenant/account admission; queue count alone cannot prove quiet-workspace progress.

PF07 owns two separate PG transactions. Schedule mutation checks If-Match and commits desired revision, audit and outbox; post-commit relay uses Temporal describe conflict token and persisted RequestId for that exact payload. Occurrence admission atomically inserts unique (schedule_id, nominal_UTC_instant), immutable RunSpec/grant/budgets/audit and binding-outbox before effects. It adopts the already-running scheduled execution, never another StartRun. A directed acyclic graph (DAG) has explicit producers; compare-and-swap (CAS) rejects stale revisions.

## Dependencies and ownership

- Blocked by [pm-reverse-etl-settlement](https://github.com/polymetrics-ai/pm-cli/issues/34): Immutable workset and attempt identity precede dispatch; distinguish success/rejection/unknown per member, reconcile ambiguous effects, and never infer member success from counts alone.

Blocking capabilities use verified issue identities below. All intended packet references resolve to verified identities; later consumers are not blocking prerequisites.

| Action | Path | Owned interfaces / responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CREATE | `internal/app/flows.go` | Own flows behavior within app; bounded role: Typed flow DAG validation and PG resource admission only; Temporal owns schedules and execution. |
| CREATE | `internal/app/admission_limits.go` | Own admission limits behavior within app; bounded role: Typed flow DAG validation and PG resource admission only; Temporal owns schedules and execution. |
| CREATE | `internal/store/migrations/postgres/0006_schedules_flows.sql` | Ordered PostgreSQL migration 0006_schedules_flows.sql: create/alter only named PM-owned state, constraints and scoped grants. |
| CREATE | `internal/store/schedules.go` | Own schedules behavior within store; bounded role: Schedule desired/applied revisions, occurrence uniqueness, flow snapshots and mutation outbox. |
| CREATE | `internal/store/flows.go` | Own flows behavior within store; bounded role: Schedule desired/applied revisions, occurrence uniqueness, flow snapshots and mutation outbox. |
| CREATE | `internal/httpapi/flows.go` | Own flows behavior within httpapi; bounded role: Create/inspect/trigger/pause/resume API |
| CREATE | `internal/httpapi/schedules.go` | Own schedules behavior within httpapi; bounded role: Create/inspect/trigger/pause/resume API |
| CREATE | `internal/cli/flows.go` | Own flows behavior within cli; bounded role: Typed flow/schedule commands |
| CREATE | `internal/cli/schedules.go` | Own schedules behavior within cli; bounded role: Typed flow/schedule commands |
| CREATE | `internal/app/flows_test.go` | TestExplicitDAGAndIndependentFailures |
| CREATE | `internal/temporal/schedule_test.go` | TestUniqueOccurrenceDSTMisfire |
| CREATE | `internal/app/admission_limits_test.go` | TestAccountFairnessAndBackpressure |
| CREATE | `internal/app/cancel_test.go` | TestCancelGracefulDrainTruth |
| CREATE | `internal/temporal/schedules.go` | ApplyScheduleCAS |
| CREATE | `internal/temporal/deployment.go` | ConfigureDeployment |
| CREATE | `internal/workflows/replay.go` | ReplayHistories |
| CREATE | `internal/store/schedule_mutations.go` | Own schedule mutations behavior within store; bounded role: Temporal schedule CAS/provenance, worker deployment versioning and immutable schedule mutation dispatch identity. |
| CREATE | `internal/store/occurrences.go` | Own occurrences behavior within store; bounded role: Temporal schedule CAS/provenance, worker deployment versioning and immutable schedule mutation dispatch identity. |
| CREATE | `internal/app/schedules.go` | Own schedules behavior within app; bounded role: PG resource permits and current grants, schedule admission and revoked-run control; no custom timer loop. |
| CREATE | `internal/temporal/schedule_cas_test.go` | TestScheduleMutationCAS |
| CREATE | `internal/temporal/occurrence_test.go` | TestScheduledAdmissionAndOverlap |
| CREATE | `internal/temporal/replay_test.go` | TestDeploymentReplayAndRetirement |

| CREATE | `internal/app/revocation_test.go` | TestSessionExpiryVersusRunRevocation |

Explicit integration ownership in this packet: `internal/httpapi/routes.go`, `internal/activities/register.go`. Bind this issue's owned public routes/handlers to the existing composition roots; registered positive/denied request and absent-handler zero-I/O case are mandatory. Client presentation does not establish reachability. UPDATE after first owner merged; preserve its contract and serialize any overlapping integration edit.

Later consuming packets: [pm-initial-five-composition-proof](https://github.com/polymetrics-ai/pm-cli/issues/41). Their integration and proof remain open; passing this packet does not close them.

## Acceptance rules

- [ ] `pm-flows-schedules-recovery-V44`: Reject cycles, missing or multiple producers. Preserve query rows as artifacts; a failed branch blocks only descendants while independent work completes.
- [ ] `pm-flows-schedules-recovery-V45`: Temporal schedule DOM/DOW AND, UTC/IANA timezone, DST gap skip and BOTH fall folds; repeated admission produces one run per schedule/UTC instant. Explicit1h catchup and overlap SKIP cover complete run lifetime.
- [ ] `pm-flows-schedules-recovery-V46`: Two worker replicas and connection aliases share PG provider-account permits; explicitly enabled Temporal fairness and bounded units avoid starvation. Unknown dispatched work retains budget; queue limit alone cannot satisfy test.
- [ ] `pm-flows-schedules-recovery-V47`: Cancel stops new claims. Known completed subsets stay partial; uncertain dispatched effects remain unknown/reconciling after drain. No implicit rollback.
- [ ] `pm-flows-schedules-recovery-R19`: Concurrent If-Match edits, lost reply, rebased payload and out-of-order tombstone delivery cannot resurrect an old revision. Describe token and exact dispatch RequestId distinguish retry from rebase.
- [ ] `pm-flows-schedules-recovery-R20`: Temporal starts effect-free scheduled workflow, first activity admits occurrence once then adopts existing execution. Denied grant sends no effects; duplicate trigger/revision collision does not create another run; overlap spans actual run.
- [ ] `pm-flows-schedules-recovery-R21`: Histories at approval/retry/unknown/rollover replay under proposed version; old worker retained for pinned open runs; unsafe command change fails replay and rollout.
- [ ] `pm-flows-schedules-recovery-R22`: Explicit matching fairness plus PG tenant/account admission sustains bounded progress for quiet workspace during noisy neighbor load; queue-specific limit cannot bypass shared provider cooldown.
- [ ] `pm-flows-schedules-recovery-R23`: Logout/short-lived session expiry leaves accepted grant usable. Explicit principal/run/delegation/membership/connection/approval revocation stops future sends; restricted read-only reconciliation handles already-dispatched unknowns without new write permission.

## Required examples and verification

All PM tests are UNEXECUTED. Standard Go tests and table subtests are the default; Gherkin is a specification notation, not Godog adoption. Future implementation needs a causal RED, GREEN and refactor record. Missing required cases, zero selection, unexpected skips, or compile-only success cannot close a behavior rule. Documentation uses inspections. Controlled fakes and Temporal SDK tests do not prove real distributed durability or live provider behavior.

### pm-flows-schedules-recovery-E01 — Ada validates and runs the DAG

```gherkin
Given in workspace alpha, a flow contains explicit artifact producers and independent branches
When Ada validates and runs the DAG
Then cycles, missing or multiple producers fail; query rows remain artifacts and a failed branch blocks only descendants.
```

Acceptance: `pm-flows-schedules-recovery-V44`. Validation: V44.

| Required case | Variation | Observable result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| pm-flows-schedules-recovery-E01-C01 | Independent branch | Can finish despite sibling failure. |

Fixture: in workspace alpha, a flow contains explicit artifact producers and independent branches. Fault/variation: Independent branch. Evidence: scoped Go test or prelaunch qualification / Planned controlled fixture; no PM execution observed. Proof owner: [pm-flows-schedules-recovery](https://github.com/polymetrics-ai/pm-cli/issues/35). UNEXECUTED.

Proposed binding: `internal/app/flows_test.go` :: `TestExplicitDAGAndIndependentFailures`. Create this first-owned test/entrypoint; later consumers do not close this obligation.

Planned command or inspection (not run):

```text
set -eu
go test ./internal/app -run '^TestExplicitDAGAndIndependentFailures$' -count=1 -timeout 5m
```

### pm-flows-schedules-recovery-E02 — Ada admits the scheduled UTC occurrence

```gherkin
Given in workspace alpha, a schedule crosses DST gap/fold or missed trigger windows
When Ada admits the scheduled UTC occurrence
Then one run per schedule/UTC instant follows DOM/DOW AND, gap skip, both folds, 1h catchup and complete-run SKIP overlap.
```

Acceptance: `pm-flows-schedules-recovery-V45`. Validation: V45.

| Required case | Variation | Observable result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| pm-flows-schedules-recovery-E02-C01 | Duplicate trigger | Do not create another run. |
| pm-flows-schedules-recovery-E02-C02 | Spring missing wall time | Skip 2026-03-08 02:30 America/New_York with zero admitted occurrence. |
| pm-flows-schedules-recovery-E02-C03 | Fall repeated wall time | Use distinct nominal UTC keys 2026-11-01T05:30Z and T06:30Z, each at most once. |

items.title: Phase 3.5-B: Continuous CDP Decisions on shared compute
items.body:
## Assumptions

- Grill handoff ([ADR-043](docs/adr/043-cdp-webhook-first-spine-dual-credential.md), demo-ui-fix grill two-track section, CONTEXT Continuous CDP spine / Decision emission budget) is authoritative; no re-interview.
- **Blocked on A1 Speed ([#601](https://github.com/thienphung00/Juli-AI/issues/601))** — not on A0 alone, and **not** on A2 Batch ([#602](https://github.com/thienphung00/Juli-AI/issues/602)). Continuous Analytics path (material webhook → ETL → targeted fetch → KPI envelope → Demo Analytics) must advance `computed_at` for B′ five KPIs on Fujiwa Mock before this PRD starts.
- Indirect prerequisite: A0 ([#598](https://github.com/thienphung00/Juli-AI/issues/598)) medallion + serving gold shape (required by A1).
- **Fujiwa Mock Demo reference shop only** for 3.5-B prove-out; multi-tenant OAuth not in scope.
- **Track B Demo UI ([#600](https://github.com/thienphung00/Juli-AI/issues/600))** may ship UX contracts in parallel; **Decision feed freshness** depends on this Backend wire.
- Rules-based scoring only in 3.5-B; **rules → ML promotion** is Phase 4+ — do not block on trained models.
- Deep modules below match Architect intent; default tests cover Rules scoring wire, Decision emission budget, Action Card persistence on compute, Demo dry-run execution, and Public Demo Decision read API.

## Problem Statement

Phase 2.10 scoped Decisions on the same precompute spine as Analytics, but the **continuous** path — material shop events driving fresh KPI envelopes **and** fresh Decision candidates — is sequenced **after** Analytics-first delivery (ADR-043). Today Demo Decisions may still lag poll/manual refresh patterns or fixtures while Analytics moves toward webhook-first freshness via **A1 Speed**.

Sellers evaluating the Demo need recommendations that **match the same intelligence** as Analytics charts, surfaced at a **healthy cadence** (not spam on every webhook, not stale for weeks), with **safe dry-run execution** on the public site. Without wiring the existing Phase 2 rules pipeline to the **same compute trigger** as KPI precompute — plus an explicit **Decision emission budget** — the Decision loop does not prove the continuous CDP story product/GTM needs.

## Solution

Ship **Phase 3.5-B** as the **Decisions-next continuous CDP slice** on the shared spine **A1 Speed** establishes:

**Same compute trigger (material webhook / hourly Mock reconcile; daily staggered reconcile when A2 exists) → KPI precompute + rules scoring → Action Card candidates → emission budget (surfacing) → Demo Decisions read API → Demo dry-run approve/execute**

Key delivery themes:
1. **Shared compute trigger:** When shop-scoped fetch-then-precompute runs after material events or reconcile jobs, invoke **both** KPI envelope build **and** rules scoring — no parallel KPI formula path for Decisions; no Decision-only ingest pipeline.
2. **Rules scoring wire:** Reuse Phase 2 aggregates → signals → recommendations → rules copy → **persisted Action Cards**; triggered by continuous compute jobs — not only manual `POST /v1/action-cards/refresh`.
3. **Decision emission budget:** Cap **surfaced** Decisions separately from KPI freshness and from candidate recomputation — daily active-set cap, per-workflow cooldown after approve/dismiss/execute, soft weekly novelty quota (ADR-038 defaults).
4. **Demo dry-run execution:** Public Mock Demo Approve/execute persists local/demo execution records only — **no** reference merchant Partner writes; **must not** call `/v1/executions`, `enqueue_approved_tool`, or `run_tool_async`.
5. **Demo Decisions read API:** Unauthenticated GET for server-bound reference shop returns ranked, emission-gated Decision envelopes for Track B UI.

**Mock mode only:** Sign-in disabled; Fake Demo Refresh re-reads envelopes; real credentialed execution remains future Phase 3 Sign-in.

### Deep modules (by responsibility)

| Module | Responsibility | Public interface (words) |
|--------|----------------|--------------------------|
| **Shared Compute Orchestrator (Decision branch)** | After targeted fetch + transform, run KPI precompute **and** rules scoring in one shop job; inherit shop mutex / #68 coalesce from A1 | Single enqueue entry; shared inputs; independent freshness vs surfacing cadences |
| **Rules Scoring Wire** | Existing aggregates → signals → recs → copy → Action Card **candidates** on compute | Callable from continuous jobs; same formulas as manual refresh |
| **Decision Emission Budget** | Throttle which candidates **surface** to Demo active set | Active cap, per-workflow cooldown, weekly novelty gate; tunable config |
| **Action Card Persistence on Compute** | Upsert ranked candidates after scoring | Shop-scoped upsert by workflow_key; candidate vs surfaced states |
| **Demo Dry-run Execution** | Simulate Approve→execute without Partner writes | Isolated module; CI guard against Partner write clients |
| **Public Demo Decisions Read API** | Unauthenticated GET for emission-gated Decision list/detail | Server-bound reference shop; masked fields; no visitor shop_id |
| **Decision Feed Freshness Metadata** | Expose `computed_at` / promotion (`surfaced_at`) timestamps for UI trust copy | Align with Analytics envelope freshness semantics |

### Emission persistence design (Must — Executor must not invent)

Dual cadence requires **candidate recomputation ≠ surfacing**:

- Persist **candidates** after scoring even when budget suppresses surfacing (user story 11).
- Surfacing state must be queryable separately from “all scored rows” — e.g. status values `candidate` / `surfaced` / `suppressed` **or** equivalent columns (`surfaced_at`, `suppressed_reason`) on `action_cards` (or a thin `gold.decision_envelopes` serving projection). Pick one model in implementation; document in MODULE.md.
- Store weekly novelty counter / window state server-side (config + durable counter), not only in Redis.
- **Cooldown / indexes:** efficient cooldown lookup on terminal actions — e.g. composite index supporting `(shop_id, workflow_key)` + terminal timestamps (`approved_at` / `executed_at` / dismiss). Cap active surfaced set at config default **5**.

**Emission defaults (tunable, not immutable law):** max **5** active surfaced; **7-day** per-workflow cooldown after terminal action; soft weekly novelty **3**.

### Redis vs Postgres SoT (Must — same discipline as Envelope Cache)

- **Postgres is SoT** for Action Card **candidates**, emission/cooldown/novelty state, and dry-run execution records.
- **Redis is read-through only** for the **public emission-gated Decision list envelope** (optional performance layer) — **never SoT**.
- Do **not** treat Redis as the source of candidate or emission truth (ADR-038 / ADR-021 discipline: cache is never SoT).
- Last-good degradation: serve last-good **Postgres** (or last-good cached copy of gated GET) on scoring failure — cache miss must not invent empty “truth.”

### Shop compute mutex (Must)

Inherit A1 / ADR-038 shop-scoped mutex + #68 15-min coalesce for the **shared** KPI+scoring job. Scoring must **not** create a second Decision-only enqueue path that bypasses the mutex. Webhook bursts must not stampede scoring.

### Dry-run isolation (Must)

Public Demo approve/execute **must not** call `/v1/executions`, `enqueue_approved_tool`, or `run_tool_async`. Separate demo dry-run module; CI test proves no Partner write client import/call on that path.

### Public Demo Decision envelope contract (for #600 swap)

Emission-gated list: max active count, order, `computed_at`, per-card `surfaced_at` (or equivalent), masked fields, server-bound shop. Fixtures in #600 must match this shape so live swap needs no IA redesign.

## User Stories

1. As a **prospective seller (visitor)**, I want Demo Decisions to reflect the **same live shop intelligence** as Analytics charts, so that recommendations feel connected to what I just saw in KPIs.
2. As a **prospective seller**, I want Decisions to update after material shop events (orders, returns, inventory changes), so that advice responds to real commerce — not a static fixture list.
3. As a **prospective seller**, I want only a **bounded number of active Decisions** visible at once, so that I am not overwhelmed by optimization noise.
4. As a **prospective seller**, I want Decisions **not to churn** every few minutes when webhooks fire, so that I have time to act and Juli’s suggestions feel deliberate (emission budget).
5. As a **prospective seller**, I want to **approve** a Decision on the Demo without changing the real TikTok shop, so that the public Demo stays safe (dry-run).
6. As a **prospective seller**, I want post-approve execution to show **Juli handles the work** (progress narrative), so that the product story matches an execution platform — UI detail in Track B, freshness here.
7. As a **product / GTM lead**, I want the **Decision loop** provable on Fujiwa continuous spine, so that sales demos show Data → Decision → Approval → (dry-run) Execution.
8. As a **platform operator**, I want KPI envelope compute and rules scoring triggered by the **same shop jobs** as A1 Speed, so that we do not maintain duplicate ingest/compute paths.
9. As a **platform operator**, I want **KPI freshness** able to move faster than **Decision surfacing**, so that Analytics stays current without Decision spam (dual cadence — ADR-038).
10. As a **platform operator**, I want emission defaults (max **5** active Decisions, **7-day** per-workflow cooldown after terminal action, soft weekly novelty **3**) as tunable starting config, so that psychology has an agreed baseline.
11. As a **platform operator**, I want candidate Action Cards recomputed even when emission budget suppresses surfacing, so that promotion logic can catch up on next eligible window.
12. As a **backend engineer**, I want the rules scoring pipeline invoked from continuous compute without forking KPI math, so that charts and cards cannot drift.
13. As a **backend engineer**, I want threshold config for signals tunable without code deploy where practical, so that Decision volume can be balanced during prove-out.
14. As a **backend engineer**, I want Action Card upserts idempotent on `workflow_key` per shop, so that webhook bursts do not duplicate cards.
15. As a **backend engineer**, I want dry-run execution paths isolated from Partner write clients, so that public Demo never uses Fujiwa credentials for mutations.
16. As a **Demo UI implementer (Track B)**, I want Decision list/detail read API with stable envelope shapes and freshness metadata, so that UX polish can ship against live feed when this wire lands.
17. As a **Demo UI implementer**, I want emission-gated active set reflected in list ordering/count, so that UI does not show suppressed candidates as active.
18. As a **QA engineer**, I want tests proving compute enqueue → scoring → persisted candidates → emission filter → public GET, so that continuous Decisions are CI-verifiable with fixtures.
19. As a **QA engineer**, I want tests that emission budget blocks surfacing but allows recomputation, so that dual cadence regressions are caught.
20. As a **QA engineer**, I want tests that Demo approve/execute never calls Partner write endpoints or `/v1/executions`, so that dry-run safety is enforced.
21. As a **security reviewer**, I want public Decision reads bound to one server-configured reference shop, so that visitors cannot enumerate other tenants’ cards.
22. As a **security reviewer**, I want rules copy and card payloads free of raw financial PII beyond masked Demo contract, so that public responses stay safe.
23. As an **on-call engineer**, I want logs for scoring duration, emission drops (reason codes), and dry-run execution starts, so that Decision lag is diagnosable.
24. As an **on-call engineer**, I want last-good Decision envelopes readable when scoring fails, so that Demo degrades gracefully (Postgres SoT; Redis optional cache).
25. As a **product owner**, I want **rules-only** scoring in 3.5-B with a documented path to **ML promotion in Phase 4**, so that we do not delay continuous wire for model training.
26. As a **product owner**, I want Sign-in/OAuth and real credentialed execution explicitly deferred to Phase 3, so that scope stays Mock dry-run.
27. As a **future ML engineer**, I want scoring wire to accept promoted T2/T6/T8 techniques later without replacing continuous enqueue, so that ML is a swap-in behind the same trigger.
28. As a **Meta/release gate owner**, I want Demo Decision API changes covered by release-evidence when public surfaces change, so that deploy verification includes Decision feed smoke.
29. As a **visitor**, I want Decision copy in seller language (Track B contract) sourced from rules copy layer, so that cards read like Juli advice — not backend jargon.
30. As a **platform operator**, I want hourly Mock reconcile (A1) and — **when A2 exists** — daily staggered reconcile to refresh Decision **candidates** the same way as KPI envelopes, so that gap reconciliation heals Decision staleness too. **A2 is not a #599 exit gate.**

## Implementation Decisions

- **Phase boundary:** Phase 3.5-B is the **Decisions-next continuous CDP** Backend track — **blocked on A1 Speed (#601)** per [ADR-047](docs/adr/047-cdp-lambda-layers-prd-split.md); distinct from Track B Demo UI (#600) and from EXECUTION “Phase 3.5 Full Web Application.”
- **Architecture:** Reuse dual-layer shared precompute ([ADR-038](docs/adr/038-phase-2.10-dual-layer-pipeline.md)); Analytics-first then Decisions sequencing ([ADR-043](docs/adr/043-cdp-webhook-first-spine-dual-credential.md)); manual refresh pipeline callables reused on continuous trigger ([ADR-021](docs/adr/021-manual-refresh-pipeline-and-action-card-persistence.md)); Demo no-auth + dry-run ([ADR-037](docs/adr/037-phase-2.10-demo-real-data-no-auth.md)).
- **Compute coupling:** Extend **A1** shop jobs to call rules scoring after KPI precompute (same targeted fetch inputs); no second parallel fetch cycle for Decisions-only; inherit shop mutex.
- **Emission budget:** Separate **surfacing** from **recomputation**; persistence model + indexes required (see above); defaults per ADR-038 §6 — config tunable.
- **SoT:** Postgres for candidates + emission state; Redis read-through for public gated GET only.
- **Execution:** Demo dry-run module only — isolated from Partner write workers; real execution deferred to Phase 3 Sign-in / 3.5-D.
- **Credential model:** Mock **production_read** Fujiwa only; Sign-in disabled ([ADR-043](docs/adr/043-cdp-webhook-first-spine-dual-credential.md)).
- **ML path:** Phase 2 rules + copy only; ML promotion gates remain Phase 4.
- **UI boundary:** Track B owns suggestion glow, no confidence UI, editable inputs, Juli-handles-all confirm, progress cards, `/decisions` load fixes — this PRD delivers **feed freshness + backend contracts** only.
- **Interactions:** Material webhook / A1 hourly reconcile (/ A2 stagger when present) → shared compute → KPI envelopes + scoring → candidate upsert → emission filter → **optional Redis read-through** → public Demo Decisions GET; Approve on Demo → dry-run module only.

## Testing Decisions

- Test **external behavior:** Action Card candidates after compute jobs; emission budget suppresses active set but allows DB candidates; public GET returns gated list; dry-run never invokes Partner writes or `/v1/executions`; shared trigger runs both KPI and scoring (integration fixture).
- **Prior art:** action-cards refresh tests, scoring pipeline tests, Demo Decisions contract tests, webhook→compute patterns from A1.
- **Default modules under test:** Shared Compute Orchestrator (Decision branch), Rules Scoring Wire, Decision Emission Budget, Action Card persistence on compute, Demo Dry-run Execution, Public Demo Decisions Read API.
- **CI posture:** fixture-driven scoring and emission tests in PR-safe lane; optional live smoke on merge queue after A1 spine green.
- **Negative paths:** scoring failure leaves last-good cards; emission cooldown respects workflow_key terminal actions; approve on Demo does not enqueue real executor tasks with merchant credentials; Redis flush does not wipe candidate/emission SoT.

## Out of Scope

- **A0 Foundation** / **A1 Speed** continuous Analytics spine (prerequisites — [#598](https://github.com/thienphung00/Juli-AI/issues/598), [#601](https://github.com/thienphung00/Juli-AI/issues/601))
- **A2 Batch** fleet reconcile as an exit gate (may refresh candidates later; does **not** block this PRD)
- **Track B Demo UI fix** — trust copy, Decision automation UX polish, `/decisions` hang, contextual assistance format errors ([#600](https://github.com/thienphung00/Juli-AI/issues/600); may ship ahead of feed wire)
- TikTok OAuth, Sign-up, Sign-in, enabling Demo Sign-in control
- Real Partner write execution from public Demo (Login-mode credentialed execution — Phase 3+)
- Trained ML inference / T2/T6/T8 promotion as 3.5-B exit requirement (Phase 4)
- Cloud LLM copy (Haiku) — Phase 4
- Multi-tenant per-visitor shop connect
- Landing Page deploy
- Home/Settings real-data wiring
- Unlimited realtime Decision spam on every webhook (explicitly rejected)
- Separate Decision-only ingest pipeline parallel to Analytics spine
- Treating Redis as emission/candidate SoT (explicitly rejected)
- EXECUTION “Phase 3.5 Full Web Application” dashboard rebuild

## Further Notes

- **Blocking dependency:** Do not start 3.5-B implementation until **A1 Speed (#601)** deployed material handoff + KPI envelope continuous path is verified on Fujiwa Mock Demo (webhook-driven `computed_at` advances on Analytics for five B′ keys).
- **Rollout:** Enable scoring branch on compute jobs behind config flag if needed; verify Decision feed freshness correlates with Analytics envelope updates; coordinate Track B UI ship when feed stable.
- **Observability:** Log scoring invoke reason, emission drops (reason codes), active-set size, dry-run execution IDs; never log tokens/PII.
- **Risks:** Shared Mock snapshot — all visitors see same Decision set; emission budget may feel “slow” to internal testers — document as product intent; Track B UI may ship before feed — set seller expectations in Demo copy.
- **Follow-ups:** Phase 4 ML technique promotion behind same scoring wire; Phase 3 Sign-in real execution; Tune emission thresholds from Fujiwa prove-out data; A2 stagger refreshing candidates post-exit.

items.title: Wayfinder: close out the SUBSIDE UI SOW — TACC signs off on ui-react at mint.tacc.utexas.edu

labels.name: wayfinder:map
labels.description: Wayfinder map: the shared route for an effort

items.body:
## Destination

TACC uses `ui-react` at `mint.tacc.utexas.edu` in place of the Lit UI, and the client
manager signs off that the SOW's acceptance criterion (§8 — a model input's variable,
standard variable and unit configured in **one** form submission) is met.

That sign-off closes out the SOW. The map ends there.

## Notes

**Domain.** MINT / SUBSIDE model catalog. See [ADR-0002](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/blob/develop/docs/adr/0002-react-frontend-replaces-litelement-ui.md)
for the React migration and [ADR-0001](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/blob/develop/docs/adr/0001-model-catalog-postgres-hasura-over-fuseki-sparql.md)
for the Hasura backend it sits on. Both have a **Traps** section — read it before debugging
anything that looks like a permissions or cache bug.

**This map carries execution, not just decisions.** The remaining work is deploy-and-verify,
so tickets do the thing rather than only decide it.

**Contract.** The SUBSIDE model-catalog UI SOW with UT Austin / TACC. Its period of
performance has expired (confirmed not to be a blocker) and the engagement is settled
financially, so the only remaining obligation is delivery and sign-off.

Contract number, terms, amounts, billing status and client contacts are **deliberately not
recorded here** — this repo is public. They live in the private metalearn wiki. Keep them
out of this map and its tickets.

**Standing preferences for this effort**
- Deploy target is TACC's own small k8s cluster, via the MINT Helm chart. Max has `kubectl` access.
- `ui-react` **replaces** Lit at `mint.tacc.utexas.edu` (decided; T1 de-risks it).
- No UAT walkthrough document — TACC gets the URL (decided).
- Skills: `/grilling` and `/domain-modeling` on decision tickets.

**State at charting (2026-08-08).** Last code commit 2026-07-20; ~3 weeks idle. `ui-react` is
containerized and published, 21 routes ported, and has run only on Vercel previews and
localhost. OAuth2 has been exercised on previews and works — but previews use a dedicated
OAuth path for preview origins, so the round-trip at `mint.tacc.utexas.edu` is still unproven.
The app has never been driven against TACC's own Hasura and CKAN.

## Decisions so far

<!-- one line per closed ticket: gist + link -->

- [Confirm SUBSIDE can live without the un-ported Lit screens](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/69) —
  none are needed; the flip is free. Most are already dead or stubbed in Lit, Analysis and
  Emulators have no nav link, thread Summary turned out to be ported, and thread Visualize was
  never functional in Lit either. Also settled the rollout: **no parallel deploy** (no users on
  Lit at TACC), Vercel is the test surface, and Lit stays deployed-but-unrouted at the upgrade
  as the only undo, removed after sign-off.

- [Tag helm-charts 9.0.0-beta.3 and bump the submodule pointer off beta.2](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/70) —
  the chart is reachable again. `9.0.0-beta.3` tagged upstream on `3d3aca8`, submodule bumped
  in [#82](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/pull/82), merged to `develop` as `200a0d7`.
  Both confirmations held: `ui_react.enabled: false` by default, and the legacy `ui`
  component is untouched (values.yaml is +52/-0, no `ui*` template in the diff, `_helpers.tpl`
  append-only). Three facts fell out — `ui_react` needs an OAuth2 client **distinct** from
  Lit's (one callback URL per client, so reusing Lit's breaks the undo — sharpened
  [#73](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/73)); its image tag is a *monorepo* SHA
  the bump automation will silently skip, so it is hand-set; and it takes its **own host**
  rather than a path prefix, making the flip a host reassignment.

- [Verify CKAN from a browser origin against ckan.tacc.utexas.edu — is CORS actually broken?](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/71) —
  fine in production, broken on Vercel. CKAN echoes `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` **only** for
  `*.tacc.utexas.edu` (not the apex), `localhost` and `127.0.0.1`; every *other* CORS header is
  sent to everyone, so it looks enabled when it is not. `mint.tacc.utexas.edu` is allowlisted,
  so production needs nothing from TACC and nothing from us — which killed
  [#74](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/74) (the nginx proxy only serves the
  origin that already works, and never touches a preview), closed unopened. `*.vercel.app` got
  no header — **since fixed**: Max added the two real Vercel origins to CKAN's nginx map as
  anchored regexes and dropped the pre-existing `*.github.io` wildcard, verified live on every
  action the app calls plus the preflight. So
  [#76](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/76) runs wholly on the Vercel preview as
  originally written, `/datasets/*` included, **on the branch alias**
  `monorepo-git-develop-mosoriobs-projects.vercel.app` — per-deployment preview URLs are refused
  and cannot be allowlisted, since the hash changes every push. No public-suffix wildcard is left
  in the allowlist, which closes the credentialed-access concern the first fix opened.

- [Commit .env.example and local-setup notes so ui-react runs for someone who is not Max](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/72) —
  a `.env` file cannot configure the dev server. That was the finding, and it made the
  ticket's premise wrong. `index.html` always loads `public/env-config.js`, so the `VITE_*`
  fallbacks never run. The real fault was one line: `HASURA_ENDPOINT` pointed inside the
  cluster, at `graphql.mint.local`. It now points to TACC's public Hasura. A clone plus
  `npm install` plus `npm run dev` now shows real model catalog data, read-only, with no
  cluster access. I verified this live from a `localhost:3000` origin. The ticket also added
  `.env.example`, `npm run config:local` and a README section, and deleted
  `.env.development`. It deleted `MODEL_CATALOG_API`, which no code used. That left
  [#75](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/75) with a fixed list of 12 keys.
  `ENSEMBLE_MANAGER_API` must be set, or thread execution stops without an error. The code is
  in [PR #83](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/pull/83), **merged to `develop` as
  `45a6d7e`**.

- [Check whether the OAuth2 redirect URI for mint.tacc.utexas.edu is already registered](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/73) —
  **already registered; nothing to do at the IdP.** The premise was wrong: Lit uses
  `/oauth2/callback` too (`${window.location.origin}/oauth2/callback`, hardcoded), so both apps
  want the *identical* redirect URI. The IdP is **Tapis, tenant `portals`** — not Keycloak — and
  client **`mint`** has `callback_url` exactly `https://mint.tacc.utexas.edu/oauth2/callback`.
  Verified live, with negative controls, against `GET /v3/oauth2/authorize`, which validates
  `redirect_uri` *before* login: the match is exact on scheme, host and path (`http://` is
  rejected), and no `mint-*react*` client exists. Tapis really is one-callback-per-client, but
  the #70 inference that `ui_react` needs its own client does **not** follow — the two apps want
  the same URI and never serve the origin at once (Lit is unrouted). **Decision: reuse `mint`**,
  so there is no IdP change at flip *or* rollback. The chart's own text argues the opposite and
  is wrong for this rollout; it only hard-fails on an *empty* `client_id`, so `"mint"` renders —
  flagged on [#75](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/75). Two constraints landed on
  [#77](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/77): the host must be exactly
  `https://mint.tacc.utexas.edu`, and Lit must be **unrouted, never re-hosted** — parked at a
  second hostname it cannot log in, making it a rollback to a broken app. Also rules out a
  staging host for `ui-react` before the flip.

- [Settle the window.__MINT_CONFIG__ values for the TACC deployment](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/75) —
  **two values, not twelve.** The deployed Lit app publishes TACC's real config at
  `mint.tacc.utexas.edu/config.js`, so no value had to be guessed. Ten of the twelve keys need
  no statement: they derive from the component ingresses or inherit shared chart values TACC
  already overrides (`google.maps.key`, `welcome_message`). Only `client_id: "mint"` and
  `data_catalog_api: "https://ckan.tacc.utexas.edu"` must be set. Derivation is *proven* safe
  for Hasura and the Ensemble Manager rather than assumed — the Lit template and the `ui_react`
  helper share the same `ingress.tls` idiom, and Lit's live output shows `https://` for both, so
  TACC declares TLS and there is no mixed-content trap. CKAN is the exception: `ui_react` derives
  it from `components.data_catalog`, which TACC does not use (it uses `external_services.ckan.url`,
  read by the Lit template only), so the key is omitted and the app falls back to a compiled
  default that is right by coincidence — hence the override. Verified live from the production
  origin: Hasura and the Ensemble Manager both send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, the
  Ensemble Manager's `/v1` routes exist, and CKAN sets no `X-Frame-Options`, so the datasets
  iframe will render. Two facts landed on
  [#76](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/76) — `ui-react` needs **no** CKAN API key
  (Lit's `DATA_CATALOG_KEY` has no counterpart; all reads are anonymous GETs), and
  `ENSEMBLE_MANAGER_API` is now set, so thread execution is in scope for the smoke test. Three
  chart cleanups landed on [#77](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/77): the dead
  `MODEL_CATALOG_API` key, the wrong "must be a distinct client" text, and teaching
  `ui-react-config.yaml` to read `external_services.ckan.url`. None block the flip.

- [Ensemble Manager calls send no Authorization header — localStorage key mismatch](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/85) —
  fixed in [PR #87](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/pull/87), **merged to `develop` as
  `4f7debf`**.
  Both REST calls read the token by string literal from a key nothing writes, and spread the
  header conditionally, so every call went out anonymous with no error. The symptom is now known
  rather than guessed, from the Ensemble Manager source: against a **`tapis`** engine, which is
  what TACC runs, submit returns **500** ("Unauthorized" escapes as a plain `Error`) and logs
  return **401** — both read as server faults, not a missing credential. The probe could not
  settle this because `fetchLog` looks the execution up *before* it reads the header, so an
  unknown id 404s either way. Both calls moved into `src/lib/ensemble-manager.ts` so the header
  is built once; the tests assert the **outgoing header**, not the storage key, and were checked
  to fail against the old code. The fix exposed a second defect and did not resolve it:
  [#88](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/88) — `ui-react` posts to
  `/executionEngines/localex`, and the only such route is `/executionEngines/tapis`, so run
  submission 404s before auth matters. **Submission is still broken at TACC; the log call is
  fully fixed.**

- [ui-react submits runs to /executionEngines/localex, a route that does not exist](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/88) —
  **two faults, not one.** The engine name was wrong for TACC, and the route was wrong for every
  engine except Tapis: `server.ts` mounts `/executionsLocal`, `/executions` and
  `/executionEngines` as three separate routers, and the last registers `/tapis` only. So a
  config key alone would not have fixed it. The engine is now the config key
  `EXECUTION_ENGINE`, and `executionEnginePath` maps each backend to its real route — the same
  map Lit makes in `mint-runs.ts:731` — so the key is honest for all three engines. **The
  default is `localex`**, matching both the chart default for the Ensemble Manager and the Lit
  fallback, so one unset value describes the same deployment in three places. The results step
  needed nothing: `MintResults` reads the engine off the execution row, not from config, and its
  `localex`/`wings` rewrite is dead because `MintThread` never passes `mintConfig`. Code is in
  [PR #89](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/pull/89), **merged to `develop` as `1d1ada9`**.
  One constraint landed on [#77](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/77): the chart must
  emit `EXECUTION_ENGINE: tapis` for TACC, derived the way `ui-config.yaml` derives Lit's — a
  prerequisite for run submission, not a cleanup. **Both halves confirmed live on
  [#76](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/76):** TACC's Ensemble Manager publishes
  exactly the three separate mounts predicted here, and its Lit config sets
  `REACT_APP_EXECUTION_ENGINE = "tapis"`.

- [Smoke-test ui-react against TACC's real Hasura and CKAN](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/76) —
  **the §8 acceptance criterion passes, for a new input.** Signed in as `mosorio@portals`, a new
  model input took label + standard variable (`soil__porosity`) + unit (`m3 m-3`) in **one**
  submission against TACC's live catalog. The form is genuinely flattened — one control for
  standard variable *and* unit, which offers the units already used with the variable chosen. The
  cmdk trap ADR-0002 warns about could not apply: this picker is plain buttons, not cmdk. Verified
  anyway by hit test and a real mouse click. Run on **`localhost:3000`, not the Vercel preview** —
  the preview is behind Vercel SSO, and `localhost` is CKAN-allowlisted with a working OAuth
  client, so it tests strictly more. **Editing an existing input fails**, and that is
  [#91](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/91), now blocking
  [#77](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/77): the junction upsert names a column this
  repo's own metadata never exposes, so it is not TACC-specific, and it half-applies. A second,
  minor fault rides along — a *successful* save renders stale until a manual reload. Thread
  execution was carved out as [#92](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/92) rather than
  fired at the client's cluster unasked. `/modeling/*` renders against real data; note the region
  filter defaults to **California, where TACC has nothing** — it reads as an empty deployment until
  you switch to Texas. All test rows were removed; TACC's catalog is back to its prior state.

- [Editing an existing model input fails: the junction upsert names a column Hasura does not expose](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/91) —
  **fixed and verified live; the write surface is a `graphql_engine` question, not a TACC one.**
  Client-only, so nothing to apply to TACC's Hasura. `SetConfigurationInputOptional` replaces the
  upsert with `delete_by_pk` + `insert_one` in **one document** — Hasura runs a mutation's root
  fields in a single transaction, so the row is never left missing — and it now fires **only when
  `is_optional` changed**, instead of for every row in `toUpdate`. Proven under a real Tapis token
  with a zero-write probe: validation precedes execution, so the old document returns
  `validation-failed` (the exact `_PLACEHOLDER` error) and the new one reaches execution. **Why
  nothing caught it:** `generated/schema.graphql` is the *admin* schema, where the column is
  updatable — codegen and all 760 offline tests validate against a schema the app never runs as.
  Treat any role-sensitive write as unverified until it runs under a real token. Fault 2 fixed too:
  the form refetches `GetConfiguration` before `onSaved`, so a save no longer renders stale.
  End-to-end on `simpleModelAnnotated` — add, edit label, toggle Optional — all clean, and the
  catalog was returned to its exact prior state. Code in
  [PR #93](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/pull/93). One thing deliberately **not** fixed:
  the save is still many mutations, not one transaction, so a mid-sequence failure still
  half-applies. No step on this path can fail that way now; ticket it if TACC hits it.

- [Thread datasets: ui-react searches CKAN free text instead of the mint_standard_variables field](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/94) —
  **fixed and verified live: 3 of 40 annotated variables → 40 of 40.** Client-only; nothing to
  change at TACC. `findDatasets` no longer sends a `q` at all — `packagesMatchingVariables` keeps
  the packages whose *resources* carry the variable, as Lit does. The ticket's premise was
  re-measured first and held. **Three defects the ticket did not name, each real:** resource
  narrowing was mandatory, not cosmetic — a dataset matches because *some* of its resources carry
  the variable, and one TACC package holds **35 resources, 1 of which** does, so binding all of
  them handed the model input files it cannot read; `datatype` was read off the first resource,
  which `MintDatasets` then filters the list on; and `rows=1000` was a silent cap, now paged.
  **Two existing fixtures encoded the bug** — they carried no annotation and passed only because
  the old code matched prose. Code in [PR #95](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/pull/95),
  CI green. **#92 is unblocked**, with one constraint landed on it: `ext_bbox` drops any package
  with no spatial extent, and **11 of TACC's 33** annotated packages have none — Texas keeps 16 of
  33, the California default keeps **0**. Lit behaves the same, so it is not a regression, but a
  region-scoped thread cannot see a third of the annotated catalog — **now
  [#97](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/97)**. The same root cause survives
  on the browse surface as [#96](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/96), deliberately
  not fixed here.

- **Missing dataset metadata must not mean an invisible dataset** (decided 2026-08-09, no ticket
  of its own to close — it scopes [#97](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/97)). The
  four constraints on the Datasets step disagreed about what *unknown* means: the standard
  variable drops it (right), the datatype offers a "Show N" link, dates **keep** it, and the
  region **dropped it silently** — because `ext_bbox` filters on *having* a location, not on
  location. Region was also the only constraint on the server. **The rule is now two rules:**
  unknown extent is shown and badged, as dates already do; known-but-outside is hidden behind the

- [How does the MINT Helm chart pass an environment variable to ui_react?](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/204) —
  **It does not, and it cannot be made to from a values file.** The chart mounts one ConfigMap
  into `ui_react` with `envFrom`, and builds it from **ten hardcoded keys**
  (`charts/mint/templates/ui-react-config.yaml`). There is no `extraEnv` and no `range` over a
  values map, so an operator cannot add a variable — the chart itself must change. A second
  blocker sits at the other end: `ui-react/scripts/generate-env-config.mjs` copies only named
  keys through `pick()`, so it drops an unknown variable even when the pod carries it. A new
  runtime key therefore costs **three repositories**: `ui-react`
  ([#206](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/206)), then the chart and `dynamo`
  ([#207](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/207), filed on this answer and blocking
  [#77](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/77)). This is
  [#150](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/150) again, and #150's own fix is the
  template to copy: `EXECUTION_ENGINE` reads `$cfg.execution_engine` under
  `components.ui_react.config`, with a chart-derived default. Note the chart forwards its two
  optional keys by **two different routes** — `WELCOME_MESSAGE` reads top-level
  `.Values.welcome_message`, shared with the legacy UI. Follow `EXECUTION_ENGINE`; #81 retires
  the legacy UI. ~~One thing this could not settle: the chart version TACC actually runs.~~
  **Settled the same day, and the "unreadable" finding was wrong.** `dynamo` is cloned locally;
  its org is `In-For-Disaster-Analytics`, not `mintproject`, so `gh repo view mintproject/dynamo`
  fails and an agent searching only the `mintproject` org calls it unreadable. It is not. TACC
  **already pins `9.0.0-beta.10`**, the latest published chart, so #207 needs a *new* release
  rather than a catch-up bump. Two more facts came with it: `ui_react` is present in
  `values.yaml` but **`enabled: false`** with no `config:` key, so #207 and
  [#81](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/81) will edit the same five lines; and the
  checkout sits on an unmerged branch. Two habits worth keeping: **a private repo is not
  unreadable until you have looked on disk**, and a runtime config key is not shipped until you
  have read `env-config.js` inside the running pod.
