  repo's* metadata, not TACC's — so stop framing the write surface as a TACC unknown and read it
  as a `graphql_engine` question. **Now fixed, client-side, with no metadata change**, and the
  edit path verified live end to end. What stays unaudited is the rest of the `user` role's write
  permissions against what the client sends. **One slice of that has graduated:** the indicator write
  is built and proved on the dev cluster, but only under the **admin** role, so
  [#136](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/136) carries it to TACC and to the `user`
  role.
- ~~Whether TACC's catalog holds the ~303 standard variables and ~107 units the typeahead
  assumes.~~ **Settled on [#76](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/76):** TACC holds
  **668** standard variables and **129** units, counted by paging since `anonymous` has no
  `*_aggregate`. Both are well above the assumption.
- Defect turnaround once TACC starts testing — unknown volume, unknown appetite.
- ~~Whether anyone but Max can run the authenticated app outside production.~~ **Fixed.** Tapis
  client **`mint-localhost-3000`** now serves `http://localhost:3000/oauth2/callback` and is the
  repo's default `AUTH_CLIENT_ID`; `mint-local` keeps `http://mint.local/oauth2/callback` for the
  dev cluster. Clients are named after the origin they serve, since Tapis allows one callback per
  client. A real login on `localhost` succeeded — and immediately exposed
  [#85](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/85), a silent auth defect no amount of
  anonymous testing could have found — which in turn exposed
  [#88](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/88). One real login has now produced two
  defects; treat that as the rate to expect from the authenticated walkthrough.

- **The chart-rendered config has never been exercised, and it is not the config every
  walkthrough has used.** The dev cluster was flipped as a rehearsal on 2026-08-29:
  `helm upgrade` to `9.0.0-beta.5`, `mint.local` reassigned to `ui_react` (image `04c5b679`,
  client `mint-local`) and Lit moved aside to `legacy.mint.local`, still deployed as the undo.
  Both hosts serve the right app. That rehearsal immediately produced
  [#150](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/150), which **blocks #77**: the chart
  emits `REACT_APP_EXECUTION_ENGINE` for Lit and emits nothing for `ui_react`, which then
  defaults to `localex` while the deployment runs `tapis`. There is no values key to override
  it, so no deployment can currently be correct. This is #88 returning through configuration
  instead of code. The reason no earlier ticket saw it is worth keeping: **every authenticated
  walkthrough so far, #92 included, ran from localhost or Vercel against a hand-written
  `env-config.js`** — the chart's own config map has never been under a browser. Expect more of
  this class at the flip, and prefer a rehearsal on the dev cluster over reading the templates.
  One known limit of that rehearsal: CKAN allowlists `*.tacc.utexas.edu`, `localhost` and
  `127.0.0.1` only (#71), so dataset surfaces are CORS-blocked from `mint.local` and cannot be
  judged there. ~~#77 is back to two blockers, #110 and #150.~~ **#150 is fixed and the rehearsal
  paid for itself twice** — the same PR closed a second omitted key, `DATA_CATALOG_API`, which no
  reading of the template had caught either. The class is now named precisely: the failure is a key
  the chart *omits*, where the image's own default then decides, silently and sometimes correctly.
  Two of the twelve keys were in that state and both are now derived. ~~**#77 is down to one blocker,
  [#110](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/110)**~~ — but the chart-rendered config is
  still only proven on `mint.local`, so keep the habit: read the served `env-config.js` at the real
  host before believing the flip.
  **#110 is closed, and #77's one blocker is now
  [#136](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/136)** — which was not a flip *risk* until
  #110 tried to open a thread at TACC and found the page would not load at all. That is a third
  instance of the class this bullet names, and the sharpest: not a key the chart omits, but a
  **client change shipped without its migration**. #106 taught `GetThread` to read the indicator's
  `label`; TACC's `thread.response_variable` still points at the legacy `variable` table, which has
  `name`, and Hasura rejects the document at validation — so *every* thread page 500s, indicator or
  no indicator. Generalise the habit rather than the instance: **before the flip, walk the real
  host as a signed-in user, and treat any `graphql_engine` migration not yet applied at TACC as a
  live blocker until proven otherwise.**
  **A fourth instance closed on [#207](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/207), and it
  reverses the direction.** The first three were keys the *chart* omitted. This one is a key the
  **client's values file** omits, which the chart then fills from its own default — `AUTH_CLIENT_ID`
  renders `mint-local` at TACC, and the `ui_react` ingress renders `mint.local` with no TLS. A
  chart default is a sane value, so nothing looks wrong. The rule that catches both directions:
  **`helm template` the client's own values file with the component switched on, and read every key
  in the rendered ConfigMap against what that deployment needs.** #207 also retired the
  `BRANDING` unknown by the right method — the key is read from inside a running pod on the dev
  cluster, not from the template. ~~**#77 is again down to one blocker,
  [#136](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/136).**~~
  **This patch is now closed. The flip ran on 2026-09-12 and the rendered config was right the
  first time** — the render against TACC's own values predicted the deploy exactly (one ingress
  removed, four `ui_react` objects added), and the *served* `env-config.js` carries all twelve
  keys correctly. The rule this bullet built is what made it uneventful, so keep it for the next
  deployment rather than for this one: `helm template` the client's values with the component
  switched on, and read every key in the rendered ConfigMap. One addition from the flip itself:
  **read the served `env-config.js` at the real host, not the template and not the pod** — it is
  the only artifact the browser actually runs.

## Out of scope

- **Porting the un-ported Lit screens** — Analysis, Emulators, Messages,
  `models-compare`/`models-calibrate`/`models-cromo`, thread Visualize, and the 3,256-LOC
  `model-view`. (Thread Summary was on this list in error — it is ported.) Never in the SOW,
  whose scope is the config workflow and the flattened form.
  [T1](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/69) confirmed SUBSIDE can live without
  them; it does not port them.
- **Retiring `ui/` entirely.** Downstream of the above, and a separate effort.
- **ISI's `mint.isi.edu` cutover.** Different host, different stakeholders, not this contract.
- **ADR-0001 leftover debt** — old `model`/`model_io`/`model_parameter` tables, Fuseki
  references in docker-compose and CI, absent row-level security on `modelcatalog_*`.
- **Issue #35** (results post-processing, indicator comparison across a run ensemble) — a
  feature, not migration work.
- **A written UAT walkthrough.** Considered and declined; TACC gets the URL.
- **The same model-type fault in `model-catalog-api`** —
  [#102](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/102): `/models` returns 44 of TACC's 55
  software from a stale subtype allowlist, and four `custom-handlers.ts` handlers are cut harder
  still, to 27. Real and measured, surfaced while resolving
  [#98](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/98). Out of scope because nothing on the path
  to sign-off touches it: `ui-react` talks to Hasura directly and never calls that API (#72 deleted
  the dead `MODEL_CATALOG_API` key), and the only consumer is the Lit UI, which stays unrouted and
  is being retired. Filed so it is not lost.
- **A ZIP component cannot run on Tapis** —
  [#108](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/108): the Ensemble Manager's Tapis path
  JSON-parses `has_component_location`, so a model whose component is a `localex` ZIP (HAND) fails
  with an opaque 500. Surfaced on the first attempt at
  [#92](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/92) and proved by negative control — the
  same 500, byte for byte, with the input dataset swapped. Out of scope because it is
  pre-existing server behaviour, Lit hits it identically, and nothing on the path to sign-off
  needs a ZIP component: #92 finished by choosing a Tapis-backed model instead. It does not
  block #77.
- **The Ensemble Manager rejects standard-variable indicators** —
  [#137](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/137): `POST /v1/problemStatements/*/subtasks`
  validates `response_variables` and `driving_variables` against the legacy `variable` table, so
  after #106 it refuses every id a client can legally store. Out of scope because `ui-react` never
  calls that route — it writes threads through Hasura — and the only consumer is the Lit UI, which
  stays unrouted and whose Variables screen renders zero options anyway. The inconsistency predates
  the migration. Filed so it is not lost.
- **Three smaller defects found while resolving #92**, all filed and none on the route to
  sign-off. [#109](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/109) — every execution row is
  written `execution_engine: localex`, including Tapis runs; the server does not read the column,
  so nothing breaks today. [#111](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/111) — the Runs
  step prints `2 runs (1 input resources × 1 parameters)`; the count is right and only the printed
  factor is wrong. [#112](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/112) — every resource with
  an empty URL shares the id `d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e`, the MD5 of the empty string.
  #112 is the one to revisit if result registration ever starts writing resource rows.








































- **A MINT design system — TACC brand tokens across the whole app.** Charted 2026-08-31 and
  cut back to the chrome. `ui-react` renders the stock shadcn slate palette, and
  `tailwind.config.ts:14` wrongly calls those slate values "TACC brand tokens (stubs)".
  Repointing `--primary` recolours every button, badge and focus ring in the app, and nothing
  on the path to sign-off needs that. Adopting Lit's top nav in place of the sidebar is out for
  the same reason: it is a product decision, not a branding one.
  **The chrome half stayed in scope** — a branding strip, a footer and a dark header, behind a
  `BRANDING` runtime key that defaults to `none`
  ([#206](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/206)). ~~It blocks
  [#77](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/77)~~ — **built, carried and closed.**
  #206 shipped the chrome in `ui-react`; [#207](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/207)
  carried the key through the chart and `dynamo` and proved it in a running pod. The flip no longer
  drops the TACC and UT Austin logos that `mint.tacc.utexas.edu` shows today, which matters because
  [#80](https://github.com/mintproject/monorepo/issues/80) hands the client that URL. The rest of
  the design system stays out of scope.

items.body:
triage#1 · hotlong · session_01Q4EjjMnyLqJdzuktEmRPXH

**本贴是分诊席(objectstack 全仓,`ui/` 在内)的唯一权威登记。** 座位贴协议见 `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/seat-post-protocol.md`;岗位说明见 `references/lanes/triage.md` 与 `references/triage-duties.md`(本贴只放现值与指针,⛔ 不抄岗位说明)。

**状态源 = 本正文 + 晚于其最后编辑的评论**(每轮的 `## R<n> round record`)。⛔ 不是 Routine prompt;二者冲突时本贴赢,本贴与受管参考冲突时受管参考赢。

> **压缩说明(2026-11-01,维护者令「重写座位贴正文」):** 旧正文约 204 KB,超出中继 `issue_patch` 的 60,000 字节上限,且「当前 PM」一段仍写着 9 月的前任会话。全文已按接管压缩规则重述为下面四段现值。**旧账一字未删,在本贴的编辑历史里**:2026-11-01 改写之前的那一版 body revision(R+220 至 R+249 各班交接台账、平台事实实测、判据 (b) 九车道读数表等)。

## 当前 PM

_Body refreshed 2026-11-12T06:50Z (takeover; read window acknowledged through comment 6815918192: R1065–R1070 round records and the takeover marker, no unanswered knock)._

- **🟢 在任:** `session_01Q4EjjMnyLqJdzuktEmRPXH`,账号 `hotlong`(`GET /user`),effort `high`。2026-11-12T05:54Z 维护者在本会话强制接管:「前任 分诊没token了」「你接手」(接管标记评论 6815918192)。
- **前任:** `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U`(os-zhuang,2026-09-28 起值守),末份轮次记录 R1070(2026-11-12T03:04Z),无收班简报,断粮。其 Routine `trig_01NcnCtMS2tH46nUg1a5TaMJ` 不在本账号的 scheduled-task 列表里,本席停不了;若它在前任会话复活,先读本贴再动手。
- **唤醒:** `Patrol:` `trig_01377heGw9UoChYTLnz93qjo`(每小时 :43,自绑本会话),外加信箱与订阅 PR 事件。
- **信箱:** `Mailbox:` PR objectstack-ai/objectstack#32588(`pm:mailbox` · `pinned`,head `claude/clever-cannon-v6v4pd`,本会话已订阅)。旧信箱 #28646 已关。敲门:评论首行 `To: triage#1`,次行为 `references/project-forms.md` 〈信箱 PR〉的键之一。
- **范围与轮转:** objectstack 一仓(`ui/` 在内,`lanes/triage.md`)。每轮最旧优先,最旧未路由超 4 小时的卡本轮先清。每轮记录末行 `Next fire: objectstack.`。

## 继承台账

⛔ 逐卡状态在卡与 PR 上,本段只列本席的未了义务与指针(读数时现读,⛔ 不沿用本段的旧值)。

- **合约复审(本席持有,`CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`):** 每轮先跑 `node scripts/pm/check-owed-reviews.mjs`,按 `references/contract-review.md` (a)(b)(c) 接无人在审的欠审 PR。本席已在任的复审记录:#26517(Version PR,现 head `936de789` PASS)、#28554、#28587、#28650。头移即欠 delta 复审,归本席。
- **发版 18.3.0 观察项(只读,⛔ 本席不合并、不派发版工作流、不打 tag):**
  - RC 锚卡 objectstack-ai/objectstack#27377:P0 重跑 objectstack-ai/objectstack#28545,复测 objectstack-ai/objectstack#28656(13 项 11 PASS / 2 FAIL)。
  - 发版阻塞:#28657(审批请求页的决定在 action 门 404,p1 `domain:server`)。
  - 未过项:`studio-authoring.expression-editors`,父卡 objectstack-ai/objectstack#27482 未按卡面修完。
- **待维护者裁决(每轮重读,已裁即移出):** objectstack-ai/objectstack#27928(倾向 D)、#28085(是否 not planned 关闭,倾向是)。
- **本席立的流程卡:** objectstack-ai/objectstack#28675(信箱敲门场景表,`domain:skills`,串行在 objectstack-ai/objectstack#28642 之后)。
- **旧正文遗留清单不再继承:** 判据 (b) 的 R+219「九车道 41 张」读数表已由每轮 sweep(`d3` 段:有车道无 pm 态)取代;如需对账,读上一版 body revision。

## 热文件串行队

- **无。** 分诊席只写标签与审计评论,不开 PR、不认领(`lanes/triage.md`),没有热文件。

## 说明

**每轮程序(细则见 `triage-duties.md`):**
1. `ReadNotifications`。
2. 互斥:读本贴晚于上一份轮次记录的评论,有他席占座即退。
3. 健康:上份记录以来 main push(CI / Lint / Release)、merge_group 与 schedule 的全部结论,⛔ 只读完成的 run。
4. p0:立卡前先查已开的 `priority:p0` 防重。车道本轮认领;一轮无人认领则点名升级;再无人,分诊派止血。
5. sweep、unlock(放行前读卡面「Why it waits」,⛔ 只看卡号不够)、新卡定级。
6. 每条定级评论首行 `Path: <定义项> | none | P<step>` 或 `Path: none`。
7. `pm:retriage`、欠审复审(见上)。
8. 轮次记录贴本 issue,末行 `Next fire: <repo>.`;向维护者中文汇报。

**写入通道:** 一切 GitHub 写经 `scripts/pm/` 门(`post-stamped.mjs`、`fleet-write/dispatch.mjs`、`issue-create.mjs`、`mailbox-open.mjs`),以 `objectstack-fleet[bot]` 落笔,首行恒为署名行。⚠️ 正文守 60,000 字节上限。

**常设裁决(维护者原话,本班生效;收班时仍未写进 `lanes/triage.md` 的,随简报交维护者定去留,⛔ 不作继承裁决):**
- 「你只处理分诊哦」(p0 止血派发除外)·「用中文」·「需要我决裁的问题,立决策卡」。
- 定级(2026-11-12/13,取代旧条「协议新增定 p1」):按影响定级的四档表(#32906)+ 定序规则(#32997):影响档 → 可达折减(仅最高权限/宿主开发者低频动作或非默认部署降一档;越权、跨租户、不可恢复丢失不降;⛔ 无「无现用者」二档折减、⛔ 无读码证据上限)→ 至多一次上调(重点功能 MCP:错答/假绿/卡住无处方才升;或「真实用户可撞」)→ 发版窗 p0。维护者原话:「接受你的优先级建议」·「重点功能（ MCP）」·「只是读代码得出的最高 p2。这个没必要吧，我们的客户不多。」·「不需要限额，也不需要自动关。其他同意。」·「你现在就开始执行这个规则。」仍有效:「平台测试清单反复变红,肯定要修啊」·「平台相关的功能,应该尽量先改平台。」
- main 或合并队列红即 p0(「宁可其他开发暂停」)。
- 发版阻塞(2026-11-12/13):阻塞卡只升 p0、⛔ 不打 `target:`(「阻塞卡升 p0，不需要打 target:18.4.0」),发版后回 p1;「同意，你觉得严重的问题应该加入发版的都敲门让席位处理」——分诊判为发版必修的(相对上一版回归、不可恢复丢失、核心流程无绕行)径直升 p0 并 `Notify: release-blocker` 敲认领席,同轮报维护者;移出或撤根因(如撤 #32198)仍交维护者。
- 「新增门禁默认否」。
- 「一个issue只要涉及 cloud ,就归 cloud pm 处理」:需改 cloud 仓的修复归 cloud PM(`domain:cloud` + `status:parked`),只改框架的留框架车道。
- 契约复审归属(2026-11-03):「目前各车道都有fable，应该不需要你契约复审」——分诊**不再做契约复审**,(a)(b)(c) 兜底一并停止。复审一律归派发席本席自审;本席档位不可用(429)或车道收班 ⇒ PR 留等复核标记、待车道席回岗或交 objectstack-ai/objectstack#29242 复审席,⛔ 不交分诊。改写 `contract-review.md`〈复核归属与资格〉见 skills 卡。取代 11-02「1+2+4」中的分诊兜底条;#29242 复审席保留。
- **契约复审恢复(2026-11-14 21:5x,维护者):「review 席位上线了，没有fable的座位，他可以契约复审」** —— 解除同日「后续所有复审都停」的暂停。按下一条路由恢复:车道有 fable ⇒ 本席自审;没有 ⇒ 交 `review#2`(os-project-manager,信箱 #33260)。欠审表上的 PR 按此路由各归其位。⛔ 分诊仍不复审，收到复审请求转 `review#N`。
- 契约复审(2026-11-13,三次裁定,以最后为准):「契约复审只有在车道没有fable的时候才会找你执行，你也可以考虑是否需要单独设一个车道」→「现在已经有了专用的 review 席位啊」→「立 skills 卡，把契约复审的路由直接改成 review 座位」「没有 fable 时，找 review 座位」——路由:**车道有 `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`(fable)⇒ 本席自审;没有(账号达不到、429、或被限额)⇒ 交 `review#N` 复核席**(在座:`review#2` · os-project-manager,信箱 #33260;`review` · os-elon-musk(#33115)服务 server 区域租约试点;`review#1` · os-tesla 已于 2026-11-14 下班);无复核席在座 ⇒ 敲有档的兄弟席或留欠审表;⛔ 分诊不在复审路由上。分诊收到复审请求 ⇒ 转 `review#N`,⛔ 不退回车道、不自己复审。写进 skills 的卡:#33157。
- 安全:「对于测试中遇到的安全问题,不适合提交issue 的,只是使用pm-dispatch技能派发」——鉴权或授权漏洞的复现 ⛔ 不上 GitHub,只写规则层面;机理只在会话里交维护者。
- ⛔ 永不合并 Version Packages(#26517)、不派发版工作流、不打 tag、不发布;分诊不重跑 CI。
- 人裁底线:卡的去留(按是非关卡)、降级、新门禁、协议键、安全边界与规则改动,一律交维护者。
- 档位(2026-11-02):「同意，分诊，车道经理都用 high」——分诊席与各车道经理席的会话 effort 为 `high`;席位派出的 os-dev 仍按卡难度定 effort(改协议语义面或 `docs/adr/**` 的卡下限 `xhigh`)。
- 轮询频率(2026-11-02):「同意，先不改频率」——分诊仍每小时一 fire;车道等分诊须敲信箱(#28899),落地后观察再议。

- [x] **F09** [HIGH] Functions idempotency does not atomically cover committed effects — closed: #58 (4481c8c). An `idempotency_effects` marker is created in each effect's own transaction and bound to uid/route/requestHash (and matterId for P1). Routes are `once` (a committed effect with no stored answer replays a stored 409 carrying `operationId`), `resume` (committeeBrain republishes from the provider receipt after a fresh permission and clearance check) or `rerun`. A takeover that releases leaves a tombstone. Independent re-audits: aacaae5 FAIL 6.5 (HIGH-1, the Codex P1 double effect after a takeover) → 226a54e PASS 8.0 (new MEDIUM: orphan adoption leaked a receipt across matters) → **a2ece0b PASS 8.5, no new defect**. e2e through the real router on the emulator: `functions/test/f09-atomic-idempotency.e2e.emu.test.ts` is 43/43; on main, 30 of 35 tests of the first version failed: the audit probe ran the effect twice, and the committeeBrain flow made 2 paid calls. `f09-effect-marker-guard.emu.test.ts` is 5/5. The auditor's attack file is 16/16 (ATK-1 to ATK-10, adoption binding). Mutants MA–MF and G1–G3 are killed. GitHub CI green on a2ece0b. Follow-ups are in the comment below.

With `SIKANDER_PERSISTENCE_MODE=firestore` the claims and answers live in Firestore (`idempotency_keys` / `idempotency_effects`, F09's model), so a key replays across instances and restarts; production fails closed (503) with no Map fallback, and the dev/test Map refuses at capacity instead of evicting completed keys. A write fence in the four `firestoreDbModular.ts` write helpers creates the effect marker in the effect's own transaction, so a committed effect never runs again for its key (409 `idempotency_effect_committed`, with the `Idempotency-Effect-Committed` header and `effectCommitted` field on every non-2xx after an effect); committee-brain marks its paid dispatch before sending. Independent re-audits: 08c0990 PASS with MEDIUM-1 (no effect-committed signal), MEDIUM-2 (five mutants survived the PR's suite), LOW-3 (guard blind spots) → **7b22c9c PASS 8.5/10**, nothing new above LOW. e2e: `tests/f10-next-idempotency.e2e.firestore.test.ts` (real routes, Admin Firestore emulator; 7 of 9 failed on main 4481c8c, incl. restart, second instance, throw-after-effect and a second paid provider call). The auditor's 21 attack tests pass; mutants M2b/M6/M7/M8b/M12/M3b/M4b/M9/M11 and S1–S4 are killed by the PR's own suite. Unit 3326/3326, rules set 680/680; GitHub CI green on 7b22c9c. F11 not bundled (stays open). Follow-ups in the comment below.
- [x] **F11** [HIGH] Next effects and audit publication are not atomic — closed: #86 (de5e92b, head 05d971e). Every Next effect write stages an `audit_outbox` entry in the same commit (the F10 fence transaction, the write's batch, a repository transaction, or the F10 marker before P1 dispatch). A request releases its entries only at its audited end: a 2xx with no throw, every idempotency claim completed, and a persisted action row for a request with a body. A one-minute Functions reconciler (`auditOutboxReconciler`) writes one `request_effect_recovered` row per entry, exactly once, for what a dead or failed request left. It dead-letters entries with no readable `stagedAt`, and alerts on `audit.outbox_backlog_stale`. Also fixes F12-LOW-2 (`auditDeadLetter.listByFirm`). **Independent re-audit PASS 8/10 at f43e936:** 32 fault-injection route runs, 10 failed before the fix and 0 after; 39/46 mutants killed; the HIGH and LOW found at 35e093e are fixed; the three Autofix commits were confirmed defective and were reverted. Merged with main ac69873 (F18) in 05d971e: forwarded committee calls write nothing in Next and stage no entry (pinned by a new F18 e2e case); full `test:rules` 758/758; CI 19/19 green. **Deploy step:** deploy the Functions codebase (the reconciler), `firestore.rules` and indexes with or before the Next app; add log alerts on `audit.outbox_backlog_stale` and the two dead-letter lines. Follow-ups FA-F11-001..003 below.
- [x] **F12** [HIGH] Next Firestore repositories scan all tenants before filtering — closed: #44 (2bf12d5, head ae11eed). **Independent re-audit 2026-10-18: PASS 7/10.** Listings of 499, 500, 501 and 1,200 rows are complete with 0 foreign rows; reads per listing are N plus (pages − 1) (1,200 rows → 2,404 documents over both collections), against 89 to 3,269 foreign rows read on main. Rows with no or empty `firmId` are neither listed nor writable; a forged member row cannot reach another firm's matter; `X-Firm-Id` and `firmId` mismatches give 403. e2e 7 failed on main, 10/10 at head. Mutation: 17 of 23 killed; the 6 survivors (M08, M14, M15, M21–M23) are test gaps listed below. One new MEDIUM next to F12 (FA-D4-001, below) was already on main and is outside F12's read-scope statement.
- [x] **F13** [HIGH] The two API stacks disagree about canonical Firestore shapes — CLOSED 2026-10-26: Master Engineer `REAUDIT_F13.md` PASS 9.9 at main `6472777a`; shared schema owner `platform/d1/matterDocument.ts`; FA-F13-* HIGH residuals closed; stale LOWs 008/019/026/027 cleared.
- [x] **F14** [HIGH] Job reads omit the matter's current clearance floor — closed: #38 (c1ee524). Independent re-audits through R8: final delta PASS 8.5/10 (head ba406a8); GitHub CI green on a60bdee (ba406a8 + main incl. #40). e2e: the F14 job group (6 files, 68 tests) incl. `functions/test/f14-job-clearance.e2e.emu.test.ts`, plus the Firestore-mode route cases and `tests/firestore.rules.test.ts` (C1, R5-D2). Cache races that remain on main too are logged on #30.
- [x] **F15** [HIGH] The PII mask is not a comprehensive confidentiality boundary — closed: #61 (403200c). Detection runs on a normalised view mapped back to the original (NFKC, every Unicode digit script, dash/space variants, format, default-ignorable, combining-mark and private-use characters dropped); main's own patterns run on the raw text as well and the spans are unioned, so the mask never masks less than main (0 losses on 230,000+ generated inputs, exact span comparison). Party names match folded (case, diacritics, Arabic letter variants, whitespace) and include the matter's client-record names. An independent residual detector (identifier-shaped digit runs, labelled identifiers, addresses, parentage) backs the rank-3/4 minimisation obligation (`not_minimised`) and records counts only on every call. Masking is documented as risk reduction, not anonymisation. Independent re-audits: R1 FAIL 6/10 → R2 FAIL 7/10 → R3 FAIL 8/10 → R4 FAIL 7/10 → R5 FAIL 9/10 → **R6 PASS 9/10 at 23e7c23**, nothing at MEDIUM or above open. e2e: `functions/test/f15-pii-mask.e2e.emu.test.ts` through the real committeeBrain route (the audit's full-width CNIC and Urdu-digit phone were sent unmasked on main). Held-out false positives 1/118 on the auditor's last fresh corpus. Unit 5212/5212; Functions F15/p1/f09 318/318; GitHub CI green. Follow-ups in the comment below.
- [x] **F16** [HIGH] Agent prompt serialization erases trust roles — closed: #62 (b48f79d). Both transports send a platform-authored system message (frozen, versioned registry; plus the digest-pinned `agent/instructions.md` on the eve path) first, then role-separated turns; nothing is flattened. The system message is immutable and verified byte-for-byte before sending (caller party names, purpose and providerOptions cannot alter it; Codex P1). Tool results and tool-call arguments travel inside an `<untrusted_content>` envelope that content cannot close (look-alikes neutralised via F15's view); file, reasoning, tool-approval and unknown parts fail closed. Every non-system part is masked and minimised; the F07 reservation covers every message sent; records store `{ policyId, version }`, never the text; a size guard keeps the Next record under 1 MiB (Codex P2). Only three read-only eve tools are enabled, with strict inputs and typed output contracts. Independent re-audit: **PASS 8.5/10 at d697075**, nothing at MEDIUM or above; 37 of 38 mutants killed; full Functions suite 1,714/1,714. e2e: `functions/test/f16-prompt-roles.e2e.emu.test.ts` through the real committeeBrain route (on main the provider received one flattened user message). Model-level injection resistance NOT DEMONSTRATED (no gateway key; the 54-case live corpus is skipped). Follow-ups in the comment below.
- [x] **F17** [HIGH] LLM outputs lack grounding and semantic evaluation evidence — closed: #63 (1f0cc27). Every Functions committee answer is graded against the authority corpus. f17.1+ policy asks for a strict JSON answer contract. Each claim's authorities resolve through the D4 gate's own steps (`lookUpCitation`, `verdictOfJudgment`, `budgetedStore`) against the active store; only a declared judgment can be VERIFIED (Codex P1). The prose is read for authorities too: it is normalised first (NFKC, format characters, digit and dash folding) and masked whole. items.body:
## Operational gap

Required current-head checks across `ContextualWisdomLab/fast-mlsirm` and the organization `.github` repository are remaining in `queued` state while obsolete heads accumulate. This blocks policy-compliant auto-merge even after CodeRabbit succeeds and review threads are resolved.

Representative evidence observed on 2026-08-03:

- `fast-mlsirm#410` current-head CI/Security/SAST runs queued after prior head jobs were cancelled;
- `fast-mlsirm#391`, `#396`, and `#401` exact-head CI/Security/SAST runs queued;
- `.github#704` exact-head CodeQL, Security, SAST, OSV, Scorecard, SBOM, Secret Scan, and Python Security runs queued;
- `.github#650`, which repairs Rust coverage provisioning for fast-mlsirm, is itself waiting on queued required checks.

The repositories must not solve this by bypassing required checks or force-merging stale evidence.

## Required diagnosis

1. Determine whether the queue is caused by hosted-runner concurrency, Actions billing/usage limits, organization policy, a reusable-workflow recursion, pending deployment/environment approval, or workflow-level concurrency keys.
2. Produce a machine-readable health snapshot containing repository, workflow, run id, event, head SHA, queue age, concurrency group, and whether the run is obsolete.
3. Distinguish a genuinely queued current-head run from a completed/cancelled job whose run-level status is stale or misleading.
4. Identify and cancel only obsolete runs; never cancel the sole current-head required evidence.
5. Add organization-level concurrency and close-event cancellation contracts where repository-local controls cannot operate before merge.
6. Alert on current-head required checks that remain queued beyond a declared SLO.
7. Preserve fail-closed merge policy: an unavailable runner is incomplete evidence, not success.

## Acceptance

- A deterministic script and scheduled workflow report queue health across allowlisted CWL repositories.
- At most one pending/running instance exists per PR-number/workflow evidence lane, except explicitly documented matrix jobs.
- Closed PRs and superseded heads do not retain expensive active jobs.
- A current-head run can be traced from PR to workflow/job state without relying on contradictory run-level summaries.
- The report identifies the external/manual action when billing, organization policy, or runner capacity cannot be fixed in code.
- Tests, documentation, least-privilege permissions, and 100% coverage/docstrings are included.

## Related work

- `fast-mlsirm#410`: repository-local current-head concurrency and bounded review churn.
- `.github#704`: hourly review-feedback repair scheduler.
- `.github#650`: Rust coverage toolchain/offline dependency provisioning.

items.title: Graph extensions: `defineGraphExtension` and `store.evolve()`
items.body:
# Graph extensions: runtime schema induction with durable restart parity

Add a production-ready graph-extension path for cases where the kind set is not known when application code is deployed.

The motivating use case is **agent-driven schema induction**:

1. An application asks an LLM or ingestion agent to inspect a corpus.
2. The agent proposes a typed schema as a JSON-serializable TypeGraph document.
3. A human or policy layer reviews and approves the proposal.
4. The live store evolves to that schema without a code change or restart.
5. Ingestion starts immediately under the new kinds with Zod validation, uniqueness, fulltext/vector metadata, query support, and durable restart parity.

Secondary use cases use the same machinery:

- Plugins that contribute graph kinds at install time.
- Tenant-specific graph schemas in a shared application.
- ETL sources whose entity types shift over time.
- Interchange adapters that translate external schema formats into TypeGraph-native extension documents.

The headline success criterion: **a runtime-declared kind should behave like an equivalent compile-time kind everywhere the public store API can reasonably support it, and a fresh process should reconstruct the same merged graph from the persisted schema version.**

---

## Final public API

```ts
import {
  createStoreWithSchema,
  defineGraph,
  defineGraphExtension,
  defineNode,
  type GraphExtension,
  type StoreRef,
  validateGraphExtension,
} from "@nicia-ai/typegraph";
```

Core verbs:

| API | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `defineGraphExtension(input)` | Build a strict, frozen graph-extension document. Pure value, no I/O. |
| `validateGraphExtension(input, options?)` | Result-style validator for untrusted/LLM-authored JSON before calling `defineGraphExtension`. |
| `store.evolve(extension, options?)` | Atomically commit a new schema version and return a fresh store carrying the merged graph. |
| `store.getNodeCollection(kind)` / `getNodeCollectionOrThrow(kind)` | Reach runtime-declared node kinds from TypeScript. |
| `store.getEdgeCollection(kind)` / `getEdgeCollectionOrThrow(kind)` | Reach runtime-declared edge kinds from TypeScript. |
| `store.materializeIndexes(options?)` | Run declared relational/vector index DDL separately from schema evolution. |
| `store.deprecateKinds(...)` / `store.undeprecateKinds(...)` | Maintain informational lifecycle signals for codegen, UI, and linting. |
| `store.removeKinds(...)` | Remove runtime-declared kinds from the active schema. |
| `store.materializeRemovals()` | Delete rows queued by runtime-kind removal. |
| `store.introspect()` | Inspect the merged schema, origins, persisted extension, deprecations, schema version, and schema hash. |

The settled naming is **`defineGraphExtension`**, not the earlier draft names `defineRuntimeExtension` or `extendGraph`.

Reasoning:

- `defineGraphExtension` mirrors the existing pure-value factories: `defineNode`, `defineEdge`, and `defineGraph`.
- `Runtime` is an implementation detail of the action, not the document. The value being defined is a graph extension.
- `extendGraph` sounds like the side-effecting operation. The action verb is already `store.evolve()`.

---

## Example

```ts
import { z } from "zod";
import {
  createStoreWithSchema,
  defineGraph,
  defineGraphExtension,
  defineNode,
} from "@nicia-ai/typegraph";
import { createLocalSqliteBackend } from "@nicia-ai/typegraph/sqlite/local";

const Document = defineNode("Document", {
  schema: z.object({
    title: z.string(),
    body: z.string(),
  }),
});

const graph = defineGraph({
  id: "research_corpus",
  nodes: { Document: { type: Document } },
  edges: {},
});

const { backend } = createLocalSqliteBackend();
const [store] = await createStoreWithSchema(graph, backend);

const proposal = defineGraphExtension({
  nodes: {
    Paper: {
      description: "An academic paper inferred from the corpus",
      properties: {
        doi: { type: "string", minLength: 1 },
        title: { type: "string", searchable: { language: "english" } },
        year: { type: "number", int: true, min: 1900, max: 2100 },
      },
      unique: [{ name: "paper_doi_unique", fields: ["doi"] }],
    },
  },
  indexes: [
    {
      entity: "node",
      kind: "Paper",
      name: "paper_by_doi",
      fields: ["doi"],
      unique: true,
    },
  ],
});

const evolved = await store.evolve(proposal);
await evolved.materializeIndexes({ kinds: ["Paper"] });

const papers = evolved.getNodeCollectionOrThrow("Paper");
await papers.create({
  doi: "10.5555/3295222.3295349",
  title: "Attention is all you need",
  year: 2017,
});
```

For long-lived services, use the `StoreRef` pattern so request handlers dereference the current store after an evolve:

```ts
const [store] = await createStoreWithSchema(graph, backend);
const ref: StoreRef<typeof store> = { current: store };

await ref.current.evolve(proposal, { ref, eager: true });

// Later code reads ref.current, not a stale captured store.
const papers = ref.current.getNodeCollectionOrThrow("Paper");
```

---

## Extension document shape

`GraphExtension` is a TypeGraph-native document, not a JSON Schema or a serialization of Zod. This is load-bearing because the current `SerializedSchema` introspection document is not enough to reconstruct Zod validators after restart.

Supported v1 slices:

- `nodes`
- `edges`
- `ontology`
- `indexes`

Supported property subset:

| Type | Supported shape |
| --- | --- |
| `string` | `minLength`, `maxLength`, `pattern`, `format: "datetime" \| "date" \| "uri" \| "email" \| "uuid"` |
| `number` | `min`, `max`, `int` |
| `boolean` | no refinements |
| `enum` | string values only |
| `array` | item types from the v1 subset |
| `object` | one nesting level |

Property modifiers:

- `optional: true`
- `description`
- `searchable`
- `embedding`

Per-kind metadata:

- `description`
- `annotations`
- `unique`

Relational indexes can be declared in the top-level `indexes` slice. Vector indexes are auto-derived from extension-declared `embedding` fields and flow through the same materialization path as compile-time vector indexes.

---

## Behavior and constraints

### `store.evolve(extension)`

`evolve()`:

1. Catches up to persisted schema state so stale stores do not trample another writer's extension.
2. Validates and merges the extension against the compile-time plus persisted runtime graph.
3. Rejects compile-time kind collisions.
4. Treats same-shape runtime redeclarations as idempotent no-ops.
5. Classifies incompatible changes against existing runtime kinds and rejects changes that would require unsafe row backfills.
6. Atomically commits a schema version with CAS.
7. Returns a fresh store carrying the merged graph.

Purely additive evolves are proportional to schema document size, not row count. Tightening an existing runtime-declared kind may run targeted row-count probes so populated kinds are not changed without a backfill path.

### Index materialization

Index DDL is not part of the schema-version commit path. `store.materializeIndexes()` runs DDL separately and records per-deployment materialization status. `evolve(extension, { eager: true })` is a convenience shortcut, but an index-materialization failure does not roll back the already-committed schema version.

### Restart parity

`createStoreWithSchema()` reads the active schema document, recompiles the persisted graph extension, and builds the store against the merged compile-time plus runtime graph. A fresh process sees the same runtime kinds, indexes, deprecation flags, schema version, and schema hash.

### Removal lifecycle

Runtime-declared kinds can be removed from the active schema with `store.removeKinds(...)`. Physical row cleanup is a separate operation via `store.materializeRemovals()`, preserving the same principle as indexes: schema commits stay fast, row-touching work is explicit.

Compile-time kinds are not removable through this API.


---

## Deferred follow-ups

These are intentionally not part of this issue's release bar:

- Richer property refinements, transforms, and conditional schemas. Compile-time Zod remains the right path for code-authored rich validation.
- Hard blocking of reads/writes for deprecated kinds. Deprecation is informational.
- Cross-process live notification. Fresh stores and explicit `StoreRef` rebinding are supported; pub/sub can be layered later.
- Automatic index drop/recreate on materialized-index signature drift.
- Backfill automation for incompatible runtime-kind changes.

---

## Release artifacts

- Guide: `apps/docs/src/content/docs/graph-extensions.md`
- Runnable example: `packages/typegraph/examples/16-graph-extensions.ts`
- Consolidated changeset: `.changeset/graph-extensions.md`

Closes when the branch merges and the release containing graph extensions is published.

Here's my **executive synthesis** of your comprehensive knowledge stack, organized for immediate action:

---

## 🎯 **STRATEGIC SNAPSHOT**

You've built **three integrated systems** that need unification:

| System | Purpose | Maturity | Status |
|--------|---------|----------|--------|
| **Zyntro Self-Contained Container** | Core infrastructure (GUI, validation, pre-commit) | ✅ Production (v1.3.0) | **Ready** |
| **Antigravity Skills Suite** | Security & PR automation (Dola-based) | ✅ Production | **Ready** |
| **Enterprise Knowledge Stack** | 5-domain knowledge base (Supabase, Agents, UX, Compliance, Governance) | ✅ Ready to merge | **Pending** |

**🚨 Critical Insight:** These are **complementary, not competing**. The Enterprise Stack **extends** Zyntro Container with organizational knowledge, while Antigravity **protects** both.

---

## 📊 **DOMAIN ALIGNMENT MATRIX**

### **✅ ALREADY IMPLEMENTED (Zyntro Container v1.3.0)**
- Self-contained architecture (no external deps)
- Schema validation & pre-commit guards
- GUI Dashboard (responsive, dark/light theme)
- SHA-256 integrity checks
- Branch strategy (main/stg/test/dev)

### **✅ READY TO DEPLOY (Antigravity Skills)**
- CVE-2026-28684 python-dotenv fix
- Dependency audit pipeline
- FastAPI code standards
- PR pre-merge validation

### **⏳ PENDING MERGE (Enterprise Knowledge Stack)**
- **5 Major Domains:**
  1. 📚 Supabase Enterprise (SSO, OAuth, Audit, Legal)
  2. 🧠 AI Agent Orchestration (6 skills)
  3. 🎨 UX/UI Standards (WCAG 2.2, Design Systems)
  4. ✅ Compliance Controls (SOC2, GDPR, HIPAA, PCI)
  5. 🛡️ Merge Protection (No-Replace Policy)

---

## 🔥 **IMMEDIATE ACTION PLAN**

### **Phase 1: Unify the Stacks (This Week)**

**1. Merge Enterprise Knowledge Stack**
```bash
# Execute the ready-to-run commands from your PR:
git checkout -b feature/full-enterprise-knowledge-stack
git add knowledge/ .github/ .gitattributes CONTRIBUTING.md manifest.yml
git commit -m "✨ Full Enterprise Knowledge Stack [DOMAINS: Supabase+Agents+UX+Compliance]"
git push -u origin feature/full-enterprise-knowledge-stack
gh pr create --title "✨ Full Enterprise Knowledge Stack"
```

**2. Integrate Antigravity Skills**
```bash
# Add to your Zyntro Container's CI/CD:
dola skill import --path Dola/Skills/ZyntroAI/PR-Suite --bundle
```

**3. Update Zyntro Container Config**
Add to `zyntro.container.json`:
```json
{
  "enterprise_knowledge": {
    "enabled": true,
    "domains": ["supabase", "agents", "ux-ui", "compliance"],
    "merge_protection": true
  }
}
```

---

### **Phase 2: Resolve Critical Gaps (Next 2 Weeks)**

| Gap | Risk | Solution | Owner |
|-----|------|----------|-------|
| **python-dotenv CVE** | 🔴 High | Upgrade to ≥2.1.0 in all repos | DevOps |
| **External Dep Conflict** | 🟡 Medium | Audit `pure-agent-dev` from task screenshot | Security |
| **Missing Schema UI** | 🟡 Medium | Build `SchemaValidator.jsx` from mockup (778.png) | Frontend |
| **Dola vs Zyntro Integration** | 🟡 Medium | Document how Dola skills enhance Zyntro | Architecture |

---

## 🏗️ **ARCHITECTURE INTEGRATION**

### **How the Systems Connect**

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    ENTERPRISE LAYER                         │
│  ┌─────────────┐  ┌─────────────┐  ┌─────────────────┐  │

│  ┌─────────────┐  ┌─────────────┐  ┌─────────────────┐  │
│  │   Core      │  │    GUI       │  │ Pre-Commit       │  │
│  │ Container.jsx│  │ Dashboard.jsx│  │ Guard            │  │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    ANTIGRAVITY SECURITY                     │
│  ┌─────────────┐  ┌─────────────┐  ┌─────────────────┐  │
│  │  CVE Fixes  │  │ Dep Audit    │  │ PR Validation    │  │
│  │  (28684)    │  │ Pipeline     │  │ Pipeline         │  │
│  └─────────────┘  └─────────────┘  └─────────────────┘  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

## 📈 **PRIORITY ROADMAP**

### **🎯 Q4 2026 (Next 3 Months)**

| Priority | Initiative | Deliverable | Success Metric |
|----------|------------|-------------|----------------|
| **P0** | Merge Enterprise Stack | Knowledge base live | All 5 domains accessible |
| **P0** | Deploy Antigravity | Security pipeline active | 0 critical CVEs in production |
| **P1** | Schema Validation UI | `SchemaValidator.jsx` | Real-time validation in GUI |
| **P1** | Mobile GUI Testing | Responsive validation | 100% pass on xs/sm/md/lg |
| **P2** | Compliance Automation | Policy-as-Code | All PRs auto-checked |
| **P2** | AI Agent Integration | Task automation | 40% reduction in manual reviews |

---

## ⚠️ **CRITICAL RISKS & MITIGATIONS**

### **🔴 HIGH PRIORITY**

**1. Dependency Conflict**
- **Risk:** `pure-agent-dev` import (from 774.jpg) may violate "Zero External Dependencies"
- **Action:** Audit immediately. If approved, document as exception. If not, remove.
- **Owner:** Security Team
- **Deadline:** 48 hours

- **Risk:** python-dotenv <2.1.0 vulnerable in all repos

- **Owner:** DevOps

- **Action:** Create `knowledge/README.md` with navigation guide
- **Owner:** Docs Team
- **Deadline:** 1 week

**4. Dola/Zyntro Integration**
- **Risk:** Two separate skill systems may cause confusion
- **Action:** Create mapping document: "Which system to use when"
- **Owner:** Architecture
- **Deadline:** 2 weeks

---

## 🎯 **RECOMMENDED NEXT STEPS**

### **Today (Immediate)**
1. **Merge the Enterprise Knowledge Stack PR** - It's ready and safe (no file replacement)
2. **Upgrade python-dotenv** to 2.1.0+ in all repositories

### **This Week**

### **Next Sprint**

9. **Document Dola/Zyntro integration** strategy

---

## 📊 **SUCCESS METRICS DASHBOARD**

| Metric | Current | Target | Timeline |
|--------|---------|--------|----------|
| Knowledge domains live | 0 | 5 | 1 week |
| Critical CVEs | ? | 0 | 24 hours |
| PR automation coverage | 0% | 100% | 2 weeks |
| GUI responsive pass rate | ? | 100% | 2 weeks |
| Compliance check automation | 0% | 100% | 1 month |

---

## 💡 **STRATEGIC RECOMMENDATION**

**Start with the Enterprise Knowledge Stack merge** - it's the foundation that enables everything else. Then immediately address the security CVEs. The Antigravity Skills can run in parallel as a separate pipeline enhancement.

**Your architecture is sound.** The three systems (Zyntro Container, Antigravity, Enterprise Knowledge) form a **complete enterprise-grade platform** when combined. The key is **integration without coupling** - keep them modular but aware of each other.

Would you like me to:
1. **Draft the PR description** for the Enterprise Knowledge Stack merge?

items.title: Run and repair the real LiteAgensh 32-peer user audit
items.body:
## Owner-requested outcome

Continue actual LiteAgensh execution and evidence-backed repair until the real user audit can run successfully: 32 equal peers, one shared Chinese goal, read-only review of the complete migration, foreground psmux operation, and a substantive audit report rather than a unit-test acceptance proxy.

## Authorization ordering

This Issue is a work carrier, not permission to execute. The existing refinement Wave excludes new native observations. First accept a separate exact-effects Wave grant, then the project-local user-audit protocol and its independent reviews. No newly paid/model operation occurs before both prerequisites merge.

## Retained boundaries

Keep the original closed development acceptance campaign closed. Continue the latest fully reconciled user-audit campaign ledger, including all prior spend, under the existing 150,000-credit cumulative and 10,000-credit per-attempt soft allowances. Keep 32 workers, 1,800-second run duration, no fixed roles, no nested model calls, no final test gate, and existing authentication/default provider. Uncertain usage or ownership blocks replacement; never reset old ledgers or evidence. No quota/account inspection, credential/access change, publication or proving dispatch.

## Completion evidence

Require real native turns and peer coordination, retained source-backed findings and independent classifications, a Chinese final audit summary in team state and the owned private output, and complete process/usage settlement. Failures remain retained counterexamples; successful tests, a launched process or deadline shutdown alone do not satisfy the requested journey. Operational success does not establish a general 32-worker/backend support claim or the owner's semantic acceptance of the migration.

## This is:

<!--- It will allow us to better understand problem and help you faster -->

## Specifications

  - Webiny Multi-Tenant App and Database Design

## Challenge
<!--- Tell us what should happen -->
The major architectural concern with multi-tenant apps is the database layer, which is also called the persistence layer. There are three aspects of database design that we’ll address:

- The level of tenant data isolation;
- Difficulties with restoring data;
- Difficulties with data encryption.

## Approach
<!--- Tell us what happens instead of the expected behavior -->

- Single Database for Single Tenant
- Separate Schema for Each Tenant
- Shared Schema for Tenants

We, Will, try to focus our discussion mainly on the best approach i.e. Single Database for Single Tenant.
